title: jsonToMessage could not parse "Integer like" double value;
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: master/v3.6.0/v3.5.0 etc.
Language: C++/Java/Python/C#/Ruby/PHP/Objective-C/Javascript
C++
**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Linux
**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
gcc 4.8.5
**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a protobuf Message
```
message Test {
    double LargeEnough = 1;
}
```
2. Create jsonString, 
{"LargeEnough": 18446744073709552000}
3. Try  JsonStringToMessage method to parse it to Test instance
`
Unable to parse number.
`
**What did you expect to see**
Since `18446744073709552000` is a valid double value, it should parse without error
**What did you see instead?**
`
Unable to parse number.
`
Make sure you include information that can help us debug (full error message, exception listing, stack trace, logs).

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**

After some digging into the source code, I found out the problem is in 
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/f130827371fc73ab6e24d44313af6577cc2f9d57/src/google/protobuf/util/internal/json_stream_parser.cc#L553
It doesn't use schema to check the float/double type. 

And in my case, since my jsonString is marshalled by golang jsonpb, and passed to c++ to unmarshal. Golang jsonpb marshalls the above proto.Message object as 
`
{"LargeEnough": 18446744073709552000}
`
I also tried MessageToJson function in c++ protobuf library, the result is 
{"LargeEnough": 1.8446744073709552e+19}, which is ok.

Therefore, the question is, whether you require external to handle double type to be the format as '.' 'E' or 'e', or you will support internally.


Thank you.

nodes.body: Sorry for the very slow reply. I just tried your test case on the current C++ parser and it worked, so I think this bug is obsolete. The JSON parser was completely rewritten for Protobuf v22 (https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v22.0).

Pass a number larger than 2,147,483,647 (MAX_INT_32) to a set{Field}() method on an int32 field

An exception that it's overflowing

title: Integration between PHP and Java/NodeJs
body:
Right now we have some integrations between node and PHP.
We could not find any implementation in PHP that used the binary serialization that we use in NodeJs and Java.

The (de)serialization in PHP uses this class CodedOutputStream that does not a binary serialization, instead it serializes in string format. The PHP support that we could check is only for JSON, and the nodeJs implementation does not support deserializing from a JSON, just the other way around.

Are we missing something?

nodes.body:
The PHP, Java, and JavaScript protobuf libraries owned by Google all support protobuf binary format.

In PHP you can serialize to binary format using `$msg->serializeToString();`. The resulting string can be passed to any other protobuf library. For more info see: https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/php-generated#message

body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. In Emacs, turn on protobuf-mode
2. `M-x eval-expression RET (derived-mode-p 'prog-mode)`

**What did you expect to see**
`prog-mode`

**What did you see instead?**
`nil`

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
`protobuf-mode` is a major mode for a programming language, albeit a restricted one. In fact, it claims to be [derived from CC Mode](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/4567a21004db641e974200f20715a2c9ab1f2378/editors/protobuf-mode.el#L41), which it actually isn’t.

That’s tangential though. In order to derive from `prog-mode`, the `defun prog-mode` at: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/4567a21004db641e974200f20715a2c9ab1f2378/editors/protobuf-mode.el#L195-L219 should instead read:
``` elisp
;;;###autoload
(define-derived-mode protobuf-mode prog-mode "Protocol-Buffers"  ;; Replace defun with define-derived-mode
  "Major mode for editing Protocol Buffers description language.

The hook `c-mode-common-hook' is run with no argument at mode
initialization, then `protobuf-mode-hook'.

Key bindings:
\\{protobuf-mode-map}"
  (kill-all-local-variables) ;; Remove spurious interactive call
  (set-syntax-table protobuf-mode-syntax-table)
  (setq major-mode 'protobuf-mode
        mode-name "Protocol-Buffers"
        local-abbrev-table protobuf-mode-abbrev-table
        abbrev-mode t)
  (use-local-map protobuf-mode-map)
  (c-initialize-cc-mode t)
  (if (fboundp 'c-make-emacs-variables-local)
      (c-make-emacs-variables-local))
  (c-init-language-vars protobuf-mode)
  (c-common-init 'protobuf-mode)
  (easy-menu-add protobuf-menu)
  (c-run-mode-hooks 'prog-mode-hook 'c-mode-common-hook 'protobuf-mode-hook) ;; Add prog-mode-hook
  (c-update-modeline))
```

title: descriptor.proto missing from protobuf-javalite
body:
Building an Android project with protobuf-gradle-plugin:0.8.12 and protobufJavaliteVersion:'3.11.4' fails if one of my proto files includes "google/protobuf/descriptor.proto".

Since the fixing of #1889, some proto files such as well-known-types are included in protobuf-javalite but descriptor.proto is still missing.

Even though the java-lite runtime doesn't make use of descriptors, it's possible to have cross-language projects that do.

nodes.body: protobuf-javalite does not include any descriptor support. The earlier missing protos had their generated code available but were lacking the .proto definitions. protobuf-javalite does not even include generated code for descriptor.proto, on purpose. So it isn't a bug that descriptor.proto is missing, but rather a feature request to include generated code for descriptor.proto.
Is there a particular reason why the descriptor code is not there? If I remember correctly, it is there in the _nano_ libraries

For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf or Stack Overflow https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/protocol-buffers

We don't formally monitor stack overflow, but there are a lot of experienced developers there who also use protobuf.
@googleberg can you take a look at this with fresh eyes and make a call?

Thanks, @fowles. It's been brought to my attention that `plugin.proto` is in the same boat. Though I can also understand that file being far less likely to appear in an API so maybe an odd thing to put in the Lite runtime. Maybe `descriptor.proto` and `plugin.proto` could be provided in a separate JAR/artifact?

We ran into this in generating Java lite APIs for [our own BSR APIs](https://buf.build/bufbuild/buf/docs/main:buf.alpha.registry.v1alpha1#buf.alpha.registry.v1alpha1.PluginGenerationResponse), for use with Connect Kotlin. Admittedly, an actual mobile client would almost certainly never call these particular endpoints. But they are in the same package as other endpoints. So to get this to generate valid, compiling code, it's much more involved to manually prune the set of protos prior to code generation. Anyhow, I understand if this is an odd request, particularly regarding `plugin.proto`. Our hope is that the request is reasonable since it reduces friction for users that happen to have proto definitions that look like this. And the fact that other users have run into this (i.e. the others that filed and commented on this issue and #8697) suggests we're not the only ones.

At the moment, we have a work-around by providing Java-lite-generated code for these in [our own Maven artifact](https://search.maven.org/artifact/build.buf/protobuf-javalite/3.22.3.1/jar?eh=). But since the classes are all named `com.google...`, it's a little squirrelly that they are provided by a bufbuild artifact instead of a google artifact.

While the idea of passing around descriptors in RPCs makes me a little queasy, it's already available to protobuf-core, so making it available in lite seems like a minor transgression. Same for plugin.proto. I guess I'd rather we provide a single, official version than have several unofficial versions published.

We're trying to use javalite and hitting the problem of com.google.protobuf.ProtocolMessageEnum not being available and I think it's also because Descriptors is missing since the interface uses them:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blame/d111589bc05f0c11d9d2b0e230bc3217f24feb40/java/core/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/ProtocolMessageEnum.java#L14

Is the only alternative to use the full proto-java?

Is there a plan to release still Maven artifacts for lite packages (kotlin and java) in 3.x range context? Based on https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/16452#issuecomment-2047931605 I have the feeling that 3.x would still be supported. I am asking it as I am particularly interested in 3.27.x to be able to benefit from the fix for this issue.

title: Protobuf accesses Non SDK Interfaces marked hidden by Android
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: master
Language: Java

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Android

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Test on Android device running 9 or above.

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Integrate [Firebase Performance](https://firebase.google.com/docs/perf-mon/get-started-android) Android SDK on a Sample App (refer [quickstart app](https://github.com/firebase/quickstart-android/tree/master/perf))

2. Launch the app

3. Any action (app startup, moving between screens, etc.) causes the following log spam on Android 9.0 or above:

```
W/com.foo.bar: Accessing hidden method Lsun/misc/Unsafe;->getInt(Ljava/lang/Object;J)I (greylist, linking, allowed)
W/com.foo.bar: Accessing hidden method Lsun/misc/Unsafe;->getInt(Ljava/lang/Object;J)I (greylist, linking, allowed)
W/com.foo.bar: Accessing hidden method Lsun/misc/Unsafe;->putInt(Ljava/lang/Object;JI)V (greylist, linking, allowed)
W/com.foo.bar: Accessing hidden method Lsun/misc/Unsafe;->getLong(Ljava/lang/Object;J)J (greylist,core-platform-api, linking, allowed)
W/com.foo.bar: Accessing hidden method Lsun/misc/Unsafe;->putLong(Ljava/lang/Object;JJ)V (greylist, linking, allowed)
W/com.foo.bar: Accessing hidden method Lsun/misc/Unsafe;->putInt(Ljava/lang/Object;JI)V (greylist, linking, allowed)
```

This happens very frequently and pollutes customer logcat (see [original issue](https://github.com/firebase/firebase-android-sdk/issues/1128)). 

See [documentation](https://developer.android.com/distribute/best-practices/develop/restrictions-non-sdk-interfaces) details.

**Note:** Issue might happen with any Firebase SDK integrating with protobuf but I haven't tested it. It could also be more broad (means not just Firebase SDKs).

**What did you expect to see**
From the [docs](https://developer.android.com/distribute/best-practices/develop/restrictions-non-sdk-interfaces#list-names), while you can currently use some non-SDK interfaces that are part of the greylist (depending on your app's [target API level](https://developer.android.com/distribute/best-practices/develop/target-sdk)), using any non-SDK method or field always carries a high risk of breaking your app.

So we expect to have protobuf migrate to SDK interfaces.
> Also see [requesting](https://developer.android.com/distribute/best-practices/develop/restrictions-non-sdk-interfaces#feature-request) a new public API from Android.

**What did you see instead?**
APIs marked hidden (Non SDK Interfaces) by Android are being accessed by protobuf.

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
Per analysis performed using the [veridex tool](https://developer.android.com/distribute/best-practices/develop/restrictions-non-sdk-interfaces#veridex-macos), all of the accessed hidden APIs for Firebase Performance are from `com.google.protobuf` library.

```
49 hidden API(s) used: 24 linked against, 25 through reflection
       44 in greylist (all usages for Firebase Performance are from Protobuf)
       0 in blacklist
       0 in greylist-max-o
       5 in greylist-max-p
```
> Note: Run the tool on a sample app that integrates "com.google.firebase:firebase-perf:19.0.5".

Refer internal ticket b/152073447#comment3 for full veridex report.

nodes.body: Issue is being tracked internally at b/154851649. The patch is planned to go into the runtime for R release.

What's the status of this issue?

I'm just reminding that half the world has their console output spammed because of this little thingy. ;)

Based on my discussion with the team Protobuf uses some of the greylisted APIs, and there is no plan to remove those APIs from a greylist for now. But given the widespread usage the platform team have added exemption list for hidden api warnings so as to avoid spamming logcat on access to these methods.

The fix has been released in Android R (11) release of the Android OS.

title: Map unknown enum cases to the default case (0)
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
This applies to Swift, generated using https://github.com/apple/swift-protobuf

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
The problem to solve is around decoding unknown enum cases from the JSON format. Currently an error is thrown when decoding a message that contains an enum case the client doesn't know about.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
When the server returns a new enum case in JSON to a client using an old spec, the `has...` field should return false for the enum's field, and the enum should be the default case (0). I'm petitioning `Swift-Protobuf` to add support for this, but they mentioned they'd like to see it supported here first.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The only alternative we would have is to never add new cases to enums, which would be very cumbersome to deal with.

**Additional context**
Please see the related issue here: https://github.com/apple/swift-protobuf/issues/972

nodes.body: To clarify, this issues isn't just with Swift, the question is a general question about how to handle enums evolving and the json encoding.
@thomasvl could you please help on this [issue](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/7322)？no one helps for a long time :joy:

There is now a test case in the conformance suite that exercises this behavior. body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v3.11.4
Language: Ruby (v2.6.5)

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
MacOS 10.15

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load IRB and require protobuf value wrappers: `require "google/protobuf/wrappers_pb"`
2. Create new Int64Value object with value set to 0: `v = Google::Protobuf::Int64Value.new(value: 0)`
3. Convert `v` to serialized string and back to object: `new_v = Google::Protobuf::Int64Value.decode(v.to_proto)`
4. Observer that `new_v` is nil instead of Int64Value: `v == new_v # => false`

**What did you expect to see**
I expected `new_v` to be `Int64Value` with `value` set to `0`

**What did you see instead?**
`new_v` is `nil`

**Bigger problem**
My issue actually is more complicated but the root cause boils down to this issue above. To see how this issue is actually causing weird exceptions within the protobuf gem itself, consider a new message type: 
```
message Value {
  oneof types {
    google.protobuf.StringValue id = 1;
    google.protobuf.Int64Value integer = 2;
  }
}
```
When compiled into ruby code, we will get code similar to one below:
```
# Generated by the protocol buffer compiler.  DO NOT EDIT!
# source: value.proto

require 'google/protobuf'

require 'google/protobuf/wrappers_pb'
Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.build do
  add_file("value.proto", :syntax => :proto3) do
    add_message "Value" do
      oneof :types do
        optional :id, :message, 1, "google.protobuf.StringValue"
        optional :integer, :message, 2, "google.protobuf.Int64Value"
      end
    end
  end
end

Value = Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup("Value").msgclass
```

Now if you try to create new `Value` with integer set to 0, you will not be able to decode proto version of it:
```
v = Value.new(integer: Google::Protobuf::Int64Value.new(value: 0))
Value.decode(v.to_proto) # => Google::Protobuf::TypeError (Expected number type for integral field 'value' (given FalseClass).)
```

title: Bazel file exposes internal headers
body:
Hello,

Today while trying to build [ViSQOL](https://github.com/google/visqol) I noticed that this project uses internal header files of protobuf.

When you build and install protobuf with CMake (or autotools) some headers that are considered internal are not installed. But the Bazel `BUILD` file unconditionally exports all of the `*.h` files:

```python
    hdrs = glob([
        "src/google/protobuf/**/*.h",
        "src/google/protobuf/**/*.inc",
    ]),
```

Because ViSQOL uses the following internal headers:
```
src/google/protobuf/stubs/status_macros.h
src/google/protobuf/stubs/statusor.h
```

It cannot be build against a protobuf that was build and installed with CMake.

I kindly ask you to do either of the following:
* Install **all** of the `*.h` files with CMake / autoconf and don't consider some internal
* Remove the internal headers from the Bazel library targets

Thanks,
Gregor

nodes.body:
> My expectation is that SerializeToString should return false and UTF8 validation should be treated as error for both decoding and encoding of a message.

I think it might be better to verify UTF-8 in the setters (with a possible "unsafe" API where the caller can claim that UTF-8 has already been validated). Then the serializer can assume that all fields contain valid UTF-8.

I think we may want to move in this direction in the coming years, but this would be a substantial migration, and there are currently no plans for it.

title: "In Python, the package directive is ignored" is incorrect?
body:
https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#packages says the following regarding `package foo.bar;` usage:

> In Python, the package directive is ignored, since Python modules are organized according to their location in the file system. 

However, this seems to be an incorrect statement as evidenced by https://github.com/spesmilo/electrum/pull/5993#issuecomment-611080550 - collision error, without a `package` directive - and then by https://github.com/spesmilo/electrum/pull/5993#issuecomment-611154987 without collision errors using the package directive.

title: Python protobuf: returning None on Timestamp
body:
The FromDateTime() function from python's protobuf returns None instead of a TimeStamp on my gRPC application.

This is how I have it set up.

```
from google.protobuf.timestamp_pb2 import Timestamp

self.forecastDate = []
ts = Timestamp()
i = 0
for qty in self.forecastData:
        self.forecastDate.append(
                ts.FromDatetime(datetime.datetime.now() + datetime.timedelta(days=i))
        )
        i += 1
```
I really don't know what I am missing because documentation asks for a datetime as a parameter for that function.

nodes.body:
Try:

```
i = 0
for qty in self.forecastData:
        ts.FromDatetime(datetime.datetime.now() + datetime.timedelta(days=i))
        self.forecastDate.append(ts)
        i += 1
```

title: Need specification for how to parse unrecognized enums in JSON
body:
I was forwarded to here by @tbkka over in the Swift protobuf library from this issue: https://github.com/apple/swift-protobuf/issues/972

As it stands the JSON serialization option in the swift-protobuf library is unusable because when it sees an unrecognized enum value that has been serialized to a JSON string, it throws an exception. There is no option to ignore the unrecognized string enum value, the only behaviour that swift-protobuf offers is to throw an exception.

To me it is abundantly obvious that any protobuf library has to ignore information that was generated using a newer schema.

For example, if a new enum field is shipped on a proto with v12.5 of an iOS app but is totally ignored (maybe it's a new feature under a shared schema that is implemented on a web app and is not implemented on the mobile app for a while). Then when this field, which is totally ignored, gets a new enum value, the v12.5 version of the app breaks because the only thing this that swift-protobuf can do is throw an exception when it sees the unrecognized enum value.

Of course this scenario is the core problem that protocol buffers as a whole set out to solve.

> Protocol buffers were designed to solve many of these problems:
> - New fields could be easily introduced, and intermediate servers that didn't need to inspect the data could simply parse it and pass through the data without needing to know about all the fields.
> https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/overview#a-bit-of-history

(Of course an iOS app is not a server but it's the same thing as far as this is concerned because it participates in a distributed protocol.)

**Could someone please provide a specification for what a protobuf library should do when it sees an unrecognized Enum value serialized in a JSON string?**

I can't imagine that every other protobuf client that supports JSON serialized string enum values here crashes when it sees something unrecognized. Can someone point me to the behaviour of some of the other client libraries so that the folks over at swift-protobuf can have some precedence for how to handle this situation?

Thank you.

nodes.body: I'm not sure about other languages, but at least for C++ you can set an option to ignore unknown fields during JSON parsing, and this includes known fields with unknown enum values. The documentation [here](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#json) says: "Proto3 JSON parser should reject unknown fields by default but may provide an option to ignore unknown fields in parsing."

Could you please update the spec to explicitly call out enums as falling into this case?  It would also help if you could clarify expectations here for repeated enum fields.

And of course, expanding the conformance tester to verify these cases would be a nice treat!
Also please document (add conformance tests) for what this means when enums are integer (vs. strings), and the value isn't a known value.

@acozzette the only place I can find code for the C++ side seems to be within `JsonToBinaryStream` in `json_utils.cc` -

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/7bff8393cab939bfbb9b5c69b3fe76b4d83c41ee/src/google/protobuf/util/json_util.cc#L186-L187

Does that come into play in normal parsing (as opposed to transcoding which is what that api sorta looks like)?

Tracing the code a little further, there is a listener to get some feedback for that, but a normal parse of json to an object doesn't have a listener, so it is a silent data loss?

Oh, and an enum field within a oneof also needs a spec.  In all these cases, does the value get ignored or does it get the default value?

Oops, and for map<> usage, how does that end up working?

Hello all! Does anyone have any updates for the questions asked by @thomasvl? I've currently encountered the same error as detailed in [apple/swift-protobuf#972](https://github.com/apple/swift-protobuf/issues/972) and would love to see how we can move this forward to get it merged in?

>Oops, and for map<> usage, how does that end up working?

Enums are not allowed to be keys for a map. From https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#maps:

>Note that enum is not a valid key_type

Here is the change the Java team made to support unknown enums and ignore unknown fields: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/4825. It seems they just explicitly check the field is an enum and rather than throwing exception, they parse unknown enums as default enum value.
Enums are only allowed as map values, not keys.
The same issue exists in C#.

Hi,
Thanks @srcreigh for reporting the issue, and everyone else for discussing and desiring to improve things! My team has also encountered this problem with both swift and python.

We would like to contribute here, but would appreciate it if the protobuf team could give some initial feedback on our approach before we begin.

1. Make a pull request adding conformance tests as the proposed specification. We’ll base the spec off of the current [Java implementation](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/4825/files)
This would mean ignoring unknown enum labels if the "ignoreUnknown" flag is set while parsing a JSON message. Both Java and C++ implementations are already aligned with this.

2. If that’s accepted, create a pull request implementing the fix for python. The change should be similar to the Java PR linked above.

@acozzette I saw your recent comment on https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/7974#issuecomment-1028257362 -- glad to hear that this is being discussed, thank you! Is it possible to share more details with us here?

My current thinking is that if we limit the scope to only enum **string** values, the decision might be easier. Concrete proposal here https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/9534.
I believe @jskeet is working on a proposal to allow optionally ignoring unknown enum string values, but the proposal has not been fully approved yet.

@antongrbin: We're still involved in internal discussions around this. I'm afraid I can't talk to timelines without those discussions being complete.

Our priority is proto3 rather than proto2, but if you have a use case you could share, that could be very helpful.

Thank you for your response!

My use case is a bit selfish: my team currently uses only `proto2` and JSON. We use it to persist structured data blobs in databases, for message passing in event queues and for APIs. Since serialized message size was not an issue for us, we went with JSON to get human readability of messages and incremental protobuf adoption for consumers.

--

Going back to our topic, the decision making for `proto2` might be simpler. In fact, the [official language guide](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto#enum) already gives us the spec:

> a field with an enum type can only have one of a specified set of constants as its value (if you try to provide a different value, the parser will treat it like an **unknown field**).

Specifically, the `proto2` JSON parser should treat an unknown enum value as an unknown field. If ignore unknown fields is set, it should ignore it.

@jskeet, am I reading this correctly? What did I miss? Would it be possible to move forward only for `proto2`?

@antongrbin: The language guide was written before the JSON format was even designed.

I don't intend to start dividing the internal discussion into "just proto2 bits" and "proto3 bits" - that's likely to just make everything take even longer.
We have a group working on doing an audit and formal definition for the correct answer for this right now.
I'm going to close this as a duplicate of #224.

> We have a group working on doing an audit and formal definition for the correct answer for this right now.

Hi @fowles, did we have any outcome from the audit? Any formal definition? I see that #224 is pretty stale at this point. And #9534 is depending on this.
What ended up being the conclusion of this work? We're using the python library and are running into the same issues as OP.

@connoranderson: Unresolved as yet, I'm afraid. Sorry - as ever, there are huge numbers of things being done, with staffing that changes over time too. I'm not giving up on this completely, but I don't expect a resolution soon.

Correct me if I am wrong, but for a subset of this problem we did align and added conformance tests.

Specifically when enums are encoded as strings and ignore unknown fields flag is set, the JSON parser should ignore the unknown enum value:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/8c1f63571668338172148a1bea4575a33736a8c2/conformance/binary_json_conformance_suite.cc#L1738

According to the code search, all languages but Python are aligned with this:
https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aprotocolbuffers%2Fprotobuf%20IgnoreUnknownEnumStringValueInOptionalField&type=code

UPDATE: In this repo, C# is also not aligned yet: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/7392#issuecomment-1884698127

@antongrbin: It's been a long time since I've looked at the ins and outs of the conformance tests, but that's definitely not the current C# behavior, and I was pretty sure this has caused a problem in languages other than Python and C# too.

@antongrbin #9534 added that conformance test, and at the time you wrote:

> Different clients yield different results when JSON parsing unknown enum string values:
>
> - java, cpp will ignore the unknown enum string value when ignoreUnknown is set
> - python, swift, c# will fail although ignoreUnknown is set

Was the Swift behavior changed? There are multiple other languages to consider too, some of which aren't covered in this repo - the ones I care most about being Ruby, PHP, Go and TypeScript.

Swift behavior was changed in https://github.com/apple/swift-protobuf/pull/1345.

I definitely agree that there are other languages than what is covered with conformance tests in this repo.

I am confused about C# though -- it has conformance tests here, and the failure list doesn't surface the tests that #9534  added: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/conformance/failure_list_csharp.txt

@antongrbin: Yup, it confuses me too - but unfortunately I don't have time to delve into what's going on right now. I do hope we don't have other conformance test failures that we're missing :(

(I think it would also be useful to have conformance tests which make the behavior clear in terms of "a repeated field with a mixture of invalid and valid values" - as that's one of the more contentious aspects. I believe the current conformance test does *somewhat* show that, but a test with `["A", "UNKNOWN", "B"] => [A, B]` would highlight it.)

I executed the unit test from https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/15368 locally. It tells us that C# is not aligned with the added conformance test. I'll also take a quick look at why the conformance test for C# is not executed, but I'll timebox it.

UPDATE: I guess we don't see the conformance test failure because C# conformance runner will skip such tests explicitly:

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/8c1f63571668338172148a1bea4575a33736a8c2/csharp/src/Google.Protobuf.Conformance/Program.cs#L77

title: Consider removing HasFoo/ClearFoo() for proto2 message fields in C#

nodes.body:
Note that we *can* also remove the Has/Clear for oneof fields, given that users can use the existing `FooCase`/`ClearFoo` pair.
There's less of a compelling case to do so, however: oneof fields can never be *explicitly* optional, so we don't get into the inconsistency between "explicitly optional in proto3 vs implicitly optional in proto2" situation.

The case for removing it from oneof fields is still fairly compelling though:

- It reduces the change when updating from proto2 to proto3
- It reduces the number of members to look through in Intellisense
- It avoids the slightly odd effect that Clear only has an effect if the oneof was set to that case already.

~~Oh, and I *think* other languages don't generate Has/Clear for individual oneof fields, either.~~

Looks like that's not the case. It also looks like this is an expected inconsistency when upgrading from proto2 to proto3 in other languages, so I'll leave it in C# too.

title: Google.Protobuf.JsonParser throws exception if Protobuf contains an enum

nodes.body: To answer my own question, it looks like the Protobuf enum was not the issue. It was because the AuthenticationRequest message in the Profobuf file used lower-case letters to begin the field names.

Proto files should generally use snake case (i.e. lower case with _ separating words) for all field names.  They will be properly translated to camelCase depending on the language being generated and the configuration.

MacOS

load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")

    name= "some_repo_with_proto_files",
    ...
)

2. In a `BUILD` file, attempt to compile a protobuf library using the rules in `protobuf` and the `.proto` files in the external repo as `srcs`:
```
load("@com_google_protobuf//:protobuf.bzl", "py_proto_library")

py_proto_library( # note using cc_proto_library doesn't fix it either
    name = "some_proto",
    srcs = ["@some_repo_with_proto_files//src:external.proto"],
    ...
)
```

**What did you expect to see**
The `.proto` file to be compiled to a `_pb2.py` file.

**What did you see instead?**
Error message:
`label '@some_repo_with_proto_files//src:external_pb2.py' is not in the current package`

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
It would be ideal to be able to keep `.proto` files in a separate repo that defines interfaces to services, and import/compile them into projects as needed. This bug prevents this from being possible in python at least.

nodes.body:
Sorry for the late response.

This is most likely an error in the upstream repository. You need whatever rule you want to use the `external_pb2.py` file to depend on your `py_proto_library` rule. Right now your `py_proto_library` rule just creates the file but doesn't ever use it anywhere else.

I'm going to go ahead and close this, but if you still can't make it work feel free to reopen.

I have the exact same issue on Raspberry Pi with python 3.7.3 and python 3.7.5. Somehow, it is does not happen on my Ubuntu laptop with Python 3.7.5.
I use protobuf 3.12.2.

I run the exact same code on both but the isinstance check fails on Raspberry Pi.

The class type name is the same on both Raspberry Pi and my Ubuntu PC, but the class object id is different on Raspberry Pi.

I know python3 is compiled on ARM for Raspberry Pi and compiled for AMD64 on my laptop. Maybe there is a difference there.

met same problems too. The weird thing i met is that, when running the same code on x86 platform, everything works fine. While when running code on aarch platform like jetson tx2 or xavier nx, the problem occurs.

I had  the exact same problem. In my case is simple, I used Linux Apline, the error occured. And if I use Ubuntu, everythin is fine.
Python: 3.7
Protobuf: 3.11.3

There appears to be an assumption baked into the generator code for python at https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/397d34ca0eb71e2af31881cccb6d8ffcdc3a0ee6/src/google/protobuf/compiler/python/python_generator.cc#L879

This explicitly references the module it expects the generated code to be available under. Combined with how the message classes are constructed dynamically via descriptors, this can result in 2 different object id's for the same message class definition appearing under two different modules.

Taking the example above for route.proto:
```syntax = "proto3";
package a.b.c;

message Route {
    string id = 1; // uuid, generated by minion
    string dst = 2;
    string via = 3;
    string link_name = 4;
    int32 table = 5;
}
```

and network.proto:
```
syntax = "proto3";
package a.b.c;

message GetDefaultGatewayResponse {
    Route route = 1;
}
```

The generated python code will look something like:
file: a/b/c/route_pb2.py
```
Route = _reflection.GeneratedProtocolMessageType('Route', (_message.Message,), {
  'DESCRIPTOR' : _DEPLOYMENTINFO,
  '__module__' : 'a.b.c.route_pb2'
  # @@protoc_insertion_point(class_scope:a.b.c.Route)
  })
_sym_db.RegisterMessage(Route)
```
file: a/b/c/network_pb2.py
```
from a.b.c import route_pb2 as a_dot_b_dot_c_dot_route__pb2

....
....

GetDefaultGatewayResponse = _reflection.GeneratedProtocolMessageType('GetDefaultGatewayResponse', (_message.Message,), {
  'DESCRIPTOR' : _GETDEFAULTGATEWAYRESPONSE,
  '__module__' : 'a.b.c.network_pb2'
  # @@protoc_insertion_point(class_scope:a.b.c.GetDefaultGatewayResponse)
  })
_sym_db.RegisterMessage(GetDefaultGatewayResponse)
```

Now this all works fine if the files are actually structured such as `a` is the project name and import `a.b.c.network_pb2` is how it is imported.

However if you are placing the files elsewhere, or changing the prefix so that the import path is `rpc.network.network_pb2` rather than what is defined as `__module__` in the generated code, it appears you end up with two identical classes but different object id's from python's perspective.

Part of what happens is that when `from rpc.network.network_pb2 import *` is done, it imports `a.b.c.route_pb2` rather than `rpc.network.route_pb2` and this appears to result in one definition of the class being registered for the module `a.b.c.route_pb2`. When the subsequent import of `rpc.network.route_pb2` occurs in the project code, the Route descriptor ends up being evaluated as a different python class even though they are identical. Because of the hard coding of the module attribute for the classes if you try to print `__class__.__module__` you'll see the same, so it looks like you are importing the same module, but they are from different modules.

I uncovered this by a snippet a bit like the following to a unit test that was failing on trying to upgrade to python 3.9.1:
```
    import sys
    for mod in sys.modules:
        if "route_pb2" in mod:
            print(f"{mod}: {sys.modules[mod]}")
            print(id(sys.modules[mod].Route))
```
combined with adding the line `print(f"expected id: {id(cls)}, got id: {id(msg.__class__)}")` to where the exception gets thrown from:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/d16bf914bc5ba569d2b70376051d15f68ce4322d/python/google/protobuf/internal/python_message.py#L1318-L1322

I don't know enough of what is happening, I could see that there were 2 different imports appearing in sys.modules for the library I was working with, and the class id was different for each one. That allowed me to work out that if I imported the file that would register and then import using the module path hardcoded in the files would result in using the same ones in all locations.
```
import rpc.network.route_pb2
from a.b.c.route_pb2 import *
import rpc.network.network_pb2
from a.b.c.network_pb2 import *
```
It appears once rpc.network.route_pb2 is imported, there is an instance added to sys.modules as 'a.b.c.route' which is used by the other files that are part of the protobuf definition, so importing from `a.b.c.route` ensures I end up using the exact same and any `isinstance` checks will pass.

#1491, #4614 and #7470 appear to suggest there is a whole bunch of fun around import paths and python generated code. I suspect the divergence between what the generated code is assuming layout to be absolute and how usage of the resulting python code may assume that it can be placed under a different root to suit application layout or even be able to provide the generated protobuf code as a library is at the core of this issue. Having popped up various times and disappearing when import load orders end up switching slightly in python versions resulting in getting the needed class rather than the alternative definition.

I did some more digging and it turned out our local code had injected additional paths into `sys.path`. This is why the equivalent of `from a.b.c.route_pb2 import *` worked.

Given the important of paths in python module imports, and the assumptions about the base package name made by the generated code, which isn't made by the generated golang code, because all files in the same directory (ignoring test files for now) are in the same package which is defined as a simple path component, I think supporting relative path imports will make this class of error go away for use in python. Might also be nice if the `__module__` value is correct, but I don't think based on my further digging, that the value stored there is anything more than cosmetic?

I have been facing the same issue, where the CopyFrom or MergeFrom works fine on ubuntu system by has the same error as metioned by OP on a raspberry pi. A workaround i found to work was something like this

    default_response = GetDefaultGatewayResponse()

title: protoc --proto_out
body:
Projected use case:

I want to use a particular message type in several languages, on a machine with limited network access. Rather than compile the .proto into every language I'm going to use in advance, I would like to 'compile' the primary .proto file which contains that message definition into a new .proto which includes the primary file and also the definitions of all deps needed to compile it. I can then transmit this single file to the server which will use it, which can compile it to whichever languages it needs.

title: add 'Date' and 'DateTime' well known types
body:
**Reasoning**
The current Timestamp well known type represents an instant in time (i.e. a specific number of seconds and nanoseconds from the epoch) in UTC.  While this is useful for marking a specific point in time, almost all modern programming languages have some representation of a date without a time and a date and time with a timezone offset (or timezone identifier).   

**New Well Known Types**
I propose moving the following google APIs types to become well known types and adding proper support in languages that support these types. 

https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/master/google/type/datetime.proto
https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/master/google/type/date.proto

Moving them to well known types should make their serialized wire protocol identical so conversion between them should be trivial.

I may suggest changing the datetime.proto to remove the OneOf that permits IANA timezone codes and only allow an offset to ensure maximum compatibility with all language representations. Since the IANA timezone field is the last numerically, it could be removed without changing the wire protocol.  However since all languages could calculate this offset if they had an appropriate timezone database, the argument could be made to keep it.  I also suggest that the "year" field be required but could be convinced otherwise.

**JSON Support**
We already use RFC 3339 (and extension of ISO 8601) to format and parse a timestamp in UTC.  I propose we use RFC 3339 (full-date) for Date and RFC 3339 (date-time) for DateTime.
https://xml2rfc.tools.ietf.org/public/rfc/html/rfc3339.html#anchor14

I also propose we update the JSON canonical representation to support the RFC 3339 string representations of those types as well.

Using the existing "js_type" option, the "string" type could imply the RFC 3339 representation, while the "numeric" type could represent the object form with fields for each of the numeric parts (i.e. { "year": 2008, "month": 10, "day": 9 } ).  Both could be interpreted automatically (just as the other types that support the same option) and converted into either representation without specifying a parsing behavior or loss of data.

This is inline with the OpenAPI specifications handling for 'date' and 'date-time' formatted strings: 
https://swagger.io/specification/#dataTypes

And the JSONSchema representation:
https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/string.html#dates-and-times

**Language Support**
I have done a high level survey of each language (though I'm not an expert in most) and their built in support of the proposed constructs.  

Like Timestamp, we can provide the appropriate conversions methods between the WKT and the language specific representation.  For the languages that don't support all or part of one constructs, the WKT itself can provide enough details to be useful and agnostic for most use cases.  

For languages that have implementation options, we can add new MessageOptions or FieldOptions to descriptor.proto to determine the generation behavior for the new constructs.

Python - Full support for Date and DateTime
https://docs.python.org/2/library/datetime.html (datetime.date and datetime.datetime)

Ruby - Full Support for Date and DateTIme
https://ruby-doc.org/stdlib-2.4.1/libdoc/date/rdoc/DateTime.html
https://ruby-doc.org/stdlib-2.4.1/libdoc/date/rdoc/Date.html

Java - Full Support of both Date and DateTime as of Java 1.8 (released March 2014).
Full support for DateTime (using java.util.Calendar) before 1.8. No support for Date before 1.8.
https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/LocalDate.html
https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/OffsetDateTime.html
https://community.oracle.com/docs/DOC-983209

Objective-C - Full Support for DateTime and Date - some implementation details
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsdate
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsdatecomponents

Golang - Full support for DateTime, no support for Date
https://golang.org/pkg/time
https://github.com/golang/go/issues/19700
https://godoc.org/cloud.google.com/go/civil

C Sharp .NET - Full support for DateTime, limited support for Date until .NET 6 and DateOnly when full support was added
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.datetime.date
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.datetimeoffset
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.dateonly?view=net-6.0

C++ - Full Support for Date, limited support for DateTime
https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/chrono/year_month_day

Dart - Full support for DateTime, limited support for Date
https://api.dart.dev/stable/2.7.2/dart-core/DateTime-class.html
https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/1424
https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/5627

JavaScript - Full Support for DateTime, limited support for Date however I suggest using the js_type suggestion above to allow for a RFC 3339 based 'string' representation
https://www.w3schools.com/jsref/jsref_obj_date.asp
https://www.w3schools.com/jsref/jsref_gettimezoneoffset.asp
https://www.w3schools.com/jsref/jsref_todatestring.asp
https://www.w3schools.com/jsref/jsref_parse.asp

PHP - Full Support for DateTime, no support for Date
https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.datetime.php

Would you be more inclined to consider it if I split this into two separate issues related to Date and DateTime separately? @haberman @acozzette @thomasvl @ericsalo any thoughts here potentially? would be great to see it as a "built in" but if it's a "won't fix" then we'll stop bumping it to keep it open.

Realistically I think this is unlikely to happen anytime soon. We have never added a well-known type since the initial set of well-known types launched in 2016. That means we don't have any precedent for how to introduce a new well-known type without breaking compatibility. Well-known types are special-cased in multiple parts of the stack (JSON parser/serializer, generated APIs), which means a change of this sort would need to be coordinated across all languages. That's a lot of work that would need to pull in a lot of people. We'd also probably need to coordinate with non-Google-owned implementations somehow.

Google APIs are using the versions from https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/master/google/type and this seems to be working for them. I can see the appeal of having these types in the core protobuf library, but given the scope of this project there would need to be a very large benefit to justify deprioritizing other projects in favor of this.

title: Protobuf DebugString() / text formatter does not support custom URL prefixes for Any type
body:
We are trying to use messages packed into an Any type, with our own custom URL prefixes. We have some C++ debugging tools which we want to use to print these messages in human readable format via PrintDebugString() and DebugString() methods. If we use custom URL's, we cannot print the message, and instead get an error:

> .../src/google/protobuf/text_format.cc:1944] Proto type <our type> not found.

I believe that the issue can be narrowed down to the fact that the text formatter for Any types eventually calls this method, which requires that the type URL for messages packed into an Any must be set to a google URL.

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/fda8544a596dd3049ed4e826edc63a515c690bfb/src/google/protobuf/text_format.cc#L201

title: Add `emit_defaults = true` option for JSON serializer in PHP

nodes.body:
By default protobuf JSON serialization only outputs fields that have been explicitly set. This is like pure JSON where you have to set a field to make it present in the output.

Some protobuf libraries such as Protobuf Ruby let you specify a `emit_defaults = true` option for JSON serializing. This will emit zeros for unset fields that don't have presence. So you would get:

```
{"name":"", "pwd":"", "capid":"", "udid": "", "error": 0}
```

We could add such a feature to PHP also.

Another option is to use `optional` fields and set them explicitly to 0/empty. For more info see: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/docs/field_presence.md
Closing this since it is consistent with JSON serialization and isn't a priority for the team.

title: UnsupportedOperationException in Android64MemoryAccessor.getByte
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 3.11.4
Language: Java

Using `com.google.protobuf:protobuf-javalite:3.11.4` and `com.google.protobuf:protoc:3.11.4` plugins.

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**

Android

I'm getting an exception trying to parse a proto2 message:

```
java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException
    at com.google.protobuf.UnsafeUtil$Android64MemoryAccessor.getByte(UnsafeUtil.java:716)
    at com.google.protobuf.UnsafeUtil.getByte(UnsafeUtil.java:255)
    at com.google.protobuf.CodedInputStream$UnsafeDirectNioDecoder.readRawVarint32(CodedInputStream.java:1719)
    at com.google.protobuf.CodedInputStream$UnsafeDirectNioDecoder.readTag(CodedInputStream.java:1337)
    at com.google.protobuf.CodedInputStreamReader.getFieldNumber(CodedInputStreamReader.java:81)
    at com.google.protobuf.MessageSchema.mergeFromHelper(MessageSchema.java:3862)
    at com.google.protobuf.MessageSchema.mergeFrom(MessageSchema.java:3844)
    at com.google.protobuf.GeneratedMessageLite.parsePartialFrom(GeneratedMessageLite.java:1532)
    at com.google.protobuf.GeneratedMessageLite.parseFrom(GeneratedMessageLite.java:1695)
    at com.google.protobuf.GeneratedMessageLite.parseFrom(GeneratedMessageLite.java:1688)
```

What I have noticed is the regression happens from `protobuf-javalite` version 3.10.0 onwards, 3.9.2 doesn't have this bug.

[Android64MemoryAccessor#getByte](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/f494cb222d1b10a56273c07a3f5991b4b107958b/java/core/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/UnsafeUtil.java#L716) gets used, but the implementation throws by default. Maybe `getByte` shouldn't get used at all?

nodes.body: I have also noticed that `Android64MemoryAccessor` and friends [got introduced between 3.9.2 and 3.10.0](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/compare/v3.9.2...v3.10.0#diff-6c9e043b78f78efc096211703bb7fa4a).

I think I figured it out: I was feeding [GeneratedMessageLite#parseFrom](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/2db0e9812a8774f5266370b7a6eae4e4e5a2cdd0/java/core/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/GeneratedMessageLite.java#L1690-L1693) with an [`UnsafeDirectNioDecoder`](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/e667bf6eaaa2fb1ba2987c6538df81f88500d030/java/core/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/CodedInputStream.java#L186). However, on Android [`supportsUnsafeByteBufferOperations`](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/2228af689f5ff4d929c85079025c49f6945b136a/java/core/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/UnsafeUtil.java#L387-L389) should actually return `false` because the AndroidXMemoryAccessors [do not support unsafe ByteBuffer operations](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/2228af689f5ff4d929c85079025c49f6945b136a/java/core/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/UnsafeUtil.java#L714-L742).

I will post a PR correcting the issue.
That code has been refactored a lot. I think this is fixed, but if you still see it comment and I'll reopen.

title: UInt32 represented as int in java
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v3.9.+
Language: Java

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Macos Catalina

Values for `uint32` fields are represented as `int` java primitive type in generated code. That type is capable of holding max value 2^32-1. `uint32` max value overflows the capacity of java `int`. 

Eg. `3 936 623 488` is returned as `-358 343 808` from protobuf generated `uint32` getter.

How to work with it properly then? Currently I have to do this to get correct value but that does not seem to be good DX.

```java
if (value >= 0) {
    return value;
} else {
    return value & 0x00000000FFFFFFFFL;
}

-------------

Integer::toUnsignedLong(value)
```

I thought of two solutions:

1) document the behaviour
2) introduce a new type of getter that returns instance of `Number` so user does not need to do conversion manually. Except current `getUInt32Field()` there would have been `getUInt32FieldAsNumber()` introduced.

Would MR with any such fix be accepted?

nodes.body:
The mapping of unsigned integers in Java is documented here: 
- https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3?hl=en#scalar
- https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto?hl=en#scalar

I don't think we can introduce a new getter for this. Also the solution you gave would not solve the problem for uint64.

version : 3.8.0

compile command:
`protoc  --cpp_out=./ google/protobuf/descriptor.proto -Igoogle/protobuf`

then I got descriptor.pb.h.  Howerver, this pb.h is different with the original google/protobuf/descriptor.pb.h.

e.g.  I got：

`extern const ::PROTOBUF_NAMESPACE_ID::internal::DescriptorTable descriptor_table_descriptor_2eproto;`

in my file.

while in the original file, it is:

`extern PROTOBUF_EXPORT const ::PROTOBUF_NAMESPACE_ID::internal::DescriptorTable descriptor_table_google_2fprotobuf_2fdescriptor_2eproto;
`

so, how to compile the descriptor.proto to get the right pb.h ?

by the way, I got a similar issue with 

`descriptor_table_proto_2fcommon_2eproto #6179`  https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/6179

nodes.body:
The compiler output is sensitive to filename of the input.

So compiling `google/protobuf/descriptor.proto` will give different output than compiling just `descriptor.proto`, even if the file contents are identical.

So if you want to get the same output as the original, run:

```
protoc --cpp_out=. google/protobuf/descriptor.proto
```

(ie omit the `-I`).

title: Discrepancy in generated code of unsafe_arena_release_foo
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 3.8.0.0 etc.
Language: C++

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Ubuntu 18.04.4 LTS
Linux 4.15.0-99-generic #100-Ubuntu SMP x86_64 GNU/Linux

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
C compiler is Clang 9.0.0
CXX compiler is Clang 9.0.0


**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to '...'
2. Click on '....'
3. Scroll down to '....'
4. See error

I was using unsafe_arena_set_allocated_* and unsafe_arena_release_* APIs to avoid unnecessary allocations when the sub-objects are only "leased" by a leasing object inside a function scope, unsafe_arena_release_*  is always called before leaving the scope.

At the beginning, I chose the unsafe_arena_set_allocated and release APIs because the other safe version of release API does an extra allocation when the object is allocated on arena. And I saw the following generated code, which does not check if the object is allocated on arena or not, so it is safe to such use unsafe_arena_* on objects allocated in both arena and heap.

inline foo* outter1::unsafe_arena_release_foo() { 
  foo* temp = foo_;
  foo_ = nullptr;
  return temp;
}

**What did you expect to see**
I expected to see consistent behavior on different types.

**What did you see instead?**

However, I later saw the following the generated code with arena check, it means it is not okay to call for heap-allocated objects.

inline void outter2::unsafe_arena_set_allocated_bar(
    std::string* bar) {
  **GOOGLE_DCHECK(GetArenaNoVirtual() != nullptr);**
... ...
}

So, why the discrepancy?

Having to use two different sets of unsafe APIs (depending allocation type) makes things harder, it also makes the code less robust to future changes. I could check allocation type at runtime and choose the APIs accordingly, but that requires much more code.

I am wondering if protobuf owners also realize such an issue and start to remove arena checking gradually, thus the discrepancy in arena checking. It that the case? If not, can protobuf provide a single set of unsafe_set_allocated&release API for both arena-allocated and heap-allocated objects? A possible solution is to remove arena checking in all unsafe_arena_* code, arena checking is not always generated for unsafe_arena_* anyway. I could be wrong, but it seems to arena checking is only done for std::string in generated unsafe_arena_* code. I wonder if it is because google internal version of protobuf has arena support for std::string, thus the special treatment.

Thanks.

title: Argument file needs support for multi-char and BOM
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
libprotoc 3.3.0 / Grpc.Tools 2.28.1

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Windows 10 Build 1803

**What did you do?**
1. Create `test.rsp` containing non-ascii:
```
--plugin=protoc-gen-grpc=ágrpc_csharp_plugin.exe
--grpc_out=grpc_out
test.proto
```
2. Run `protoc.exe @test.rsp`

**What did you expect to see**
`protoc` running and creating the files.

**What did you see instead?**
UTF-8 without BOM: `--grpc_out: protoc-gen-grpc: Das System kann die angegebene Datei nicht finden.`
UTF-8 with BOM: `You seem to have passed an empty string as one of the arguments to C:\Users\dejhbk0l\.nuget\packages\grpc.tools\2.28.1\tools\windows_x64\protoc.exe.  This is actually sort of hard to do.  Congrats.  Unfortunately it is not valid input so the program is going to die now.`

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blame/master/src/google/protobuf/compiler/command_line_interface.cc#L1326 uses `std::ifstream` instead of `std::wifstream` and therefore does not allow BOM or wide characters.

This is a minimal example. We stumbled over this in https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/17995 as we distribute `protoc` and the `protoc-gen-grpc` through NuGet and the default for `dotnet nuget locals global-packages` is `%userprofile%\.nuget\packages\`. For some of our users, the username includes non-ascii characters which leads to `protoc-gen-grpc` containing non-ascii characters and the argument file not being parsable.

nodes.body:
CC:
* @anandolee because it's protoc
* @acozzette as implementer of the method
* @jtattermusch as related to `Grpc.Tools`

I'm not sure if making the `ExpandArgumentFile` function support `std:wifstream` is feasible (the functions returns a std::string which is then processed by the command_line_interface.cc logic, and the entire logic is written in terms of std::string and it doesn't know about wide characters at all).

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/3f5fc4df1de8e12b2235c3006593e22d6993c3f5/src/google/protobuf/compiler/command_line_interface.cc#L1425

Not too deep into C++, but AFAIK this would mean that the whole chain would need to support `std::wstring`. So this change would need to go a long way.

It's a bit sad to see that UTF-8 is still not the default in 2021 in so many situations (not just here).

Not supporting UTF-8 in the year 2022 is a complete anachronism. This really must be fixed.
But std::wstring isn't the solution: http://utf8everywhere.org.
Best would be to just keep using std::string, but make it Unicode capable.

The original link to command_line_interface.cc is no longer valid. This seems to be the location it was referring to:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/512f42c8c65ff33a4cb1c726c48a0f01103f7e4a/src/google/protobuf/compiler/command_line_interface.cc#L1429

BOM doesn't need supporting. Grpc.Tools writes out the argument files as utf-8 without BOM.

Looking at the protobuf code, the **fix isn't** changing from `std::string` to `std::wstring` and using `std::wistream` in `CommandLineInterface::ExpandArgumentFile` - in fact I think that is not the correct solution.

Reading each line of the utf-8 encoded file into a `std::string` is correctly (each line is just a sequence of bytes). It is when the string is used that conversion from utf-8 to `std::wstring` needs to be done.

**io_win32.cc** handles conversion from utf8 to `std::wstring` correctly (in `as_windows_path()`).

The problem seems to be when calling the plugins in **subprocess.cc**. `Subprocess::Start()` uses `CreateProcessA` instead of `CreateProcessW` and doesn't do the utf-8 to wstring conversion.

I've tested my own fix locally.

nodes.body: Sorry for the late response. Are you still seeing this error in newer versions of protobuf?

I want to clarify, I think the feature request here is to support hash initialization of struct fields:

```ruby
Google::Protobuf::Struct.new({foo: "bar"})

title: Regression in 3.12: toString() returns incorrect ascii when there are duplicate keys in a map
body:
Prior to protobuf 3.12, when parsing a map using TextFormat:
* If there are duplicate map keys, the last key seen is used.
* toString emits the duplicate keys in the original order, so if the ascii representation was parsed again, the same last key will be used, and the original message will be preserved.

In 3.12.0-rc-1 and 3.12.0-rc-2:
* The last key seen is used.
* toString does not retain the original order. In some cases, the last value printed for a key, is not necessarily the value that is being used in a message. As a result, parsing again the output of `toString` results in a different message.

In other words, `m.toString()` is producing a text representation that when parsed does not give the original `m` back.


**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 3.12.0-rc-2
Language: Java
**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Ubuntu 19.10

**What did you do?**

np.proto:
```
syntax = "proto3";

package mypkg;

message Msg {
  map<int32, int32> m = 1;
}
```

Main.java:
```
import mypkg.Np.Msg;

import com.google.protobuf.TextFormat;
import com.google.protobuf.util.JsonFormat;

import java.lang.String;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
            String input =
            "m: {\n" +
            "  key: 1\n" +
            "  value: 1\n" +
            "}\n" +
            "m: {\n" +
            "  key: -2147483647\n" +
            "  value: 5\n" +
            "}\n" +
            "m: {\n" +
            "  key: 1\n" +
            "  value: -1\n" +
            "}\n";

            Msg p = TextFormat.parse(input, Msg.class);
            int i1 = p.getMMap().get(1);
            Msg p2 = TextFormat.parse(p.toString(), Msg.class);
            int i2 = p2.getMMap().get(1);
            System.out.println(i1);  // prints -1
            System.out.println(i2);  // prints 1, expected -1
    }
}
```

**What did you expect to see**
Either a failure to parse, or:
```
-1
-1
```

**What did you see instead?**
```
1
-1
```

nodes.body: What is the output of the `p.toString()` call here?

I think the subtraction here is overflowing:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/java/core/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/TextFormat.java#L513

If I change this to use `Integer.compare((int) getKey(), (int) b.getKey())` your test passes.

Thanks for the report. I'll make sure this is fixed before 3.12.0 is released.
The fix is released in 3.12.0.

title: Rubygems release 3.12.0 differs from github release version
body:
Checking the code for the tag of the Ruby release 3.12.0 shows the following:

```
s.required_ruby_version = '>= 2.3'
```

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/v3.12.0/ruby/google-protobuf.gemspec

However download the Gem from Rubygems shows:

```
s.required_ruby_version = Gem::Requirement.new([">= 2.5".freeze, "< 2.8.dev".freeze])
```

This is causing issues with applications dependent on this such as aws-fluent-plugin-kinesis.

```
ERROR:  Error installing fluent-plugin-kinesis:
	google-protobuf requires Ruby version < 2.8.dev, >= 2.5.
```

nodes.body:
It appears that RubyGems rewrites our gemspec when the gem is uploaded.

However the rewritten gemspec is arguably more correct, as we dropped support for binary gems for Ruby <2.5: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/7453. It had become impossible to build our gem on these versions. Also upstream dropped support for Ruby 2.3 on 2019-03-31 and Ruby 2.4 on 2020-03-31.

This is mentioned in the changelog for Ruby:

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v3.12.0

Sorry to hear this is causing problems for you. If you are still on an older version of Ruby is it possible to keep using the older version of protobuf?
Thanks for the explanation. Closing the issue.
Ruby 2.3 and 2.4 are supported again in 3.12.1.

In that PR, we need to fix the bazel target `:protobuf_objc`, but we can't add the test target to `kokoro/linux/bazel/build.sh` because it's a linux kokoro runner. The `:protobuf_objc` target probably have something in it that says that will only build in darwin.

Here are the relevant parts from my Dockerfile and Gemfile:

Dockerfile:
```
FROM ruby:2.6-alpine3.12

```

Gemfile:
```
source 'https://rubygems.org'

gem 'rails', '~> 5.2.3'

gem "grpc", "~> 1.31", platforms: ["ruby"]
gem "google-protobuf", "~> 3.12", platforms: ["ruby"]
```

I'm not exactly sure which of the following changes (or combination of them) got everything to work, since I picked up the suggestions by following the several links in this thread:

- libc6-compat
- BUNDLE_FORCE_RUBY_PLATFORM=1
- CFLAGS="-Wno-cast-function-type"
- bundle config build.google-protobuf --with-cflags=-D__va_copy=va_copy
- gem "grpc", "~> 1.31", platforms: ["ruby"]
- gem "google-protobuf", "~> 3.12", platforms: ["ruby"]

But in the end, this combination actually compiles without errors and also runs without segfaulting.

Hmm, that is odd, not sure what happened there.

The newest version of the code no longer uses `va_copy()`, so this shouldn't be an issue any more as of https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/8184 and 3.15.0-rc1.

It has been brought to my attention elsewhere that this is because maps are represented as repeated fields internally. Recommendation: change the error message to
```
Maps are considered repeated fields, which are not allowed in oneofs.
```
I am also filing a PR with the doc maintainers to make this clearer in the docs. Belt and suspenders.

title: Messages with a oneof always fail in ConvertMessage
body:
# Issue
Calling the `ConvertMessage()` method on a JSON Object (message) with a `oneof` set raises the exception `'Message type # should not have multiple # oneof fields.'`
This ConvertMessage method is called in a number of places, e.g.  a method I've made that calls `ParseDict()` from the same `json_format.py` file as linked below.

# Call Stack & Code
```python
        proto_message: ProtoMessage = self._proto_msg
        message_dict = self.to_dict()

        walk_collection(message_dict, to_proto_field_case, None)

        ParseDict(message_dict, proto_message)  # <-- in here
```

Then inside `json_format.py` file:
```python
# Check no other oneof field is parsed.
        if field.containing_oneof is not None:
          oneof_name = field.containing_oneof.name 
          if oneof_name in names:
            raise ParseError('Message type "{0}" should not have multiple '
                             '"{1}" oneof fields.'.format(
                                 message.DESCRIPTOR.full_name, oneof_name))
          names.append(oneof_name)
```
we add the oneof field name to the list of names, meaning that the next field we look at (which is also in the oneof list but has value of None) will raise the exception.
_see:_ https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/39d730dd96c81196893734ee1e075c34567e59ae/python/google/protobuf/json_format.py#L540

### I changed to this to remove error
```python
# Check no other oneof field is parsed.
                if field.containing_oneof is not None:
                    oneof_name = field.containing_oneof.name
                    if js[name] is not None:
                      if oneof_name in names:
                          raise ParseError(
                              'Message type "{0}" should not have multiple '
                              '"{1}" oneof fields.'.format(message.DESCRIPTOR.full_name, oneof_name)
                          )
                      names.append(oneof_name) # TODO Matt query this!
```
This instead only adds the oneof field name to the list of names to check if a value is assigned (i.e. not None message).

# Question
Is this an issue with how I am generating my messages?
Is this an issue in the `json_format.py` code? (Happy to make a PR)
Is the message supposed to incorporate fields of the oneof such as:
```python
message = {
  a = "foo",
  b = None,
  c = None
}
```
where the message definition is `oneof = {a, b, c}`.?

title: Update documentation to clarify that packed repeated fields are not wire-compatible with optional fields
body:
(This was previously discussed in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/2905.)

As far as I can tell, protobuf wire-format parsers are not expected to translate packed repeated fields -> optional fields (indeed, this would be acting contrary to the behaviour of at least the Go and Java generated client libraries, both of which I have tested).

As discussed in the linked issue, it sounds like it's expected that optional is compatible with repeated, and repeated is compatible with packed repeated, but packed repeated is not compatible with optional.

That's fine, but it's very confusing because the documentation doesn't really say anything about this. In particular confusion arises in the proto2 documentation [here](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto#updating): `optional is compatible with repeated. Given serialized data of a repeated field as input, clients that expect this field to be optional will take the last input value if it's a primitive type field or merge all input elements if it's a message type field.` This documentation doesn't say anything about packed repeated fields.

It's also especially confusing in the proto3 documentation [here](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#updating), because there's not even mention of optional <-> repeated compatibility. Users who are used to proto2 semantics may assume that optional is compatible with repeated, without realising that since proto3 repeated fields are packed by default, this compatibility is broken (at least until they explicitly set `packed=false`).

Can the documentation here please be updated?

Suggestion (for the proto2 paragraph quoted above): `optional is compatible with repeated. Given serialized data of a repeated field as input, clients that expect this field to be optional will take the last input value if it's a primitive type field or merge all input elements if it's a message type field. Note that if the repeated field has packed=true, serialized data in this format will not be interpreted as an optional field, and will instead be treated as an unknown field.`

Suggestion for the proto3 documentation: `As in proto2, optional is compatible with repeated. However, by default all repeated proto3 fields are packed. For proto3 repeated fields to be compatible with optional, those fields must be annotated with packed=false.`

(Obviously the optimal answer would be to make packed repeated compatible with optional, but I suspect that might be impossible!)

nodes.body:
@BenBirt Thank you for reporting this, I'm working on updating the documentation now. I am leaning toward going a little bit further and actually saying that this is unsafe for all numeric fields. Even if a field has `packed = false`, who knows if it used to be `packed = true` and there is still old data lying around. It seems best to just play it safe.

We have thought a little bit about changing the parser to resolve the incompatibility, but I doubt that this will happen any time soon. That would be a big change to make since it would affect every language implementation, and even then, you would have to worry about code using older protobuf versions.

The documentation update is now live:
https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto#updating
https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#updating
@acozzette thanks for the docs update!

title: Incorrect source generation for GPBExtensionDescription

nodes.body:
Can you provide more specific repo steps?

The current code never uses the `name` part of the union, that is left over to allow supporting running with that was compiled against older headers with the new runtime.  The current extension code always does the `clazz` reference: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/3.12.x/src/google/protobuf/compiler/objectivec/objectivec_extension.cc#L128

I don't think a `pod install` can actually take care of building `protoc`, so the this might actually be down to the binary you have installed and are generating with (`protoc --version` / `which protoc`).

Repo steps:

Pull the source linked above.
Build it with `pod install` and then open Xcode and build.
Note that there is an error from the code being incorrectly generated as described.

The `protoc` executable inside of the `Pods/!ProtoCompiler/` directory is the one that is used and it works for all other code generation reliably, just not this particular component.
What's your exact error message?

The compiler error about not having the struct existing because the code generated doesn't match the headers.

Protoc should be generating:
`.messageOrGroupClass.name = GPBStringifySymbol(HttpRule),`
It's geneerating:
`.messageOrGroupClassName = GPBStringifySymbol(HttpRule),`

As a result, the code won't compile.

My workaround currently is to run `sed` prior to the build:
`sed -i -e 's/messageOrGroupClassName/messageOrGroupClass.name/g' ./google/api/Annotations.pbobjc.m`

We're looking for the exact error message.  We're sorta surprised there aren't errors for the `extendedClass` either.

The code is not generated, it is checked in: https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/ios-docs-samples/tree/master/text-to-speech/Swift/TextToSpeech/google/api

> locking the gRPCPlugin to version 1.27

What did you do for this?  I'm not clear where that plugin comes into play?

Right - in that project it is checked in. In the private project that I cannot share I have run into the issue as we don't want to check in generated files if possible...

re. locking to 1.27, this was because of a dependency problem: https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/22781

It should now be resolved, as 1.29.1 works fine as of yesterday.

If you aren't checking in generated files and getting this problem it means you are using a non matching version of protoc to the runtime version you are using.  Keeping those in sync will avoid the problem.

I don't really see how that can be the case; the Pods contain the library and that is the only instance. 

Aside from this one issue, everything is working great.
What's your exact step for pinning, I haven't had to do that, so I want to be sure I'm doing the same thing.

in the `googleapis.podspec` (https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/ios-docs-samples/blob/master/text-to-speech/Swift/TextToSpeech/googleapis.podspec)

Change the line:
`s.dependency "!ProtoCompiler-gRPCPlugin", "~> 1.0"`
to
`s.dependency "!ProtoCompiler-gRPCPlugin", "1.27.0"`

As I'm tracking things, it looks like grpc isn't building protoc, it is picking up an old one: https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/src/objective-c/!ProtoCompiler.podspec

So it actually does seem to allow the runtime support (Protobuf.podspec) to be a different version that what the compile being used is (!ProtoCompiler.podspec).
Interesting - so you're suggesting pinning the `protoc` version somewhere too then?

ObjC protos does have an issue in that we try to support old generated code, but the setup here seems to not really ensure that the version of the runtime matcher the version of the generator.  As log as the generator (protoc) doesn't get _ahead_ of the runtime, it should work.

From what I can see, `!ProtoCompiler` is at 3.11.2, and the `Protobuf` is at 3.12.

Is this break expected between these versions?

To test, I added a further dependency to the googleapis.podspec:
`s.dependency "Protobuf", "3.11.2"`

It now generates the code just fine.
So is the real issue that https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/src/objective-c/!ProtoCompiler.podspec should lock to the correct version it needs?

yes and no?  😄   I haven't traced through all the flows here yet, generally you want to use a protoc that matches the runtime you are using.  This would have "just worked" if we didn't have this bug as we try to ensure the runtime supports sources from older versions of the library.  We're working on a fix here to maintain that source compatibility contract in either case, just trying to figure out the right way to do so.
Fixed on the branch.
3.12.3 is released with the fix.
