title: C# WriteDelimitedTo(Span)
body: Hello, is there an API we can use to achieve the equivalent of WriteDelimitedTo a Span<byte> output?

nodes.body:
I suspect this is not possible at the moment, unless you come up with a workaround (you can use `WriteTo(this IMessage message, IBufferWriter<byte> output` to write the message content and write the delimiter yourself). 
Note that you can still use the old WriteDelimitedTo API if that's a functionality you need.
What is your use case?

@jtattermusch My use case is serializing many small messages to a **preallocated** byte array.

1.Write 5 length prefix messages to the array.
2.Send the written portion of the array over the wire.
3.Receive the bytes and read them one by one. This is achievable since the items are length prefixed. So i pick up the 5 items on the other side.
4.Achieve all of the above without additional allocations.

The way i achieve "WriteDelimitedTo a Span" currently is:
1.Given a message i want to put in the array, calculate the size of the message.
2.Call CodedOutputStream.WriteLength.
3.Write the message to the CodedOutputStream.
4.The CodedOutputStream is special in that it wraps my a special stream object i wrote that is resettable on the current position so that i can use a single allocated CodedOutputStream around my single preallocated array.

If there was a native "WriteDelimitedTo a Span" then i could do what i want without needing to allocate a CodedOutputStream and needing to implement a custom Stream that is resettable.
I then could just call var writtenBytes = Message.WriteDelimetedTo(array). The way i would write my 5 messages would then become:

for (var i = 0; i < 5; ++i)
   span = span.Slice(0, messages[i].WriteDelimetedTo(span));

So as you can see no need for a CodedOutputStream allocation or any special Stream implementation.

**Alternatively, is there a simple no allocation way to write just the length that is a simple int32 to a span?**
WritingPrimitives is internal and anyway does not expose such a method.
@MaximGurschi  I don't have the bandwidth to look into implementing this myself, but we can consider adding this if there's a PR that implements WriteDelimitedTo.

title: Ruby Oneof Fields WellKnownType Fields with Default Values Don't Decode Properly
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Language: Ruby 2.6.2
Version: google-protobuf-3.11.4-x86_64-linux

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Generate ruby code for the following message:
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package sample;

message SampleMessage {
  oneof value {
    google.protobuf.StringValue string = 1;
    google.protobuf.Int32Value int = 2;
  }
}
```
2. Initialize a message with a default value (empty string or zero) for either of the oneof fields:
```rb
msg = Sample::SampleMessage.new(string: Google::Protobuf::StringValue.new(value: ""))
# #<Sample::SampleMessage string: <Google::Protobuf::StringValue value: "">, int: nil>
```
3. Encode the message to protobuf:
```rb
msg.to_proto
# "\x0a\x00"
```
4. Decode the resulting bytes
```rb
Sample::SampleMessage.decode("\x0a\x00")
# #<Sample::FooDto:0x2ad3d4d00b38>
```

**What did you expect to see**
The decoded protobuf should be identical to the message before encoding.

**What did you see instead?**
The decoded protobuf is left in an inconsistent state without the oneof value having been initialized. Attempting to access the string value results in a confusing exception:
```rb
Sample::SampleMessage.decode("\x0a\x00").string
# Google::Protobuf::TypeError: Invalid argument for string field 'value' (given FalseClass). 
```

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
This issue only appears when using well-known types `StringWrapper`, `Int32Wrapper`, `Int64Wrapper`, and `FloatWrapper`. `BoolWrapper` is _not_ affected, for whatever reason. Similarly, substituting the Google protobuf wrappers with home-grown wrappers (e.g., a simple message with a single primitive field) does _not_ exhibit this issue.

Attempting to decode the slightly-modified protobuf format `"\x0a\x02\x0a\x00"` _does_ result in the expected message, which leads me to believe that the issue lies specifically in attempting to populate a default (0-byte) value for a well-known type when decoding a oneof field.

We were able to get around this issue in our project by updating our oneof to use only primitive fields rather than wrappers (the wrappers are pointless in this case because we can't set a oneof to `nil`), but this still seems like undesirable behavior.

nodes.body:
This should be fixed by https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/8184, which is released in 3.15.0-rc1 and after. Please give it a try and let us know if you're still seeing the problem.

I'm not sure why our tests didn't catch this problem, as we do have some tests for wrappers in a oneof:

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/aee143afe8c17a3d2c7e88b70ffa6e08a73e2683/ruby/tests/common_tests.rb#L1392-L1427

In any case, the new code as of https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/8184 is much simpler and better tested, so I expect that this issue is fixed in that PR.

Comment in generated file looks like this: /// This should cause a line break in VS 2019:  < br/ > 
(Remove the spaces - caused github to insert a line break...)

**What did you see instead?**
Comment in generated file looks like this: /// This should cause a line break in VS 2019: &lt ;br/> 
(Remove the spaces - caused github to insert a line break...)

**Here is the reason:**
Line 58 causes this behaviour:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/845/commits/67dd42c50d2b6d9c208bb1a4c63ee879781a9ac1#diff-2aeac396543d7beb1aafa7d047aef3d9

@jskeet I don't see the reason why you did the replacement: 
comments = StringReplace(comments, "<", "&lt ;", true);

nodes.body:
This is working as intended. There's no fixed format for protobuf comments - so there's no guarantee whatsoever that a `<` will be part of a valid XML element, or that the XML element is intended to actually be a C# XML doc comment.

Instead, we escape the `<` so that the *text* node of the XML doc comment is the *text* of the original protobuf comment.

I wouldn't expect this to change.

No, I don't think that's a good idea - I'd expect that to wreak havoc with Intellisense, for example, which would probably only show the first summary tag. Fundamentally just because a comment is on several lines doesn't mean it's several separate ideas, which is what having multiple summary tags would imply.

Basically, we're treating the comment as a blob of opaque text, and reproducing that in the summary tag. I don't think there's much more that protoc can do, without knowing more about the expected format of the comment.

I second the feature-request of the author. Problem here is, that comments are rendered very much like xhtml, therefore if you have no `
` all comment lines from proto are rendered into one concatenated line, which is very inconveniente. In fact, you don't need a `\n` in C# doc at all, only the `
` is important for a comment block. So converting every comment linebreak from proto files to `
` for C# would be very reasonable. There could be an option to enable/disable this feature, analog to existing ones like `option csharp_namespace = "Foo.Bar.Project";` or `option java_multiple_files = true;` for example example: ``` option csharp_doc_convert_comment_linebreak_to_break_tag = true; ```

A very primitive approach would be this: https://github.com/juwens/protobuf/commit/58937ba25a09d77db0aca804d6197b043c0ed08f As professional C# developer myself, i guess that this would be a viable solution for at least 90% of the cases. Because, why do you do a linebreak in proto? - you want to format your doc - your line gets too long It's the same reason you would write a `
` in C# doc. I totally see, why you don't want to allow for tags to pass through the converter. But explicitly adding the `
` at the end of every converted line **in** the csharp converter should be fine from your perspective, or is it not okay four you?

title: Use of cmake and installation of cmake files on Linux
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->
I found installing protocol buffers from source for use with cmake on platforms not having a sufficiently recent version to be suprisingly painful. Most of the issues I had I think relate to the FindProtobuf.cmake module in cmake (links below). This ticket covers the remaining issues I have with protocol buffers itself.

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v3.5.0
Language: C++

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**

CentOS7

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

g++ 4.8.5
cmake 3.18

**What did you do?**

install using configure/make:

./configure --enable-static --enable-shared --with-pic --prefix=/opt/protobuf-3.5.0
sudo make install

install using cmake:

mkdir build
cd build
cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/protobuf-3.5.0 -Dprotobuf_BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=off ../cmake
make
sudo make install


**What did you expect to see**

cmake configuration files should be installed to /opt/protobuf-3.5.0/lib64/cmake.

**What did you see instead?**

cmake files are not installed for the configure build but are for the cmake based build.

However, with the cmake based build it is not possible to create both static and shared versions of protocol buffers at the same time.
You would have to do:

mkdir build
cd build
cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/protobuf-3.5.0-static -Dprotobuf_BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=off -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON ../cmake
make
sudo make install
cd ..

mkdir build2
cd build2
cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/protobuf-3.5.0-shared -Dprotobuf_BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=on ../cmake
make
sudo make install

**What would you like to see?**

1. The cmake/README.md should clarify whether the maintainers support its use on Linux or just windows.
    As it works on Linux I suggest it should be considered supported.

2. The cmake build should allow you to create both shared and static libraries at the same time.

3. The configure and cmake builds should ideally be consistent and equivalent.
Both should install .cmake files if possible 
(this could be done by adding a switch to `configure` to tell it to create them piggy backing of cmake install somehow).

Failing that the build instructions should warn that cmake configuration files will only be installed if the cmake build process is used instead of the configure one.

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**

The file protobuf-3.5.0/cmake/README.md starts:

> This directory contains *CMake* files that can be used to build protobuf
> with *MSVC* on *Windows*. You can build the project form *Command Prompt* 
> and using an *Visual Studio* IDE.

This seems to imply that the cmake build is only intended for use on windows.
However it works just fine on Linux apart from the caveat of not being able install both static and shared libraries simultanously.

I found it necessary to use the cmake build on Linux to work around some issues with FindProtobuf.cmake (in cmake 3.18).
See:

* https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/21228 - FindProtobuf documentation out of date
* https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/21229 - Adding a hint to find_package(protobuf) prevents it finding the package elsewhere
* https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/21230 - FindProtobuf - FindPkgConfig cannot be used as a hint to Find_Package(protobuf)

---

-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON  is needed if the static protocol buffer libraries happen to be
used in shared libraries or you will get recompile with -fPIC errors at link time.
Using static libraries is preferable to avoid end users having to install proto buffers themselves on Linux platforms that don't supply the correct version natively.

nodes.body: Just stumbled upon this issue and was wondering if there's any activity in that regard? I was also surprised that cmake config files are not installed with autotools build and that cmake build is described only for Windows platform.
Any update on this issue?
It is being worked on, but the build system for protobuf is pretty large, so it takes time

Quick update: We're currently in the process of deprecating Autotools usage entirely, and pivoting to supporting only Bazel and CMake.  The CMake configuration is already generated by Bazel today, and we're adding test coverage for build/test/install.  Once Autotools is removed, CMake's install will be the only way to install protobuf from source.

I'll make sure to update the documentation and look into the shared/static issue too

The README has been updated to make it clear that we do support CMake on linux, and we now have tests for build/test/install.  Autotools will be removed entirely very soon (see #10132), so that ambiguity should disappear.

For the static/shared issue I'm a little confused what the problem is.  Are you trying to build shared and static library with a single cmake command?  Or are you trying to install them both to the same directory?  The former seems WAI

body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 3.13.0, (with Lite option on)
Language: Java

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
MacOS 10.15.6

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
AdoptOpenJDK 14, com.google.protobuf 3.13.0 gradle plugin

**What did you do?**
Consider the following oneof type (Proto 3).

```
message Status {
    oneof status {
        bool ok = 1;
        Error error = 2;
    }

    message Error {
        string reason = 1;
    }
}
```

and then merge 2 messages of this type, with different oneof cases:

```
val ok = Status.newBuilder().setOk(true).build()
val error = Status.newBuilder()
        .setError(
            Status.Error.newBuilder()
                .setReason("reason")
                .build()
        ).build()

val result = ok.toBuilder().mergeFrom(error).build()
assert(result.equals(error))
```

**What did you expect to see**
I expected the `error` to override `ok` oneof case in `result` message, so the `result` will contain `error` message, since oneof cases are mutually exclusive.
However, I can't find any rules of merging oneof fields in the documentation, so my expectation might be wrong.

**What did you see instead?**
Crash in mergeFrom method:
```
java.lang.ClassCastException: java.lang.Boolean cannot be cast to com.google.protobuf.MessageLite
	at com.google.protobuf.Internal.mergeMessage(Internal.java:387)
	at com.google.protobuf.MessageSchema.mergeOneofMessage(MessageSchema.java:1409)
	at com.google.protobuf.MessageSchema.mergeSingleField(MessageSchema.java:1355)
	at com.google.protobuf.MessageSchema.mergeFrom(MessageSchema.java:1184)
	at com.google.protobuf.GeneratedMessageLite$Builder.mergeFromInstance(GeneratedMessageLite.java:423)
	at com.google.protobuf.GeneratedMessageLite$Builder.mergeFrom(GeneratedMessageLite.java:418)
```

@acozzette I haven't tested the changes in that PR yet, but just after briefly reviewing the code, I don't think it covers the case I described here

I could be wrong but it looked to me like this test case covered the same bug reported on this issue: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/b774da0d4255e56b957e78115cde7d4e3112af03/java/lite/src/test/java/com/google/protobuf/LiteTest.java#L1358

title: Generated Python protobuffers allow synthetic oneofs in HasField/ClearField/WhichOneof
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: master/v3.6.0/v3.5.0 etc.
Language: C++/Java/Python/C#/Ruby/PHP/Objective-C/Javascript
3.13.0
**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Ubuntu 20.04
**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Python 3.8
**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Compile a proto3 file with optional fields
2. Create an instance of that protobuffer
3. Use the name of the synthetic oneof (i.e. an underscore followed by the name of the field) in `HasField`/`ClearField`/`WhichOneof`

You can see an example of this with `WhichOneof` in a test case: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/b7742c51fdfa2f31f6a5f341f6d0b0df586b4ef1/python/google/protobuf/internal/message_test.py#L1716

**What did you expect to see**
The same errors you get when using non-existing fields with these methods. According to https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/docs/implementing_proto3_presence.md#updating-a-code-generator, there shouldn't be accessors for synthetic oneofs.
**What did you see instead?**
It behaves the same way as a regular oneof

nodes.body: Thank you for the bug report, but I think it was actually a deliberate decision to allow `WhichOneof` to work with synthetic oneofs, since it is a quasi-reflective API. Reflection-based logic that doesn't know about proto3 optional fields should still be able to call `WhichOneof` on a synthetic oneof in order to work correctly. @haberman knows more about this and can correct me if I'm wrong.

title: Add ruby 3.0.0 support
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
ruby

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
Ruby 3.0.0-preview1 was released over the weekend. We'd like to check our ruby services before the official ruby 3.0 release (probably on christmas, as this is the usual ruby release date for new versions). However the google-protobuf gem explicitly prohibits bumping the ruby version to beyond 2.7 (the current stable version):

    Gem::RuntimeRequirementNotMetError: google-protobuf requires Ruby version >= 2.3, < 2.8.dev. The current ruby version is 3.0.0.preview1.
     An error occurred while installing google-protobuf (3.13.0), and Bundler cannot continue.    
     Make sure that `gem install google-protobuf -v '3.13.0' --source 'https://gem.givve.io/'` succeeds before bundling.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The google-protobuf gem is installable under ruby 3.0.0. I'd be happy with a solution that is locked to the preview without any guarantee of functionality in production environments.

nodes.body: Do you know where this requirement is coming from? I see that our gemspec requires `>= 2.3` but I don't see the `< 2.8.dev` anywhere (is that coming from one of our dependencies?)

After hours of being stumped and studying the code for both bundler and gem (since if it isn't provided by you, it must be injected somewhere, right?), it dawned on me that the google-protobuf gem is being supplied in different versions:
- the plain version which we've been looking at, which apparently doesn't have the restriction
- a precompiled version, which has the restriction in place, see https://rubygems.org/gems/google-protobuf/versions/3.13.0-x86_64-linux 

So this seems to be injected by the build process or build system. Which makes sense since the ABI has changed.
I'll have to figure out how to tell bundler that I don't want the precompiled version. Adding a ruby-3.0.0 version to your build system would be great too, though :)

@sriedel Thanks for tracking that down, that is a little surprising but I guess it makes sense. I think in principle we should be able to make our next release add a ruby-3.0 compatible version. @haberman Does that sound doable?
Is there any ETA for supporting ruby 3.0 ?
xref: #8134
This should be fixed as of #8184, released in 3.15.0-rc1. Please let us know if you run into problems.

title: v3.13.0 from Packagist is not up-to-date
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v3.13.0
Language: PHP
Implementation: pure-PHP

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Linux

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a new `composer.json` file with `{
  "require": {
    "google/protobuf": "3.13.0"
  }
}`
2. Run `composer install`
3. Go to `vendor/google/protobuf/src/Google/Protobuf/Internal/Message.php`
4. Look at the content of the function `private function existField`: its content starts with **`$oneof_index = $field->getOneofIndex();`**
5. Go to the v3.13.0 source in [GitHub](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/v3.13.0/php/src/Google/Protobuf/Internal/Message.php#L1571), its content starts with **`$getter = $field->getGetter();`**

**What did you expect to see**
The same content in the vendor package as in the GitHub source.

**What did you see instead?**
An older version of the source code in the vendor package.

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
Because of this, the `Message->serializeToJsonString()` method fails to print proto3 optional fields (see https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-php/issues/425). There may be other consequences we did not notice yet.

nodes.body:
This appears to be related to https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/10346 

As well as the error above the `hasOneOf()` etc method is missing in both the packagist install and the native extension.

As a result packages compiled with protoc 3.13.0 now contain multiple `hasXXXX()` methods that all throw fatal errors when called - for example many of the methods added in https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-php/pull/3327

There seem to be another consequence of this issue as previously reported by @acoulton and recently by https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-php/issues/432: the [`Message.hasOneof` method is defined in v3.13.0](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/v3.13.0/php/src/Google/Protobuf/Internal/Message.php#L228) but is does not seem to be present when using `"google/protobuf": "3.13.0"` in `composer.json`.

Looks like v3.13.0 of [protobuf-php](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-php/blob/v3.13.0/src/Google/Protobuf/Internal/Message.php#L1560) includes the `getOneofIndex`. We should try to get v3.13.0 retagged with the correct code

title: Timestamp JSON parsing doesn't raise ParseError on non-string input
body:
```python
from google.protobuf.json_format import ParseDict, MessageToDict, ParseError
from google.protobuf.timestamp_pb2 import Timestamp

ts = Timestamp()
ts.GetCurrentTime()
rfc3339_time = MessageToDict(ts)
assert isinstance(rfc3339_time, str)
ParseDict(rfc3339_time, ts)
```

This is expected:
```python
try:
    ParseDict('foobar', ts)
except ParseError:
    print('parse error as expected')
```

but this isn't:
```python
try:
    ParseDict({}, ts)
except ParseError:
    pass
```

A good solution IMO would be to gate it in `_ConvertGenericMessage` before calling `FromJsonString` on the respective value.

title: Java toString() skips enums if the index is 0 (proto3)
body:
The java toString() on protobuf objects does not print out enum, if the enum value is 0.
Since proto version 3 requires that the first enum's value must be 0, you are guaranteed that any message using that enum value will not print anything out for that field in a message.

nodes.body: Thank you for the bug report but I think this is working as intended. Proto3 ordinarily makes no distinction between a primitive field being absent and being set to its default value, so if an enum field is set to 0 then that's the same as it not being set at all. However, we are bringing proto2-style optional fields back to proto3. If you want this behavior, you can just mark the field `optional` in your `.proto` file and make sure to pass `--experimental_allow_proto3_optional` to protoc.

No 0 is not the same as not being set. 0 is a valid value. In fact it's a
required valid value because the first entry in the enum must have a value
of zero.

The enum also generates a undefined value of -1. That should be the unset
value. I assume thats why it's there.

If your telling me you cant tell the difference between a unset and set
value and that's correct behavior , that seems crazy to me.

On Thu, Oct 1, 2020, 13:56 Adam Cozzette <notifications@github.com> wrote:

> Thank you for the bug report but I think this is working as intended.
> Proto3 ordinarily makes no distinction between a primitive field being
> absent and being set to its default value, so if an enum field is set to 0
> then that's the same as it not being set at all. However, we are bringing
> proto2-style optional fields back to proto3. If you want this behavior, you
> can just mark the field optional in your .proto file and make sure to
> pass --experimental_allow_proto3_optional to protoc.
>
> —
> You are receiving this because you authored the thread.
> Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub
> <https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/7934#issuecomment-702393154>,
> or unsubscribe
> <https://github.com/notifications/unsubscribe-auth/ABM4KFCA7FS7B6OJMGLQ62DSITUJVANCNFSM4SA5K4UA>
> .
>

Enums need to have a zero value precisely because that is the value they hold when they're unset. The -1 `UNRECOGNIZED` value in Java is different and is what you get if you parse a message containing an unknown enum value. Have you tried setting your field to `optional`? I think that would give you the behavior you're looking for.

body:
I have been using MessageToJson to convert Vision API response to JSON. But today it suddenly stopped working. 

After doing, 
response = client.document_text_detection(image=image)

Then I convert it to JSON using,
json_string = MessageToJson(response)

nodes.body: @monark12 Could you verify what library has the `client.document_text_detection` function?

I think I know what's happening.
I am assuming that the client library version was updated recently. The new versions of Google Cloud API client libraries use [Proto Plus](https://github.com/googleapis/proto-plus-python) to define message types.
The new means of converting to/from json is now:
```python
response = client.document_text_detection(image=image)
json_string = type(response).to_json(response)  # Also works to use the message type directly, e.g.
                                                # json_string = MyMessageType.to_json(response)
```
`to_json` and `from_json` aren't visible to message instances; they _must_ be called from the message class, and the message itself is then passed in.
https://proto-plus-python.readthedocs.io/en/stable/messages.html#serialization

Let us know if that solves the problem!

title: Use ujson or orjson (or any other fast implementation of json) in json_format.py
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
Python

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
Serializing to and deserializing from json in python is painfully slow.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
There're many fast implementations of json in python. The most popular ones are ujson and orjson.
Those implementations are up to 11x times faster than the builtin Json implementation ([source](https://github.com/ijl/orjson#performance)).
Using those (whenever they exist) will make this much faster.
We should also add the optional extra `protobuf[fastjson]` in the python package that will install the fast json implementation as a dependency.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
In our project we're using `json_format.MessageToDict` and `json_format.ParseDict` and serializing to/from json ourselves. But we feel like having it built-in would be nicer.

nodes.body:
Any traction on this ? Some messages can be very long and using `orjson` would speed up de-/serialization a lot.

Since `orjson` is a drop-in replacement of `json`, https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/d16bf914bc5ba569d2b70376051d15f68ce4322d/python/google/protobuf/json_format.py#L53 could be rewritten as 
```
try:
    import orjson as json
except ImportError:
    import json
```

As far as I can tell, neither ujson nor orjson support `object_pairs_hook`. Duplicate rejection is part of the observable interface in json_format:

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/d16bf914bc5ba569d2b70376051d15f68ce4322d/python/google/protobuf/json_format.py#L431

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/d16bf914bc5ba569d2b70376051d15f68ce4322d/python/google/protobuf/json_format.py#L390-L396

Unfortunately, that means `ujson` and `orjson` would not be suitable for use in protobuf.

title: Unmarshal into incorrect type does NOT result in error

nodes.body: Thank you for the bug report but this is actually expected behavior. A protobuf message's schema is expected to change over time, adding new fields and/or removing old ones. The parser ultimately has to be fairly lenient and able to tolerate unexpected fields. As a result, it is pretty typical for a serialized proto to be parsable as a proto of a completely different type. You can get an error if there are missing required fields or if a `string` field has non-UTF8 data (or maybe a few other cases I'm forgetting), but otherwise there usually won't be an error.

To my mind, that's still a bug until it is documented to be the case.  But beyond that, a lenient parser should still provide the ability to determine if you deserialized something incorrectly, even if it is simply comparing typeURL in a serialized form with a static typeURL in the structure. Otherwise, it is literally impossible to determine if you've deserialized a buffer into the correct form, and untold errors could result.  Even if you want the parser to allow that to be done, for deserializing into compatible protos or something, providing a function which would at least allow a check to be performed explicitly seems more than reasonable to provide.  

But documenting the behaviour of the marshal and unmarshal functions when using incompatible protobufs is absolutely necessary.  There is probably lots of inadequately tested code out there that is assuming that the error return value from Unmarshal() is actually meaningful.
For me it is still a bug and not expected behaviour as stated above, unless all the common fields match type, name and position/order in the proto definition, which is not the case here.

title: Syntax for adding a map field to a message builder using FieldDescriptors
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
Java

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**

I'm trying to write a function to populate a message object with arbitrary data for fuzz testing. It recursively traverses the object setting values using FieldDescriptors. The getField/setField API doesn't adequately support doing this for map objects. It requires constructing protobuf.MapEntry objects and adding them as repeated fields. Not only is this syntax unwieldy, but the MapEntry objects fall outside the public API.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A syntax along the lines of `Message.Builder.putMapField(fieldDescriptor, Object key, Object value)` would make this easier and avoid the explicit use of private APIs.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Alternately, I plan to use private APIs and deal with any breakages that might suddenly arise from this.

nodes.body: Fuzzing is valuable and also an edge case that deliberately violates normal boundaries. I'm not hugely surprised or bothered if you have to do weird reflection stuff here to make it work. We'd need a more normal use case to consider this.

title: Question: Why are protobufs not designed to handle large messages?
body:
Dear Protobuf developers

I found https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/techniques#large-data,
> Protocol Buffers are not designed to handle large messages. As a general rule of thumb, if you are dealing in messages larger than a megabyte each, it may be time to consider an alternate strategy.

However, on [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47564437/why-protobuf-is-bad-for-large-data-structures), it seems like answerers have concluded protobufs are not optimal for large data for 1 reason: serialisation/ deserialization overhead. I guess you mean as a file gets bigger, you're less likely going to need all the data, so protobufs (where deserialization is a requirement) would be unoptimal.

_1. Are there any other reasons that come to mind as to why you wouldn't recommend ?_

Finally, the documentation states
> Protocol Buffers do not include any built-in support for large data sets 
_2. What would built-in support look like?_

3. What would you say is the best option for uploading many lists of many numbers (Floats/ doubles)? Serialization is expensive, but sending a stringified list is also space inefficient.

Thanks for reading 🙂

nodes.body:
Strictly speaking, there is a system limit around 2GiB, so it's possible to deal with serialized data up to that size.

The main reason for the advice, however, is that serialization and deserialization incurs unavoidable copies, and often, users store the entire _serialized_ message in memory (in addition to the _deserialized_ structures).

The de/serialization overhead is sort of a red herring in this case... there is overhead, but it's doing something useful. Without understanding your use case, I don't see how the cost of de/serializing could be argued to be worthwhile or not.

Thanks 👍 

> Without understanding your use case, I don't see how the cost of de/serializing could be argued to be worthwhile or not.

Is it right to think that applications which are already processing that data (and thus have it in memory) would find protobufs more useful? This is my use case. An idea I had was to send the output (e.g. feature vector of 2048 floats) of a neural network running on device for many inputs (1000 images) to a server over http in a protobuf message. For 1000, this could be 8MB, but for more images it could be 100MB. 

It seems I am prematurely optimizing, and should just try this approach and see if there are any bottlenecks. Alternatively I can send each feature vector separately in a protobuf message, and incur the overhead of making separate network requests and separate protobuf objects. (Protobuf serialization performance is probably linear though). In this case it would be 8KB of feature vector data per request.

@ben-xD 
It seems that the individual time is reduced, but your transmission times have increased, and the overall time is not necessarily reduced.

nodes.body: Facing the same issue '...Case()' since plugging proto3 classes into Apache KafkaProtobufSerializer.

For the original bug, is it possible that you are running an old version of the protobuf runtime library?

The line numbers in your stack trace seem to match up with protobuf 3.11.x. But the proto3 presence changes were introduced in 3.12.0, and require that version of the library (or newer).

For the Apache KafkaProtobufSerializer, that library may need to be updated to support proto3 presence. Anything using descriptors should be aware that if a oneof is synthetic, it will not have a `*Case` accessor. More information here: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/docs/implementing_proto3_presence.md

title: About style guide for repeated fields
body: In the [style guide](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/style#repeated_fields), it said we should use pluralized names for repeated fields. But if we add a repeated field like "members", generated code gives methods like getMembersList() and getMembers(int index). Should we update the style guide?

nodes.body: I think this is a case where some language implementations are set up better than others when it comes to repeated field naming. For example, the C++ accessors work well with plural names, but in Javascript they sound better with singular names. Unfortunately it is hard to go back and fix things at this point, and I'm afraid we're stuck with the imperfect style guide decision.

title: Accessing `descriptorpb.MessageOptions` in `proto.Marshal` and `proto.Unmarshal`
body:
# Context

I'm working on a security research project where I'd like to be able to modify the `proto.Message`s passed as arguments to `proto.Marshal` and `proto.Unmarshal` based on message options set in the original `.proto` file. 

This behaviour is a hard requirement - we want to ensure any attempt for data to leave the system is correctly handled before it leaves the system 

# Issue 
Unfortunately, I'm unable to access `m.Descriptor().Options()` without first needing to import `descriptorpb` package inside the `proto` package, and that causes a cyclic import loop (because it turns out `descriptorpb` depends on `protoimpl`, which depends on the `proto` package). 

Is there any way that I can access message options inside `proto.Marshal` and `proto/Unmarshal`?**

# What I've Tried So Far

1. I've tried to bypass the import loop by making a Golang `plugin` to dynamically import my mutators in `proto.Marshal` and `proto.Unmarshal`. This plugin correctly imports `descriptorpb`. Unfortunately, I get a panic on using functions loaded in this way, stating: `panic: Descriptor.Options called without importing the descriptor package`

2. I've tried to duplicate `descriptor.pb.go` and create shadows of each referenced folder. That turns out to be prohibitively complex. 

# The Full Import Loop

This is what happens if I try to import `descriptorpb` inside `proto/encode.go`:

title: C#: Increase recursionLimit for MessageParser
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
C#

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
No way to set `recursionLimit` via `MessageParser`.

gRPC library for .NET has [this issue](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/22682) where it fails to parse a message with high recursion. However, there's seemingly no hook to configure a `MessageParser` (the entry point that the generated gRPC code uses) to increase the default recursion limit from 100 to an arbitrary value.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Have a configuration value to set a recursion limit to a higher value, either on a `MessageParser` level or globally.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
-

**Additional context**
Downstream issue: https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/issues/4224

nodes.body:
This is a problem in particular for Kubernetes resources which have many nested elements when represented as yaml, combined with using unstructured data via [Google.Protobuf.WellKnownTypes.Struct](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/c5f7b4b0b32baab4396d6c023dd4d74d593a0e2f/csharp/src/Google.Protobuf/WellKnownTypes/Struct.cs#L80), which effectively reduces the recursion limit by a factor of 3x.

A much needed quick fix could be to simply increase the default recursion limit to account for this, from 100 to 300 or more, and a long term configurable limit could be devised after said quick fix is released.
I think the right solution would be to provide a hook for configuring the marshallers in gRPC. Increasing the limit globally for everyone doesn't sound like a good solution.

I filed https://github.com/grpc/grpc-dotnet/issues/1983 to address the root cause of this and I'm going to close this issue as changing the default recursion limit doesn't really solve the problem (as different projects will need different recursion limits).

title: Documentation: Using CMake for non-Windows builds
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for feature requests (including cleanup requests) only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->


**What language does this apply to?**
CMake

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
I want to integrate protobuf in a CMake based cross platform build, especially the library. The documentation of the cmake subfolder only mentions Windows. However, building on MacOS with CMake works as intended for me.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
If possible I'd like to use CMake to perform the build on all platforms :) So I'd really appreciate if the documentation would contain any information on building for different platforms than Windows to be sure that I'm not relying on untested or undefined behaviour.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
If that's indeed untested or risky for some reasons, I'd like to find some more explanation about that in the cmake subfolders readme on why it's not possible and if this will be possible in future.

nodes.body: CMake should work on other platforms and we were actually thinking about using CMake as a general replacement for the autotools builds, but we do need to update the documentation.

One caveat here: the new CMake files installed by protobuf itself use a lower-case package name (`protobuf`), while CMake itself ships with a `FindProtobuf.cmake` script that requires an upper-case package name (`Protobuf`). This can cause issues, either the newer scripts not being found on UNIX systems (as filesystems are case-senstive there) or the older ones being used, resulting in an error with `find_package_handle_standard_args` complaining about wrong casing in the package name.

To mitigate the issue, explicitly tell CMake which method you want to use, either the find module or the package config files.

For older protobuf versions without CMake support, or if you don't want to use the newer scripts and have headers/libs in your prefix path list, use:

```cmake
find_package(Protobuf MODULE REQUIRED)
``` 

To use the protobuf-provided config files, call it like this:

```cmake
find_package(protobuf NO_MODULE REQUIRED)
```

This makes writing CMake scripts for builds you don't have under your control a bit iffy though, you'd need to run both commands and see if one of them finds protobuf:

```cmake
find_package(Protobuf MODULE)
if(NOT TARGET protobuf::libprotobuf)
    find_package(protobuf NO_MODULE)
    if(NOT TARGET protobuf::libprotobuf)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "Protobuf not found, but required!")
    endif()
endif()
```

In case you prefer the protobuf-provided config files, check with `NO_MODULE` first. If the package is not required, leave out the inner `if` statement.

title: Support repeated / map fields in explicit presence tracking
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
Regarding proto3 optional fields added experimentally in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/docs/field_presence.md

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
With re-introduction of presence tracking (thank you!) since 3.12 it's now much more convenient to use protobuf for "patch" functionality where the same message format / API can be used to store state, as well as incremental updates to it. However it's still not a complete system, since repeated and map fields do not support presence tracking, thus there is no way to distinguish repeated/map field not being set and being set to empty value.

My use case is for proto3 message to represent a "patch" / "diff" / "override" of other message, where fields set on given message are treated as higher priority / updated values of prior/existing message. When repeated field in the new message is set to non-empty value there is no problem, I can replace the existing value with new collection, but when new message has empty repeated field, there is no way to distinguish whether the empty collection is intended as new value or simply lack of update.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
repeated and map fields should support HasField functionality, depending on language 'null' could be used to represent lack of presence for given field.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- not using repeated fields, or wrapping them in sub-messages
- using external mechanisms for tracking presence of repeated/map fields (separate / field mask field)
- using a sentinel "special" value inside repeated field collection to mark "empty" collection (in this scenario empty repeated field could be interpreted as no-presence of that field and singleton with sentinel value could be interpreted as present "empty" value)

**Additional context**
I suppose this feature is currently not supported due to wire-format used for repeated fields (and map fields, which AFAIK are simply repeated key-value pairs underneath), which doesn't explicitly track the repeated collection itself and instead relies on elements using the repeated field's number to be appended to the collection in the object. Because of this design unfortunately I don't see a way to add such feature while keeping binary compatibility with repeated fields not using optional presence tracking.

I suppose the only way to implement it would be to add some special marker for optional repeated fields in the wire format. Anyway, it would be great to have this feature considered or to get your opinions on that - this would bring much more completeness to the API exposed by proto3. For "patch" functionality specifically it's still not the end of the topic, since that needs to also represent "field removal", however it's easier to settle on workarounds and conventions for that than solving repeated field assignment / presence checks.

nodes.body: I'm afraid we will not be able to support this directly, since as you mentioned the wire format has no inherent way to represent presence for repeated fields and maps. A separate field mask might be the best way to go.

Does anyone else prioritize having field presence for repeated fields and maps over the current repeated/map wire format? Is it possible (in proto4, for example) to reconsider the wire format for repeated/maps in order to support the `optional` flag for maps and repeated fields, even though it will sacrifice the benefits of the current wire format?

Sorry if the question is naive, I'm also designing gRPC Update RPCs and would prefer not to use FieldMasks. I'm am aware of https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/v3.12.0/docs/field_presence.md but don't have too much context on historical decisions with regards to field presence in the protobuf community.
Closing per @acozzette 's comment

title: [C#] Make message parsing primitives public
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
C#

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
Trying to manually marshall a message from a buffer, but unlike Java, several parsing primitives from `CodedInputStream` such as `ReadRawVarint32` are not public. This significantly limits the utility of the new high-performance API's (e.g. `IBufferWriter<byte>`) or requires poor code hygiene (see the alternatives section below).

**Describe the solution you'd like**

At a very bare minimum, having some of the the same Java members available in dotnet, including:

##### CodedInputStream
- [ ] `public static int readRawVarint32(final InputStream input)`
- [ ] `public static int readRawVarint32(final int firstByte, final InputStream input)`
- [ ] `public static int decodeZigZag32(final int n)`
- [ ] `public static long decodeZigZag64(final long n)`

##### CodedOutputStream
- [ ] `public static int encodeZigZag32(final int n)`
- [ ] `public static long encodeZigZag64(final long n)`

Much, much, more practically for those using `IBufferWriter<byte>` to do custom (zero/minimal-copy) marshaling, it would be ideal to have access to many of the members of `ReadingPrimitives` and `WritingPrimitives`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
1. Copy-and-pasting Protobuf source into my application. 😞 
1. Hand-rolling varint code.
1. Casting `IBufferWriter<byte>` to `ArrayBufferWriter<byte>`, pinning the array, and then passing an `UnmanagedMemoryStream` to `CodedOutputStream`. This works, but is violating abstractions, requires an `unsafe` block, and breaks if you call `SerializationContext.SetPayloadLength` which causes `SerializationContext.GetBufferWriter` to return a `HttpResponsePipeWriter` instead of a `ArrayBufferWriter`.
1. Both 1 and 2

**Additional context**
Related to:
- protocolbuffers/protobuf#3431, and my use case is very much aligned with those mentioned in that issue.
- jtattermusch/protobuf/pull/8 as this is another big missing piece 😉

nodes.body:
I have a related but perhaps more easily encountered problem: providing a `BytesBuffer` object to satisfy a `bytes` field requires copying the data.[1] `ByteString` as well. A private constructor exists which does no copying. This constructor or another API should be exposed to elide the copies. This could be taken further and the C++ API mimicked so a pointer and length could be submitted to avoid copying in data via Marshal.

The latter was claimed to be problematic but this concern was not clearly articulated. Certainly C# is deficient in that all safe types must be constructed with copying but a workaround is worthwhile. Either 2 (unsafe) or 3 (safe) copies are needed before protobuf has the data.

body:
<!--

-->

Version: v3.9.

ubuntu 18.04

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
gcc 7.5

**What did you do?**
I have a wrapper for protobuf which has some bugs and may pass size=-1 to msg.SerializeToArray()
It supposed to be failed but nothing occures. 
I checked the source code in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/3.9.x/src/google/protobuf/message_lite.cc#L488
The thing is when we compared a size_t with int(-1), -1 will be treated as 18446744073709551615(=2^64-1), thus SerializePartialToArray() won't return false and size will not be checked anymore.

title: PROTOBUF_MAYBE_CONSTEXPR should not be constexpr on MinGW
body:
I tried to compile protobuf 3.14.0 for Windows with MinGW-w64 and got this compiler error:
```
src/google/protobuf/map_field.h:336:37: error: call to non-'constexpr' function 'google::protobuf::internal::WrappedMutex::WrappedMutex()'
```
It appears this is documented and fixed as an MSVC issue, but it seems to be a general Windows issue.
So after making the following change compilation was succesful:
```
patch -ulbf src/google/protobuf/port_def.inc << EOF
@@ -560,10 +560,10 @@
 #define PROTOBUF_CONSTINIT
 #endif

-// Some constructors can't be constexpr under MSVC, but given that MSVC will not
+// Some constructors can't be constexpr under Windows, but given that Windows will not
 // do constant initialization of globals anyway we can omit `constexpr` from
 // them. These constructors are marked with PROTOBUF_MAYBE_CONSTEXPR
-#if defined(_MSC_VER)
+#if defined(_WIN32)
 #define PROTOBUF_MAYBE_CONSTEXPR
 #else
 #define PROTOBUF_MAYBE_CONSTEXPR constexpr
EOF
```

title: Breakout "well-known" protos out of Java core library into separate bazel rules
body:
This applies to Java.

Is there anyway to break out "well known" protos into separate jar instead of in core? https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/c981d39d1e3d033c4f00dd48d16e8bdce55a3861/java/core/BUILD#L103

The reason is that we vendor all protobufs and compile them on our own to ensure the same version. Right now, the "well known" protos are compiled into the core library and thus collide with our vendored ones.

The ideal solution would be to have two bazel java_library rules the current "core" rule (without the well known protobufs as sources) and "well_known_java_protos" (with the well known protos as source to compile). The "well_known_java_protos" can be a dependency on "core". This would allow us to use our vendored versions of the well known protos.

Alternative solutions would be to doctor resulting core jar to remove well known proto java class files, but this is less than ideal and would rather be avoided.

nodes.body: I'm afraid this would break backwards compatibility.

title: mergeFrom for repeated fields
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for feature requests (including cleanup requests) only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->


**What language does this apply to?**
Java

If it's a proto syntax change, is it for proto2 or proto3?
proto3

If it's about generated code change, what programming language?
Java

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
In the current `mergeFrom` implementation, it will override existing fields if those are singular. However, for repeated, `mergeFrom` would simply concatenate the fields.

This will cause a lot of duplicates.

As an example, let's say we have a wrapper (`orders.proto`) that has 10 (`order.proto`) at the moment.
With new messages coming in (which contains 5 new orders and 5 existing orders), the mergeFrom as the name suggested, I expect it would only concatenate new orders which would result in 15 orders.


**Describe the solution you'd like**

Instead of using `addAll` method from `java.util.Collections.emptyList()`, we can either
> use `set` to drop the duplicate

> iterate through the new list, and only if add the order not already in existance

**Describe alternatives you've considered**



**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

We could add an overloaded method of `mergeFrom` to give this option to mergeWithoutDuplicte.
```
public Builder mergeFrom(... other, boolean mergeWithoutDuplicte) {

  .....
 if(mergeWithoutDuplicte){
   //drop the duplicate
 }
}
```

nodes.body:
I'm not a Protobuf dev, but I think this needs a bit more clarification. Are you suggesting that merging repeated (what about composite?) fields should behave like singular values and get overwritten with the values in the other message, or are you suggesting some sort of smart merge based on the values of the data?

Protobuf is a serialization format that has no context about what the values represent, so it'd be the wrong place for implementing some sort of smart value filtering. (Why are you sending unwanted duplicate orders in the first place?)

I was wondering what's the state of this issue? API wise I'd say that merge from should accept some strategy to specify whether repeated fields should be replaced or merged. As for the use case you can imagine bidirectional streaming where the server sends full tick only once, then send small delta updates for fields that have changed. As the client only wants to know the current state it's convenient to mergeFrom proto messages in order to get one object with all the fields containing the most recent value.

Changing the existing semantics for this is definitely not something we want to pursue.  There is too much code that would break.  Adding a policy object is possible, but is a far larger piece of design and change then we will likely take on in the near term

I fully understand the hesitation with this feature, and agree that's not exactly in the scope of protobufs. However, it seems like this request is popping here and there since 2012 so maybe it's worth reconsidering it?

In case I'd like to fork the project and compile my own version, could you provide some more insights regarding what can go wrong? I don't have much knowledge about protobuf internals, however, since most of the work for merge is already done, and list case with replacing value should (hopefully?) be easier than merging itself I was wondering what are the possible places I could mess something up? Would replacing `ListFieldSchema` in `ManifestSchemaFactory` (based on java implementation) with my own version doing replace rather than merge ` be a good place to start looking?

body:
Version: 7b352d318b9ae8f65ddc85b7eb7e9921911cec6f
OS: Ubuntu 18.04.2, Linux 4.15
Toolchain: G++ 7.4

### Context

Version 4b389fad575f830fee4a39287ebfd53a6f0862b2 removed PTHREAD_CFLAGS from "Libs" in protobuf.pc.in and protobuf-lite.pc.in. This results in "-pthread" not passed to the linker.

GCC manuals from version 7+ state, for "-pthread":

Update "m4/ax_pthread.m4" to use latest version. Have not verified if latest version adds "-pthread" to PTHREAD_LIBS, I'd expect so. Can this be a submodule so this is up-to-date with the GNU repo?

The only Arm based package that I can see on the release page is `protoc-3.14.0-linux-aarch_64.zip`.

When adding the `protoc` binary to my PATH, I receive a `cannot execute binary file` when executing `protoc --version` in my terminal for example.
It might take us some time to be able to start publishing precompiled binaries for Apple ARM machines, but you should still be able to use protobuf by building from source.

Why was this issue closed? I still see no precompiled binaries for Mac arch 64? I am particularly interested in a precompiled Java build. 

```

     Searched in the following locations:
```

> It might take us some time to be able to start publishing precompiled binaries for Apple ARM machines, but you should still be able to use protobuf by building from source.

@acozzette how would you do that? - I'm unable to do so: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/8372
Why closed this issue?
LOL. Classic Google move.

Having this Just Work™️ would be fantastic, and I think it makes sense to keep this issue open until then.

While waiting, I have had success by using the `protoc` binary from brew:
* follow instructions on https://brew.sh to install brew
* run `brew install protobuf` in a terminal.
This should result in `protoc` being available in your path. Note that with the default zsh, the default shell on recent macOS, one needs to type the command `rehash` to detect newly installed binaries or changes to the `PATH` environment variable.

Would really love to see some support for this - protobuf is an awesome project, and there are a lot of automated build systems (Maven for example) that break when including standard protobuf dependencies. M1 is most likely here to stay for quite a while and I'd be happy to provide remote access to an M1 machine if Google doesn't have them readily available.

A stopgap solution was merged https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/8557 However this issue is about true native support, rather than reusing the x86_64 artifact, so I feel this issue should be reopened.

title: support for code generation by urls
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
I do not know the internal architecture of protoc, but I guess loading .proto files are common for all languages. So it should apply to all supported plugins. (At least that's how I would do it)

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
Sharing .protoc files between different projects in a microservice arrangement is challenging. Even if someone owns all the client and server ends its not obvious to share the same proto definitions between them. Furthermore, protoc's dumbness about relative and absolute paths does not help. If a service publishes its interface definitions on a HTTP endpoint that can be downloaded by clients, however the process is complicate to automatize. The trivial solution would be if the code generation mechanism used the HTTP endpont (URL) directly for generation.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Generating a single proto file with a plugin (plugin is a placeholder here):
`protoc --plugin_out=plugin_specific_stuff http://my.service/proto/service_definition.proto`
Searching for imports using a "wildcard" url:
`protoc --plugin_out=plugin_specific_stuff --proto_path=http://protos.google.com/well-known-types/ http://my.service/proto/service_definition.proto`
In this case the generator would use the url specified at --proto_path to find any import in the service_definition.proto file by appending the given url with the proto file name such as 
`http://protos.google.com/well-known-types/google/protobuff/empty.proto`
for an import defined as
`import "google/protobuf/empty.proto";`
[note: the http://protos.google.com/well-known-types/ url is just an idealistic example]

**Additional context**
As GRPC becomes the de facto standard for interservice communication and as being supported by frameworks like .NETCore or Flutter it is evidently going to be the standard for client-server communication also - it should have bigger and better support in terms of tooling and automatization. The difficulties that protoc has at the moment will avert developers coming from convenient development environments from using it and therefore slowing down adoption of this great technology. I think it is inevitable to provide better support for the most common usage scenarios. If my case seems to be one, thank you for considering my suggestions. Anyways, great work, thanks.

nodes.body: Inside google this problem is completely solved by the source repository. .proto files are source code and can be shared just like .java files, .xml files, .py files or anything else. This doesn't seem like a feature that belongs in the layer of the proto library itself.

title: mergeFromJsonString dumps core for a valid RFC3339 timestamp
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 3.10
Language: PHP

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Linux

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
php 7.2.24

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Perform `mergeFromJsonString` on an `RFC3339` compliant timestamp with a non zero minute time offset `"2020-11-15T11:10:00+02:30"`. (Note: this works perfectly for `"2020-11-15T11:10:00+02:00"`)

**What did you expect to see**
The `json` read correctly into `\Google\Protobuf\Timestamp`; as `protobuf` says that `Timestamp` (as a WKT) uses `RFC3339`.

**What did you see instead?**
Segmentation fault (core dumped)

Make sure you include information that can help us debug (full error message, exception listing, stack trace, logs).

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**

If I followed along the code correctly, here the minutes are hardcoded as "00" effectively disallowing any timestamp with non-"00" offset in minutes.
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/php/ext/google/protobuf/php-upb.c#L6931

If I understood [RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) correctly, there should be no such restriction.

I could not find any existing open or closed issue which addressed this under php label, hence, I created one.

nodes.body: Can you try with the newest version of protobuf? The protobuf-PHP library has changed a lot since version 3.10.

I'm glad to hear it's no longer a segfault.

The parse error you see is intentional: the code is written to only accept time zone offsets ending in `:00`. When I wrote the code I believed that this was according to spec, however I may have been mistaken. I'll circle back with the team to discuss when we're all back at work next week.
The conclusion is that we should accept any minute 0-59 in the offset. I'll write a fix for this.

title: Fortify flags memory leak
body:
Microfocus Fortify is (sadly) the current standard static code analysis tool for the department of defense. Among the many false positives it detects, this construct does appear to be a real memory leak.

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/d7a26435fb36b61d742c053407e3a61fb1012706/src/google/protobuf/repeated_field.h#L1572

`new_rep` is last referenced on line line 1585, and I can't see where it is assigned to any RAII type or otherwise managed before it goes out of scope.

If I'm missing something, I'll mark this as yet another false-positive and move on.

nodes.body: The logic here is a bit convoluted but new_rep does end up getting deleted. `arena_or_elements_` stores `new_rep->elements` [here](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/d7a26435fb36b61d742c053407e3a61fb1012706/src/google/protobuf/repeated_field.h#L1583), and the destructor deletes it [here](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/d7a26435fb36b61d742c053407e3a61fb1012706/src/google/protobuf/repeated_field.h#L1210), using the `rep()` member function which subtracts an offset from `arena_or_elements_` to get back a pointer to the `Rep`.

Could you walk through it in a bit more detail? The line in question is only reached if the `arena` is null. Here is a naked new, assigned to a pointer, and no initialization. The pointer is cast, but no constructor fires. On line 1583, where `arena_or_elements_` is assigned, it has no value.

Fortify is incredibly stupid, and protobuf gives it fits, but I'm just not able to justify this finding yet.

Hmmm. Looks like `rep()` is ... questionable, but I guess I see how it's working. `new_rep->elements` is an array, so it is a valid address to assign on 1583. "Clever" pointer arithmetic lets you back up to the base address.
Right, `new_rep->elements` is basically equivalent to `new_rep + 8`, so we can get back the original pointer by subtracting 8 again. (It would be different on 32-bit platforms but you get the idea.)

title: bufferSize must be >= 0
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for feature requests (including cleanup requests) only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->


**What language does this apply to?**
Java

If it's a proto syntax change, is it for proto2 or proto3?
proto3

If it's about generated code change, what programming language?
Java

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**

The current type for serializedSize is `int`, which has a size limit of 2,147,483,648. For a larger sized data, it will throw out
`bufferSize must be >= 0` during serialization.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

instead of 
```
    public int getSerializedSize() {
      int size = memoizedSize;
      if (size != -1) return size;
...
```

Can we change to `long`

```
    public int getSerializedSize() {
      **long** size = memoizedSize;
      if (size != -1) return size;
...
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

nodes.body: This is a constraint imposed by the protobuf format. A length-delimited value's length is an int32, so this can't be changed without breaking the format.

title: Why use 64-bit representation for negative numbers

nodes.body:
this is as per protobuf wire format:

*If you use int32 or int64 as the type for a negative number, the resulting varint is always ten bytes long – it is, effectively, treated like a very large unsigned integer.*
https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/encoding

I guess the exact reason is that there's only one "varint" wire type in protobuf wire format and  you need to be able to decode a value even without prior knowledge of whether something is int32 or int64
 https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/encoding#varints 
(but I'm actually not an expert on protobuf wire format design - perhaps other would have a better explanation).

According to the current design of Protobuf, the data can be decoded in the absence of type information;

But in fact, there is type information in the code generated by the proto file, so if I hold the type information of the field, can I not need to store 10 bytes?

> According to the current design of Protobuf, the data can be decoded in the absence of type information;
> 
> But in fact, there is type information in the code generated by the proto file, so if I hold the type information of the field, can I not need to store 10 bytes?

Pragmatically, it's quite simple - if you need negative values to not be 10bytes long when encoded, just use the `sint32` type and you're done.
Yep I understand it. thanks！！

title: How to use the new Span API on the C# project
body:
I'm trying to do the following:

I have a C# application that uses a C shared library and does a pinvoke to this C lib, it then receives a IntPtr pointing to data allocated in C side containing a protobuf message.

I'm trying to build this message on C# side by using Message.MergeFrom() on the C# side but without allocating new memory, just accessing directly the unmanaged memory from C side.

I thought this would be possible now since https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/5888 but I'm having a hard time trying to figure out how.

Any help?

Best!

nodes.body: Removed assignment from myself - I haven't looked at the Span API in detail with protobuf and don't have time to take on work outside my main projects right now.

Note that general usage questions shouldn't be posted here, just actual issues.

Nevertheless: to parse from unmanaged memory, what you want to do is to first create a Span<byte> from the unmanaged pointer to the data. (That needs to be done under `unsafe` block). After that you can just call, 
e.g. `YourMessage.Parser.ParseFrom(ReadOnlySequence<byte> data)`.  A read only sequence can be created allocation-free from a Span<byte>.  

FTR the API was added here: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/7351

Sorry and thanks @jtattermusch. Can you say how do I create the ReadOnlySequence from the Span? I can't find any method for doing so...

I'm trying like:

```
Span<byte> data = new Span...
Protos.Request.Parser.ParseFrom(new ReadOnlySequence<byte>(data));
```

But this isn't allowed: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'System.Span<byte>' to 'System.ReadOnlyMemory<byte>' csharp(CS1503)

> Sorry and thanks @jtattermusch. Can you say how do I create the ReadOnlySequence from the Span? I can't find any method for doing so...
> 
> I'm trying like:
> 
> ```
> Span<byte> data = new Span...
> Protos.Request.Parser.ParseFrom(new ReadOnlySequence<byte>(data));
> ```
> 
> But this isn't allowed: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'System.Span' to 'System.ReadOnlyMemory' csharp(CS1503)

Sorry, I spoke too soon.

Yes, you need to create a ReadOnlyMemory<byte> from an unmanaged pointer (as ReadOnlySequence doesn't take Span).
That's done by subclassing a MemoryManager:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.buffers.memorymanager-1?view=net-5.0

Examples:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/d7a26435fb36b61d742c053407e3a61fb1012706/csharp/src/Google.Protobuf.Test/ByteStringTest.cs#L392

title: Security vulnerability
body:
Veracode scan found this security vulnerability in map_entry_lite.h:275

Integer Overflow or Wraparound (CWE ID 190)(3 flaws)
Description
An integer overflow condition exists when an integer that has not been properly sanity checked is used in the
determination of an offset or size for memory allocation, copying, concatenation, or similarly. If the integer in question
is incremented past the maximum possible value, it may wrap to become a very small, negative number, therefore
providing an unintended value. This occurs most commonly in arithmetic operations or loop iterations. Integer
overflows can often result in buffer overflows or data corruption, both of which may be potentially exploited to execute
arbitrary code.
Effort to Fix: 2 - Implementation error. Fix is approx. 6-50 lines of code. 1 day to fix.
Recommendations
Perform bounds checking to ensure that integers do not exceed the maximum possible value.

273 int GetCachedSize() const override {
274    int size = 0;
275    size += has_key() ? static_cast<int>(kTagSize) +
276                            KeyTypeHandler::GetCachedSize(key())
277                      : 0;
278    size += has_value() ? static_cast<int>(kTagSize) +
279                              ValueTypeHandler::GetCachedSize(value())
280                        : 0;
281    return size;
282  }

nodes.body: `GetCachedSize` is always called after `ByteSizeLong`, which ensures the size doesn't exceed 2G.

The line in question is:
size += has_key() ? static_cast<int>(kTagSize) + KeyTypeHandler::GetCachedSize(key()) : 0;
Even if ByteSizeLong is called before, how can you guarantee that the sum of 
static_cast<int>(kTagSize) + KeyTypeHandler::GetCachedSize(key())
is not > 2G?

title: Documentation is a little misleading and it should be updated
body:
See https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/go-generated#invocation

> If the --go_opt=paths=source_relative flag is given to protoc, the output file is placed in the same relative directory as the input file. For example, the file protos/foo.proto results in a file named protos/foo.pb.go.
When you run the proto compiler like this:
`protoc --proto_path=src --go_out=build/gen --go_opt=paths=source_relative src/foo.proto src/bar/baz.proto`
the compiler will read the files src/foo.proto and src/bar/baz.proto. It produces two output files: build/gen/foo.pb.go and build/gen/bar/baz.pb.go.

The problem here is 
> the output file is placed in the same relative directory as the input file

and then 
> It produces two output files: build/gen/foo.pb.go and build/gen/bar/baz.pb.go.

Why are the new files not placed where the docs say they should be placed i.e. `src/` and are instead placed where the flag `--go_out=build/gen` dictates? It seems if both flags are provided there is special behavior where the compiler doesn't guess the output directory based on the package name, but it _**doesn't**_ necessarily put the output files where `--go_opt=paths=source_relative` dictates they should go. Seems like the special behavior is when both are provided just use `--go_out` to calculate the output directory from the root.

Either way, can we please make this more clear? I can't find the repo for the google-developers documentation as it is probably not open.

title: Add null as new wire type.
body:
Protobuf as tagged protocol has field presence but not nullability. All proposed nullability approaches like message boxing or oneof have various disadvantages. Explicit nullability could be useful for mapping Json merge patches (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) to gRPC.
I guess it would be convenient to have explicit nullability at wire protocol level. Null value can be expressed as a new wire type, i.e. 7. Null encoding should be empty, without any data following tag. Fields can be marked as nullable with some attribute in proto definition. Nullable field can be present on wire as tag with null wire type or field own type. Like in json, fields will have three possible states: none/null/value.

title: /BUILD and /protobuf.bzl have unnecessarily hard dependencies on rules_python
body:
The files `/BUILD` and `/protobuf.bzl` both load from `@rules_python` at the top level, which defeats Bazel's lazy fetching of dependencies. This forces projects that depend on Protobuf, but not Python, to need the `@rules_python` dependency declared.

For `/BUILD`, I recommend moving the `py_library` targets into a new file `python/BUILD` and setting up aliases at the old locations. See PR #7190 for a similar change applied to the Java targets.

For `/protobuf.bzl`, the `py_proto_library()` symbol should be moved into an equivalent file under `python/`. Doing this as a breaking change would be easiest since `py_proto_library()` is unfortunately a macro, but it may also be possible to replace it with a rule and thereby maintain the existing API.
