title: Python precision wrong in Float fields
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v3.11.3
Language: Python

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Windows/Mac

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Python 3.7

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
`pip install onnx`
```
import onnx
value = 0.1
attr = onnx.AttributeProto(type="FLOAT", f=value)
assert attr.f == value # AssertionError
#  0.10000000149011612
```

**What did you expect to see**
Assert successfully.

**What did you see instead?**
Assertion failed.

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
Issue: https://github.com/onnx/onnx/issues/3261
ONNX uses protobuf (3.11.3) to define its model graph. Actually I am not sure it's a protobuf issue or it's something we can handle from ONNX. I also tried a solution here: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/4569 by setting `export PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python`, but I still encountered the same error.

Is it a known float issue in protobuf? Thank you!

nodes.body:
This is the expect behavior.

History: python language itself does not have C-style 32-bit floats, a Python float is a C-style 64-bit double. Thus the pure Python protobuf implementation was using double precision for both float and double fields in memory (the cpp extension implementation uses 32-bit single float precision for float fields). However the wire format for float is always 4 bytes (32-bits), so after a serialize/parse round trip, pure python could have a different number.. Example:
  msg.float_f = 99.997
  self.assertEqual(msg.float_f, 99.997)  # pass
  msg.ParseFromString(msg.SerializeToString())
  self.assertEqual(msg.float_f, 99.997)  # fail

Thus we changed pure protobuf python behavior to use 4 bytes (32-bits)  for float field.


Doing equality comparisons on floating point values is fragile. Ways to prevent breakages for compare: 
    1. Use assertAlmostEqual(), assertSequenceAlmostEqual(), round(), format()... 
    2. Change the float field to a double field in .proto files if required and safe (usually not safe).
    3. Only use float precision accurately presentable values in tests.


Feel free to reopen if still have questions

Hi, I wonder if there is any other solution besides set `export PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python` or replace `float` to `double`.because datatype must be distinguished in out projects。
I look forward to hearing from you soon.
Hey @Moxie1337 , did you find any solution?

title: Fatal error with v3.14

nodes.body: Also, no error when using google/protobuf:v3.14.0 PHP library. However the C extension throws the above Fatal error.

I think I know what is going on (thanks for the excellent repro, btw). The newer version of the code (soon to be released in 3.15.0-rc2) gives a better error message:

> PHP Warning:  proto descriptor was previously loaded (included in multiple metadata bundles?): proto/common/common.proto in /tmp/protobuf_testcase/serviceB/client/php/src/ServiceB/Metadata/Common/Common.php on line 24

The problem is that `.proto` files are uniquely identified by their file name, relative to whatever base or base directories you are using. In this example you appear to have two files whose canonical name is `proto/common/common.proto`. This means that both files cannot be loaded into the same runtime image: loading the second one will fail, which will then cause the symbols from the second file to not be found.

The solution is either to change one of the file names, or alternatively include the parent directory (`ServiceA` / `ServiceB`) in the canonical filename path.

Hi @haberman,

Thanks for checking this. From your reply, I understand this is happening because of the conflicting paths.

However, since this was working fine with v3.10.0 and breaking in one of the recent releases, shouldn't it be considered a regression?

Also, if this is the intended behaviour, the PHP extension should produce the same error message as the C extension, but that works fine.

Sorry for being too pushy on this but the suggested solution is not convenient nor reliable. As a downstream service which calls multiple other services by loading their clients via composer, it's very hard to ensure their paths do not collide. It also does not make sense for a consumer to dictate where the upstream service places it's proto files.

I agree that the PHP extension should be fixed to produce the same error message.

I can understand your perspective that this appears to be a regression. But the old behavior is buggy and can't be supported in the longer term.

For example, protobuf reflection generally offers a way to look up a file's reflection from its filename. In C++ you can write:

```c++
  google::protobuf::DescriptorPool::generated_pool()->FindFileByName("proto/common/common.proto");
```

This function should eventually be available in PHP also. If we allowed multiple files named `proto/common/common.proto`, the line above would be ambiguous.

Other languages like C++ already disallow this. It's important that we don't have protos that are loadable in some languages but not others. 

I do apologize that this wasn't checked before, I recognize it is intrusive that we are starting to check this now.

> It also does not make sense for a consumer to dictate where the upstream service places it's proto files.

There is already an expectation that upstream services will not create conflicting PHP class names, yes? If you had two libraries that both defined a class called `Proto\Common\Common`, the class names would conflict. If two libraries both had filenames like `Proto/Common/Common.php` those would conflict too. The same concept applies to .proto files.

Hi @haberman this stand has been recently changed for the golang compiler https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/1122, https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go/commit/febffdd88e85cb4402205142aaa1a4cc64d0d375

Are there plans to change this for PHP as well? If not we would still need to enforce unique file paths across services.

> There is already an expectation that upstream services will not create conflicting PHP class names, yes?

But the upstream services *are* disambiguating their names. One is defining `package serviceA.common;` and the other is defining `package serviceB.common;`. The requirement that every _source_ filename is globally unique across _all source code_ is unworkable in the real world, where not everyone works for the same company and checks code into the same monorepo.

> It also does not make sense for a consumer to dictate where the upstream service places it's proto files.

Is it the intention, then, that changing Protobuf source file layouts is to be considered a breaking API change?  This isn't mentioned anywhere in the [File location](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#location) documentation, probably because it would be a bizarre requirement to impose.

**What language does this apply to?**
This request pertains to Python generated code.

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
A *\_pb2.py should fail gracefully if it is being run against a version of Protobuf that is too old.  Something similar is implemented for C++ compilation in the generated *.pb.h which contain, for example for Protobuf 3.9.x

For example, 3.12.x *\_pb2.py could exit gracefully if \_\_version\_\_ (from \_\_init\_\_.py) is less than 3.12.0.

C++ generated code

I am using protobuf with arena allocation enabled. When I called Reflection::SetAllocatedMessage and Reflection::ReleaseMessage on the message with arena enabled, I noticed that ReleaseMessage returns a heap object as expected.

I tried to call the reflection equivalent, [Reflection::UnsafeArenaReleaseMessage](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/69694080ff3fbc496ec01d9a88248aa3e6faaf67/src/google/protobuf/generated_message_reflection.cc#L1628), but found that it's private. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Since the implementation of UnsafeArenaReleaseMessage repeats the error checking from ReleaseMessage, it might be simple as marking UnsafeArenaReleaseMessage as public:

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/69694080ff3fbc496ec01d9a88248aa3e6faaf67/src/google/protobuf/generated_message_reflection.cc#L1661-L1663
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/69694080ff3fbc496ec01d9a88248aa3e6faaf67/src/google/protobuf/generated_message_reflection.cc#L1631-L1632

I'm happy to submit a PR if the maintainers agree that this method can be made public.

Avoid using arenas and reflection at the same time, but this would cause a big performance regression in my application.

none

title: Python Wheel using dynamic linking (e.g. built with `--cpp_implementation` not `--cpp_implementation --compile_static_extension`)
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for feature requests (including cleanup requests) only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What language does this apply to?**
Python
If it's a proto syntax change, is it for proto2 or proto3? N/A
If it's about generated code change, what programming language? Python

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**

Trying to use protobuf with cpp_implementation in the same python process as a library that's _also_ using protobuf under the covers.

This seems to be a widespread issue in the tensorflow community.  My issue isn't with tensorflow but the problem is identical. Tensorflow seems to have fixed this by suggesting people pin to an older version of protobuf before the wheels started shipping the native extension.

(e.g. https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/8394, 
https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/9525#issuecomment-385475293
https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/24976,
https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/35573,
https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/v2.0.0/tensorflow/contrib/makefile/rename_protobuf.sh,
https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/16104)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An option to install a wheel which relies on dynamic linking instead of static linking, allowing both libraries to reference protobuf without causing segfaults and undefined behavior.

I think this could take a few forms:
- We could add the native extension as a an `extra` (e.g. users would `pip install protobuf[cpp]` to get the cpp extension).
- We could ship `libprotobuf.*.{dylib, so, dll}` as `package_data` and explicitly load it at import time with `cdll` which would allow other libraries to also find and load them.
- We could publish another package all together (e.g. `protobufdynamic`)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Tried loading protobuf symbols from `_message.*.so` instead of libprotobuf`- not all symbols were baked in and seems overall risky/unstable
- Tried a similar approach to tensorflow and renaming protobuf itself (e.g. https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/v2.0.0/tensorflow/contrib/makefile/rename_protobuf.sh)

OSX defaults to RTLD_GLOBAL when loading libraries -https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/dlopen.3.html

title: php: Implement JsonSerializable interface
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
PHP

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
I would like to be able to serialize my protobufs with PHP's native [`json_encode`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.json-encode.php). This would make working with protos in a mixed environment significantly easier – consider a case like the below, where an existing endpoint returns data that is serialized to JSON farther up the stack:

```php
return $this->json([
  'some' => 'existing data',
]);
```

Ideally, you could return data from a proto like this:

```php
return $this->json([
  'some' => 'existing data',
  'some_additional_data_from_proto' => $my_proto,
]);
```

However, protos currently `json_encode` to an empty object.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
PHP proto message objects should implement the [`JsonSerializable`](https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.jsonserializable.php) interface.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
For responses that are entirely proto, you can return the result of `serializeToJsonString` directly. As demonstrated above, this breaks down when you are working with existing non-protobuf data. As a workaround, one could `json_decode($proto->serializeToJsonString())` to get a natively serializable object, but that doesn't feel particularly idiomatic.

title: clang with c++2a: 'no_destroy' attribute cannot be applied to types
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: master, first appearing in commit a00125024e9231d76746bd394fef8876f5cc15e2
Language: C++

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
linux (ubuntu 20.10)

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
clang 11.0.0-2 in C++2a standard

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. `CC=clang bazel build --cxxopt='-std=c++2a' //:protobuf`
2. observe `error: 'no_destroy' attribute cannot be applied to types` in basically any generated pb source file (and some non-generated ones)

**What did you expect to see**
No errors, hopefully. It would be nice. It worked up until now.

**What did you see instead?**
Compilation failures. One possible result:
```
src/google/protobuf/duration.pb.cc:32:20: error: 'no_destroy' attribute cannot be applied to types
PROTOBUF_CONSTINIT PROTOBUF_ATTRIBUTE_NO_DESTROY DurationDefaultTypeInternal _Duration_default_instance_;
                   ^
src/google/protobuf/port_def.inc:592:41: note: expanded from macro 'PROTOBUF_ATTRIBUTE_NO_DESTROY'
#define PROTOBUF_ATTRIBUTE_NO_DESTROY [[clang::no_destroy]]
                                        ^
```

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
Nothing that comes to mind. It's unclear what the problem is here exactly, whether this is misbehavior by LLVM or a mistake in the protobuf library; from what I can tell based on [the documentation](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/AttributeReference.html#no-destroy) this *does look* like the right way to use the annotation.

nodes.body: Oh fantastic, since I went to sleep @Yuhanun opened #8296 with the right answer.

title: Language reference mistake in grammar of reserved
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

The grammar for the `reserved` keyword references the `fieldName` construction ([Link](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/proto2-spec#reserved)), which does not allow quotes. It seems like Protobuf uses quotes, as also showcased by the example `reserved "foo", "bar";` in the language reference.


Seems like this has already been reported 2 years ago on the mailing list:
https://groups.google.com/g/protobuf/c/IzIkUMUPkgc/m/IkD0jg6hCwAJ

nodes.body: Seeing now that this is already on the issue tracker here as well, closing.

title: Compilation fails with gcc trunk (futur gcc 11), protobuf 3.15.0 and -std=gnu++20: const_cast is not accepted in a constexpr expression
body:
Hi,

All is in the title: I tried to compile protobuf 3.15.0 with gcc trunk and -std=gnu++20, and it fails with this error:

```
google/protobuf/unittest_lite.pb.cc:155:86: error: 'constinit' variable 'protobuf_unittest::_TestAllTypesLite_default_instance_' does not have a constant initializer
  155 | PROTOBUF_ATTRIBUTE_NO_DESTROY PROTOBUF_CONSTINIT TestAllTypesLiteDefaultTypeInternal _TestAllTypesLite_default_instance_;
      |                                                                                      ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
In file included from ./google/protobuf/unittest_lite.pb.h:25,
                 from google/protobuf/unittest_lite.pb.cc:4:
google/protobuf/unittest_lite.pb.cc:155:86:   in 'constexpr' expansion of 'protobuf_unittest::TestAllTypesLiteDefaultTypeInternal()'
google/protobuf/unittest_lite.pb.cc:149:7:   in 'constexpr' expansion of '((protobuf_unittest::TestAllTypesLiteDefaultTypeInternal*)this)->protobuf_unittest::TestAllTypesLiteDefaultTypeInternal::<anonymous>.protobuf_unittest::TestAllTypesLiteDefaultTypeInternal::<unnamed union>::_instance.protobuf_unittest::TestAllTypesLite::TestAllTypesLite((google::protobuf::internal::ConstantInitialized(), google::protobuf::internal::ConstantInitialized()))'
google/protobuf/unittest_lite.pb.cc:97:5:   in 'constexpr' expansion of '((protobuf_unittest::TestAllTypesLite*)this)->protobuf_unittest::TestAllTypesLite::default_string_.google::protobuf::internal::ArenaStringPtr::ArenaStringPtr(0)'
../../src/google/protobuf/arenastring.h:179:9:   in 'constexpr' expansion of '((google::protobuf::internal::ArenaStringPtr*)this)->google::protobuf::internal::ArenaStringPtr::tagged_ptr_.google::protobuf::internal::TaggedPtr<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char> >::TaggedPtr(default_value)'
../../src/google/protobuf/arenastring.h:95:14: error: conversion of 'const google::protobuf::internal::ExplicitlyConstructed<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char> >*' null pointer to 'google::protobuf::internal::ExplicitlyConstructed<std::__cxx11::basic_string<char> >*' is not a constant expression
   95 |       : ptr_(const_cast<ExplicitlyConstructed<std::string>*>(ptr)) {}
      |              ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```

It seems that const_cast can't be used in a constexpr expression, so the constinit instantiation failed.

Note: one way to avoid reinterpret_cast or other kind of forbidden casts in constexpr expression might be to use some union struct having the multiple types you want to cast things into.

Cheers,
Romain

nodes.body: @Romain-Geissler-1A Thanks for the bug report. I am going to disable our use of constinit for GCC until we can figure out a better solution.
This no longer appears to be an issue as of gcc-12-4218-g57c7ec62ee0.

title: Python runtime MethodDescriptor is missing a CopyToProto() method
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**

Version: master
Language: Python

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**

OS independent

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

Python version

**What did you do?**

Here's an example script showing that the `CopyToProto` method doesn't exist in the Python implementation, and how it might be implemented otherwise. You can comment out the line changing the env var to get it to instead use the CPP runtime, in which case the extra redirection is unnecessary. Run this script in the same directory as generated Route Guide stubs.

```python
import os

os.environ["PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION"] = "python"

from google.protobuf import descriptor_pb2, descriptor_pool

# import for side effect of registering descriptors to the pool
import route_guide_pb2, route_guide_pb2_grpc

pool = descriptor_pool.Default()
method_desc = pool.FindMethodByName("routeguide.RouteGuide.ListFeatures")
method_desc_proto = descriptor_pb2.MethodDescriptorProto()

try:
    method_desc.CopyToProto(method_desc_proto)
    print("Copied the method descriptor to the proto.")
    print(method_desc_proto)
except AttributeError as e:
    print(e)
    service_desc = method_desc.containing_service
    service_desc_proto = descriptor_pb2.ServiceDescriptorProto()
    service_desc.CopyToProto(service_desc_proto)
    method_desc_proto = service_desc_proto.method[method_desc.index]
    print("Got the method descriptor proto from the service proto.")
    print(method_desc_proto)
```

**What did you expect to see**

The CPP runtime does have a `CopyToProto()` method.

**What did you see instead?**

The Python runtime does not have a `MethodDescriptor.CopyToProto()` method, as can be seen here: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/python/google/protobuf/descriptor.py#L869

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**

Overall my project was doing the `MethodDescriptor.CopyToProto()` dance because method descriptors don't have discoverable method cardinality (see https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/4731). 

The code above gives a possible implementation. Unfortunately since the construction of `MethodDescriptor`s (and other descriptors) happens inside generated code files and the method descriptors don't contain the `_serialized_start`/`_serialized_end` attributes, I don't think there's any better way than reaching up to the service descriptors and letting `ServiceDescriptor.CopyToProto()` grab the information from the serialized file descriptor.

title: int64 as JSON number marshal option
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
All supported protobuf languages. This would be in the protobuf JSON marshaling support for each language.

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
The [JSON Mapping](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#json) for `int64`, `fixed64`, `uint64` maps to a JSON string, presumably since per [RFC 8259 §6](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8259#section-6), there's not a guarantee beyond `2^53` that the implementation will treat a number as an integer. [YAML](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2/spec.html) is a strict superset of JSON, but has a specific behavior that it treats JSON strings with numbers in them as strings. Thus, when interpreted by a YAML parser, the output of the protobuf JSON marshaling yields the incorrect type.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The JSON standard does not itself restrict the range or precision of numbers, but allows implementations to set limits. I suggest adding a new [JSON Option](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#json_options) that would "Emit int64 values as integers instead of strings". This could then be used by destined-for-YAML-parser marshalers to have integer type fidelity.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
* Post-processing
  * "manual" coercion of the resulting JSON based on known messages.
  * if we walked the message descriptors to process this dynamically, we'd have reimplemented the various language's marshaling code
* A direct-to-YAML marshaller. This might have some benefits, but with this the above small tweak, we can use YAML's existing support
* An option to emit numbers for `2^53` and below, and strings for above. This muddles the output type and makes it harder on any parser to consume the values intelligently.
* An option to inject [`!!int`](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2/spec.html#id2803828) tags to allow YAML parsers to type-coerce the outcome. This has various issues, not the least of which is that it renders it into invalid JSON.

**Additional context**

Spurred by https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/1280#issuecomment-783861560.

This happens to occur when using Kubernetes' generated protos, e.g., [core.v1](https://github.com/kubernetes/api/blob/master/core/v1/generated.proto), to configure Kubernetes. These types contain `int64`, but if we render it to JSON, we lose the type information, and they get treated incorrectly as strings. The generated protos are created using [`go-to-protobuf`](https://github.com/kubernetes/code-generator/blob/v0.20.4/cmd/go-to-protobuf/protobuf/generator.go#L454) which maps the `int64` types straight across.

nodes.body:
**Additional alternatives considered**

* An option to both _require_ that protobuf `int64` fields fit into `2^53-1,-1*2^53` and to emit them as numbers. This has an unfortunate runtime cliff, since traditional protobuf fillers won't know that they're out of bounds.
* Edits to Kubernetes types to use `Int64String` as described in [`json.Marshal`](https://golang.org/pkg/encoding/json/#Marshal) uniformly and then amend `go-to-protobuf` to balk if it sees bare `int64`. This would bring Kubernetes Go, JSON, and protobuf into agreement, but change the field type of all existing objects, which would break all current use :(.

title: Maximum 32 bit float value fails to round trip.
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 3.14.0
Language: Python

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
MacOS X 10.15.4

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Python 3.8.0

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Encode a message with a float who has the maximum 32 bit float value as defined in `type_checkers._FLOAT_MAX`.
2. Decode that message into a python dictionary using `json_format.MessageToDict`
3. ReEncode the python dictionary into a new protobuf message using `json_format.ParseDict`

**What did you expect to see**
A new protobuf message with the `float_value` set to the maximum float value.

**What did you see instead?**
The library raised an error because the float value was too large.

I created a pull request [not intending to merge] to exemplify the round trip failure over [here](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/8335). If that test were to pass we would know that the issue has been resolved.

The crux of the issue is [this code](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/python/google/protobuf/internal/type_checkers.py#L75).
Python rounds up on this maximum float value. That causes the actual number to be greater than the max float which means it cannot be encoded in four bytes.


[Possibly related to this old issue in C++](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/3615)
**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
N/A

Thanks for the report and the self-contained repro.

This is a result of https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/8184, which should significantly increase performance, but also changes the memory management model.

I want to do more investigation to get a more detailed root cause. But for now I'll share an overview of the new memory management model, in case it gives you the info you need to fix the problem on your end.

- **The old model was:** every message is its own Ruby object, which is collected whenever Ruby GCs it.
- **The new model is:** messages are allocated in C-based arenas, and none of the messages in an arena are freed until the entire arena is GC'd. Any reference to any message in the arena will keep the whole arena alive.

To get a root cause for your issue, we should figure out why the arenas are growing so big. Messages end up in the same arena in a couple of ways:
- If you parse a payload, all of the parsed messages are in one big arena. Keeping even a single reference to any message in the tree will keep the whole tree alive.
- Whenever you assign `msg.foo = msg2`, then `msg` and `msg2`'s arenas are joined, and none of the messages in either arena will be freed until all messages in both arenas are garbage.

You can't "break up" an existing arena, but you can use `Google::Protobuf.deep_copy` to copy messages out of an arena to a new, fresh arena that will contain only that message and its children. (Note: `dup` and `clone` won't work for this: since those are shallow copies, they contain references to the other arena still, so they must keep it alive).

I am hoping that a few well-placed `Google::Protobuf.deep_copy` calls will fix the problem you are experiencing.
For your repro, is it possible to reduce it further so that it is just protobuf operations?

title: s390x protoc artifact on Maven Central uses the wrong classifier
body:
protoc artifacts on Maven Central should be using names agreed upon with the os-detector plugin so that the correct binary can be automatically downloaded when available by the Maven and Gradle protoc plugins. The current classifier "s390x" disagrees with os-detector's "s390_64" so can't be found by the plugins. See https://github.com/google/protobuf-gradle-plugin/issues/472

It's not clear how the current s390x classifier name was chosen. I see https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/7073 explicitly remove the _64 suffix, but there's no background or reasoning provided. I see they were added in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/6558, but I didn't see discussion about the classifier name. I have to assume that people just weren't aware that the names were important and not arbitrary.

CC @salamaniibm, @Hendrik-H, @voidzcy

nodes.body: I could understand if the binaries published as part of the [release on GitHub](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v3.15.2) didn't want to use s390_64, since it is atypical. But the binaries published on Maven Central should use the s390_64 or you should discuss with os-detector about changing it (which is probably a bad idea as it'd break other usages of os-detector).

@salamani I expected the fix to be part of protoc 3.15.6, which was release shortly after the fix for this issue was merged but https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/google/protobuf/protoc/3.15.6/ still shows the wrong name. Which release will pick up the fix?
The fix didn't make it in until after we cut the 3.15.x branch, so the fix will be released with 3.16.0.
thanks, looking forward for that

title: Is there any chance to make protobuf self-describing?
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
Currently protobuf 2&3's binary format for one field is:

| 5bit(or more bit) | 3bit   | n bit |
|-------------------|--------|-------|
| field id          | typeId | value |

And the TypeId could be:

| Type | Meaning          | Used For                                                 |
|------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| 0    | Varint           | int32, int64, uint32, uint64, sint32, sint64, bool, enum |
| 1    | 64-bit           | fixed64, sfixed64, double                                |
| 2    | Length-delimited | string, bytes, embedded messages, packed repeated fields |
| 3    | Start group      | groups (deprecated)                                      |
| 4    | End group        | groups (deprecated)                                      |
| 5    | 32-bit           | fixed32, sfixed32, float                                 |

The meaning of typeId is not unique for type. The disadvantages are:

1. The gateway couldn't parse binary data completely. So the HAProxy ntroduce new instruction [ungrpc](https://cbonte.github.io/haproxy-dconv/2.0/configuration.html#ungrpc).
2. Some troubleshooting tools cannot parse binary data without description. So wireshark need [setting protobuf search paths](https://grpc.io/blog/wireshark/), the Charles Web Proxy needs to [set descriptor_set paths](https://www.charlesproxy.com/documentation/using-charles/protocol-buffers/).
3. Some storage components, such as DB, need to convert when the description changed.

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**

1. let gateway could resolve binary data without description.
2. let troubleshooting tools can parse binary data completely
3. storage components needn't convert when the description changed.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

So I want to replace TypeId with 8bit:

| 5bit(or more bit) | 3bit                    | 8bit   | n bit |
|-------------------|-------------------------|--------|-------|
| field id          | pseudo-typeId(always 7) | typeId | value |

So we have a new chance to redesign typeId, the new typeId could be:

| Type | Meaning          | Used For                    |
|------|------------------|-----------------------------|
| 0    | Varint           | int32, int64, bool, or enum |
| 1    | Varint           | uint32, uint64              |
| 2    | Varint           | sint32, sint64              |
| 3    | 64-bit           | fixed64                     |
| 4    | 64-bit           | sfixed64                    |
| 5    | 64-bit           | double                      |
| 6    | Length-delimited | string                      |
| 7    | Length-delimited | bytes                       |
| 8    | Length-delimited | embedded messages           |
| 9    | Length-delimited | packed repeated fields      |
| 10   | 32-bit           | fixed32                     |
| 11   | 32-bit           | sfixed32                    |
| 12   | 32-bit           | float                       |

At protobuf v4, the pseudo-typeId 0-5, and 7 can be accepted.
At protobuf v5, the pseudo-typeId 7 is only accepted.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I thought to extend 3bit to 4bit or more, but it will break compatibility. So `pseudo-typeId(always 7)` is used.

**Additional context**

nodes.body: Would https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/techniques#self-description work for you?

Any change to the binary format would have to be incredibly beneficial in order to adopt it; I don't think this would meet that bar.  Roy's suggestion, https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/techniques#self-description , is probably the best for now.

Thanks for the report, and I'm sorry this is causing trouble for you.

We'll be monitoring this bug and (any other reports we get about this problem) to get a sense for how many users are affected. We don't want to break users, but given how widely used protobuf is, it's hard to make a change like this that won't break anybody. A fair number of the results of the GitHub search appear to be false positives, so it's difficult to quantify how many users are affected.

Thanks so much for taking a look!  I can empathize with how hard it is to make changes in a project relied on my so many.  That said, I can comment that this will break how we at Lyft use protobuf and require us to do an extremely costly migration, never upgrade past 3.14, or maintain our own fork - none of which are appealing options.  I can see if I can poke around in sourcegraph or another system to find other places in OSS that will be hurt by this.

What's going to happen to the well known types that are already in the `google.protobuf` namespace?

Happy to brainstorm any solutions here, would an alternative namespace like `pb_implementation` or `pb_internal` work for you folks?

Thanks for the extra info about the impact, it's really helpful. To answer your questions:

> What's going to happen to the well known types that are already in the google.protobuf namespace?

Unless the protobuf language itself gets type aliases, it's not possible to change these in a backward-compatible way. So these are currently out of scope.

> Happy to brainstorm any solutions here, would an alternative namespace like pb_implementation or pb_internal work for you folks?

The main goal of this change is that users can refer to `pb::Message` as a new public namespace. It's not about an internal namespace change.

This change is motivated by the fact that the namespace is currently bifurcated: open-source protobuf uses `google::protobuf::Message` while Google internally uses `proto2::Message`. Neither of these is ideal: `google::protobuf::` is too long, while `proto2::` suggests that the namespace is related to `syntax = "proto2"`, while they are actually unrelated.

Several other alternatives we have evaluated have already been deemed infeasible (`pbuf::`, `proto::`, etc).
Thanks so much @dlj-NaN and @haberman!

Hi @georgthegreat, thanks for the feedback. It's true that if our symbols were declared directly in `pb`, then they could coexist with user types declared in that namespace. But it is not a good long-term strategy for us to share a namespace with user types. It opens up the possibility of conflicts between the library and users.

I think we would want to adopt [compatibility guarantees like ABSL](https://abseil.io/about/compatibility), which states:

> **You may not open namespace absl.** You are not allowed to define additional names in namespace absl, nor are you allowed to specialize anything we provide. We expect there may eventually be templates that are valid extension points provided by Abseil — there are not currently. (This is similar to the restriction in the C++ standard — there are very few things you are allowed to do in namespace std.)
>
> **You may not forward declare Abseil APIs.** This is actually a sub-point of “do not depend on the signatures of Abseil APIs” as well as “do not open namespace absl”, but can be surprising. Any refactoring that changes template parameters, default parameters, or namespaces will be a breaking change in the face of forward-declarations.

> But it is not a good long-term strategy for us to share a namespace with user types. 

I agree, but this does not allow to change the status quo: for every possible short namespace there will be some company named accordingly, and this company will be using protobufs enclosed into corresponding namespace. When the code does not belong to [Plethora Brands Company](https://www.pb.company/), [PB Company Limited](https://www.facebook.com/Pb-Company-Ltd-113161650324032/) or [PB Products](https://pbproducts.nl) (none of three looks like an IT company to me), enclosing the code into `package pb` does not makes a lot of sense to me. Backward compatibility matters though.

IMO, the strategy suggested above should be declared and the migration should take place disregarding possible co-existence of a user-defined namespace / package. This should happen is a separate major release (3.16 is a good candidate).

title: SEGV in Ruby when initializing with nil
body:
Per @tmtrademarked on [#8311](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/8311#issuecomment-788329847) (filing here as it is a different bug, needing a different fix):

---

After updating from 3.14.0 to 3.15.3, we started seeing a crash that appears related, even with the fix provided in the above PR. If the Inners field contains nil, you can still get a segfault. (In 3.14.0, this does not happen)

I've modified the repro script here slightly to demonstrate the failure mode:

```
require 'google/protobuf'

Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.build do
  add_file("inner.proto", :syntax => :proto3) do
    add_message "Inner" do
      # Removing either of these fixes the segfault.
      optional :foo, :string, 1
      optional :bar, :string, 2
    end
  end
end

Inner = ::Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup("Inner").msgclass

Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.build do
  add_file("outer.proto", :syntax => :proto3) do
    add_message "Outer" do
      repeated :inners, :message, 1, "Inner"
    end
  end
end

Outer = ::Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup("Outer").msgclass

outer_proto = Outer.new(
  inners: [nil]
)
puts outer_proto
```

With 3.14.0, I get the following output:

```
tom:branch (master *)$ bundle exec ruby --disable-did_you_mean ./repro.rb 
<Outer: inners: [nil]>
```

With 3.15.3, I get a segfault. I don't think that's quite what the intended behavior is, right?

title: Question about subclassing generated Message classes
body:
Hi, I'm an engineer at Valve working on upgrading some of our projects from Protobuf 3.5.1 to 3.15.3, and the one problem I've run into is that generated Message classes are marked as final. We have some code that derives from generate Message classes, and I'm trying to evaluate whether (temporarily) disabling ShouldMarkClassAsFinal for generated Message classes is going to result in any bad behavior, or if it's just going to result in poorer optimization of the resulting classes.

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/9d203953a9950a2f2054b9029490940859ba153f/src/google/protobuf/compiler/cpp/cpp_message.cc#L987

It looks like that came across in a quite large merge, so I don't see any useful commit messages, and the only documentation I've seen regarding it is in v3.12 where it states "Mark generated classes as final; inheriting from protos is strongly discouraged."

I will be evaluating the removal of such sub-classing from our code, but I was wondering if the reasoning for this is documented anywhere? We're proto2 syntax, if that matters and wasn't somehow implied already in my question.


Thanks,
Daniel

nodes.body: I believe the main motivation for the change was that the compiler could generate more optimal code if it knew that generated messages couldn't be subclassed. It should be fine to undo this change in your local fork of protobuf if you just want to upgrade without having to remove message subclassing first.

Thanks Adam, I'm happy with that answer as my preliminary tests with that change haven't caught anything on fire.

Have a good evening!

Hmm, `protobuf.keep_descriptor_pool_after_request=1` may not be functioning as intended if the destructors for global objects (such as `DescriptorPool_destructor`) are running before the [request shutdown function](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/php/ext/google/protobuf/protobuf.c#L185-L188). This feature is not well-tested.

We may want to move that shutdown code into the `DescriptorPool_destructor`: we can test whether this DescriptorPool is the generated pool (`PROTOBUF_G(generated_pool )`) and `protobuf.keep_descriptor_pool_after_request=1` is enabled, and avoid calling `upb_symtab_free()` in that case (we should cache it in `PROTOBUF_G(saved_symtab)` instead).

-->
```
2021/03/02 17:07:24 Failed to read configuration from storage.jsonnet: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Failed to unmarshal configuration: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type map[string]json.RawMessage
```

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
go

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Linux 

**What runtime / compiler are you using**
go

**What did you do?**
When running JSON through the unmarshaler it will always work when formatted correctly. When formating incorrectly you're given a very unhelpful error message.  Something like 

```2021/03/02 17:07:24 Failed to read configuration from storage.jsonnet: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Failed to unmarshal configuration: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type map[string]json.RawMessage```

This makes it very hard to determine why the unmarshaler doesn't work. What would be great is if it would tell you what field was off or anything to help you dig into to issue. I've currently been commenting out JSON in a binary search to figure out the issues which isn't the most efficient way to do it. 

Thank you!

source 'https://rubygems.org'
gem 'google-protobuf', github: 'jamesgecko/protobuf', branch: 'jd/fix-ruby-compile', submodules: true
```

Visiting the location indicated by `bundle info google-protobuf | grep Path` and navigating to the `lib/google/protobuf` directory shows that the following generated protobuf files are missing when the gem is built through `bundler`:

any_pb.rb

duration_pb.rb
empty_pb.rb
field_mask_pb.rb
source_context_pb.rb
struct_pb.rb
timestamp_pb.rb
type_pb.rb
wrappers_pb.rb
```

I'm not very familiar with how building gems works, but it looks like it's skipping some steps in the `Rakefile` when bundler builds the gemspec?
</details>

Edit: Ah, apparently the reason I'm still having trouble building my branch with bundler after these changes is because I've been sourcing the gem directly from git. Bundler wants the gemspec file to be in the root directory of the repo. Because bundler and gem make a lot of assumptions about directory structure, the `google-protobuf` gem would probably have to be moved into a submodule for compilation to work when the gem is sourced directly from a git repo.

nodes.body:
This can be hacked by:

```
sed -i '' -e 's|endian.h|machine/endian.h|g' src/google/protobuf/*.h src/google/protobuf/stubs/*.h src/google/protobuf/io/*.h
```

So it's just wrong include path on FreeBSD. After that hack project builds w/o issues.

Strange FreeBSD seems already supported...
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/87dd07b4367b7676af42105d0d102f4e536c248b/src/google/protobuf/stubs/port.h#L60-L66

FYI in google/or-tools we are using (and we test using github macos runner (ed provide virtualbox support), and a Vagrant FreeBSD box)
```cpp
#if (defined(__APPLE__) || defined(__FreeBSD__)) && defined(__GNUC__)
#include <machine/endian.h>
#elif !defined(_MSC_VER)
#include <endian.h>
#endif
```

```C
#ifdef __APPLE__ || defined(__FreeBSD__)

title: How to reuse the same fields in two message?
PHP float broken after use of pack function
body:
We updated or PHP application to use version 3.15.5 today and found that some of our tests are failing because float values are not what we expected. We traced it to the change from https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/8187, before the change everything was fine.

We think that the use of `unpack("f", pack("f", $var))[1]` is problematic because it breaks with even very simple numbers... at least in our environment (debian:buster-slim with php7.3). According to the php manual the pack/unpack functions are machine dependent.

```
var_dump(unpack("f", pack("f", 2.34)));
```
```
array(1) {
  [1]=>
  float(2.3399999141693115)
}
```

Any ideas?

nodes.body: I am not very familiar with this issue but my understanding was that #8187 corrected a case where we were being more precise than we were supposed to be, so if you're seeing a loss of precision then that could be an expected consequence of the fix.

This is working as intended. `float` fields in protobuf are represented as IEEE 754 single precision numbers. This means they have less precision than PHP floats, [which are generally IEEE 754 double precision numbers](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.types.float.php). So when you convert:

`PHP float` -> `protobuf float` -> `PHP float`

you lose precision.

Previously the protobuf PHP library was not properly clamping the precision. This made it inconsistent with the PECL C extension and inconsistent with other languages. Also the precision loss would happen anyway when serializing to binary format.

If this isn't the behavior you want, the best option is to switch your field from `float` to `double`. Unfortunately this is not a wire-compatible change.
Thank you, we will switch to `double`.

title: Range based for loop does not work as expected for repeated enum fields in c++
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 3.11.4
Language: C++

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
ubuntu 20.04.1 LTS
**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
gcc 9.3.0

**What did you do?**
consider a simple protobuf file with two messages 
```
enum AnimalEnum {
    CAT = 0;
    DOG = 1;
}
message A {
    repeated AnimalEnum animals = 1;
}

message AnimalInfo {
    string name = 1;
}

message B {
    repeated AnimalInfo animal_infos = 1;
}
```
Message A contains a repeated enum field. Per tutorial, https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/cpptutorial 
I can iterate over `repeated AnimalEnum` field as expected in the following snippet

```
void PrintAnimal(AnimalEnum animal){
    printf("%s\n", AnimalEnum_Name(animal).c_str());
}
int main(){
    A a;
    a.add_animals(AnimalEnum::CAT);
    a.add_animals(AnimalEnum::DOG);
    for (int i = 0; i < a.animals_size(); i++){
        PrintAnimal(a.animals(i));
    }
    return 0;
}
```
If I try a range based loop, I get a compiler error
```
void PrintAnimal(AnimalEnum animal){
    printf("%s\n", AnimalEnum_Name(animal).c_str());
}
int main(){
    A a;
    a.add_animals(AnimalEnum::CAT);
    a.add_animals(AnimalEnum::DOG);
    for (auto& animal : a.animals()){
        //animal type is const int&!
        //error: invalid conversion from ‘int’ to ‘AnimalEnum’ [-fpermissive]
        PrintAnimal(animal);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

Range based loop works for a repeated non enum field
```
void PrintAnimalInfo(const AnimalInfo& info){
    printf("%s\n", info.name().c_str());
}
int main(){
    B b;
    for (auto name : {"Luna", "Max"}){
        AnimalInfo animalInfo;
        animalInfo.set_name(name);
        b.add_animal_infos()->CopyFrom(animalInfo);
    }

    for (auto& info : b.animal_infos()){
        PrintAnimalInfo(info);
    }
    return 1;
}
```

In the autogenerated protobuf code, `class RepeatedField` is used to represent repeated enums.
Should repeated enums be represented with `RepeatedPtrField` instead?
one could certainly do something like this to fix the compiler error
```
    for (auto& animal : a.animals()){
        //animal type is const int&! 
        PrintAnimal(static_cast<AnimalEnum>(animal));  //"fixed" with casting
    }
```

nodes.body:
Sorry for the long response.

Unfortunately this is intended behavior as documented [here](https://engdoc.corp.google.com/eng/doc/devguide/proto/reference/cpp-generated.md?cl=head#repeated_enum). For repeated enum fields `.animals()` returns `RepeatedField<int>&`. This is mainly due to how repeated enums are stored. Implementing it like this would cause us to not be backwards compatible and change the efficiency, so it will not be reimplemented.

I think the alternatives you offered are the best way to work around this.

body:

Version: 3.14.0

Mac/Linux

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Apple clang version 12.0.0 (clang-1200.0.32.29)

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. proto file:
```
syntax = "proto3";

message Foo {
  uint32 code = 1;
}
```

`protoc --cpp_out=. foo.proto`

2. Compile c++ code:
```
#include "foo.pb.h"

int main() {
  Foo foo;
  foo.set_code(0);
  foo.PrintDebugString();

  foo.set_code(1);
  foo.PrintDebugString();
  return 0;
}

```
Build with `clang++ -std=c++11 -o foo foo.cc foo.pb.cc -lprotobuf`.


**What did you expect to see**
```
code: 0
code: 1
```

**What did you see instead?**
```
code: 1
```

I think `Foo.code` = 0 is legal, `DebugString` should contain `code: 0`.

nodes.body:
Singular proto3 fields do not distinguish between `0` and unset. If you change your field to `optional uint32 code = 1`, you will get your expected behavior.

For more info see: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/docs/field_presence.md

title: Failing to link against static library on Windows (unresolved external symbols)
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v3.12.3
Language: C++

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Windows 10

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
VS 2019, cmake 3.19

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Checkout v3.12.3
2. Build & install protobuf with cmake and VS2019:

      -G "Visual Studio 16 2019" -A x64 -T host=x64
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/path/to/protobuf/install
      -Dprotobuf_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF
      -Dprotobuf_BUILD_TESTS=OFF
      -Dprotobuf_MSVC_STATIC_RUNTIME=OFF
      -Dprotobuf_WITH_ZLIB=OFF

3. Checkout head of onnx-mlir (which uses protobuf on Windows)
4. Use cmake with VS2019 to build onnx-mlir:
      -G "Visual Studio 16 2019" -A x64 -T host=x64
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
      -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/protobuf/install

**What did you expect to see**
Green build

**What did you see instead?**
Multiple linker errors:
LNK2001: unresolved external symbol "__declspec(dllimport) ..."
LNK2019: unresolved external symbol "__declspec(dllimport) ..."

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
I actually figured out what the problem is, but I would like to have it documented for posterity, and, ideally, this would be added to an FAQ somewhere.

My issue was that the recent versions of cmake try to be particularly helpful when finding the protobuf library. Specifically, when find_package is called on protobuf, it silently creates and sets a number of variables to the "most likely" scenarios. In this case:

```
          if (MSVC AND NOT Protobuf_USE_STATIC_LIBS)
            set_property(TARGET protobuf::libprotobuf APPEND PROPERTY
              INTERFACE_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS "PROTOBUF_USE_DLLS"
            )
```

Since onnx-mlir does not set Protobuf_USE_STATIC_LIBS and I did not do so in the call to cmake for onnx-mlir, this resulted in PROTOBUF_USE_DLLS being defined in onnx-mlir and the unresolved external symbols. Passing -DProtobuf_USE_STATIC_LIBS=ON to the cmake command for onnx-mlir resolves the issue.

nodes.body: Protobuf_USE_STATIC_LIBS is cmake specific. It doesn't exist in this repo.  It is only for cmake's FindProtobuf module. But I believe that module is not maintained by the developers of this repo.

title: Support optional map values in explicit presence
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
proto2 and proto3

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
I need to batch update some configuration value for a list of items, this value may have values in range -10…10 (including zero) but also it may be disabled.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
`map<string, optional int32> value = 1`

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- `map<string, MaybeInt32> value = 1` where MaybeInt32 is similar to google.protobuf.Int32Value (or contains extra `bool set` field for clarity) but a different message to work around https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/issues/669 - it works, but it's ugly and less convenient to use than native "pointer to int32" type generated for `optional` in many languages
- rewrite map as repeated message with key and (optional) value fields - the downside is it's became unclear from protocol that key must be unique
- using value outside of allowed range to signal "disabled" - I believe downsides of such a "special" values are clear to anyone

**Additional context**
At a glance, adding `optional` support for map values feels natural, compatible with existing wire and proto formats and should make proto2/3 `optional` support more complete.

@haberman I'm picking this up where @heyZeus left off. Using a whole bunch of logging I've narrowed down where the data is getting corrupted, but I'm still not able to create a repro. I'm hoping with this information it will be enough to get us further. The problem seems to happen when lists of protos are concatenated. Let me explain with a high-level overview of our code.

The client code does 3 or 4 lookups to the document server, concatenates all the results, then creates wrapper objects for each document -- which is the point at which the Base64 decode and JSON parse happens. High level it looks kind of like this:

```
documents = fetch_some_docs + fetch_some_more + fetch_a_third_type
if some_condition
  documents += fetch_a_fourth_type
end
documents.map { |d| create_wrapper(d, other_superfluous_data) }
```

Each of the `fetch` methods calls the documents service with different parameters and returns `message.documents` (the return proto of the service has a `repeated Document documents` field). By inserting logging inside each of the fetch methods and right before `documents.map` I can tell that the `json_metadata` field is valid up until just after the concatenation. Also, it is always the first document in the final list that is corrupted.

To lend further credence, if I change the logic slightly to the below, the problem disappears:

```
documents = []
documents += fetch_some_docs.map { |d| create_wrapper(d, other_superfluous_data) }
documents += fetch_some_more.map { |d| create_wrapper(d, other_superfluous_data) }
documents += fetch_a_third_type.map { |d| create_wrapper(d, other_superfluous_data) }
if some_condition
  documents += fetch_a_fourth_type.map { |d| create_wrapper(d, other_superfluous_data) }
end
documents
```

It so happens that for the particular repro case I'm working with, the first and third fetches return no documents, and `some_condition` is false, so in theory it should be equivalent to do something like `[] + fetch_some_more + []`. However, I'm not able to repro it so far with this:

```
docs = fetch_some_more
2000.times do
  a = [] + docs + []
  a.each { |proto| JSON.parse(Base64.decode64(proto.json_metadata)) }
end
```

Shortly after writing the above, I remembered that in Ruby repeated fields aren't actually arrays, they're `RepeatedField`. So I wondered if converting to a real array before concatenating would also solve the problem, and sure enough it does. I changed each of the `fetch` methods, which used to return `message.documents`, to instead return `message.documents.to_a` and the problem disappears again. Sadly, doing the reverse translation in my attempt to repro didn't work. This still does not reproduce the error:

```
docs = fetch_some_docs
2000.times do
  a = Google::Protobuf::RepeatedField.new(:message, DocumengManagement::Document, []) + docs + Google::Protobuf::RepeatedField.new(:message, DocumengManagement::Document, [])
  a.each { |proto| JSON.parse(Base64.decode64(proto.json_metadata)) }
end
```

I'm trying to verify the patch, and having a devil of a time getting it working. I've tried compiling from source and using a `path:` option in my Gemfile, and then tried `gem 'google-protobuf', github: 'protocolbuffers/protobuf', branch: '3.18.x'` after seeing that your patch is merged, and nothing's working right. I'm either getting `cannot load such file -- google/protobuf/descriptor_pb` or `.../ruby/lib/google/protobuf/descriptor_pb.rb:6:in '<main>': undefined method 'build' for #<Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool:0x00007fccaec2c220> (NoMethodError)`. I'm not sure what to do about that. Is there a released version I can use instead?

Sorry about that. The fix is released in 3.18.0, just released: https://rubygems.org/gems/google-protobuf/versions/3.18.0-x86_64-linux

Want to give it a try and see if it fixes your problem?
I'm a few thousand iterations into a loop of 20k, with no issues so far. It's always failed in the first few hundred before, so I'd say that it's fixed. Thank you!
Excellent, thanks for your patience and for creating a helpful repro.

title: Ruby version `Timestamp.from_time` feels like there should be a class method
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
Generated Ruby code

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
Working with timestamps is somewhat awkward. To create a protobuf timestamp from Ruby time objects, you have to do the following:
```
ts = Google::Protobuf::Timestamp.new
ts.from_time(Time.now) # returns the nanos rather than the Timestamp itself.
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It seems like it would be easier if the Timestamp class just defined a class method as well as an instance method. Something like:
```
def self.from_time(time)
  return if time.nil?
  new(seconds: time.seconds, nanos: time.nsec)
end
```

This would allow developers to create timestamp objects in a slightly more natural syntax:
```
ts = Google::Protobuf::Timestamp.from_time(Time.now)
```

nodes.body: This functionality was added in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/8562, so newer forms of protobuf should have it!

      optional :type, :enum, 1, "Foo.Type"
    end
    add_enum "Foo.Type" do
      value :TYPE_FOO_ZERO, 0
      value :TYPE_FOO_ONE, 1
    end
    add_message "Bar" do
      optional :type, :enum, 1, "Bar.Type"
    end
    add_enum "Bar.Type" do
      value :TYPE_BAR_ZERO, 0
      value :TYPE_BAR_ONE, 1
    end
  end
end

Foo = ::Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup("Foo").msgclass
Bar = ::Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup("Bar").msgclass

foo = Foo.new(type: :TYPE_FOO_ONE)
p foo

bar = Bar.new(type: :TYPE_BAR_ONE)
p bar

p foo == bar
```

**What did you expect to see**

```
<Foo: type: :TYPE_FOO_ONE>
<Bar: type: :TYPE_BAR_ONE>
false
```

**What did you see instead?**

```

<Bar: type: :TYPE_BAR_ONE>
true
```

I assume the new behavior is due to the fact that the two messages have the same Proto serialization (`"\b\x01"` in both cases), but I think the previous behavior was more correct. Generally, comparing two instances of different classes should return false. Even ignoring that, the inner enum types are different. Just because the numerical values happen to be the same does not mean the messages are equal.

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
N/A

title: Spec for options in protobuf language syntax is incomplete
body:
I'm not sure where this documentation is hosted, but the following specifications for the protobuf language:

https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/proto2-spec
https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/proto3-spec

Are incomplete, they say nothing about the syntax of message literals when used in options. For example, this example from the developer guide for options:

```protobuf
optional int32 b = 2 [(foo_options) = { opt1: 123 opt2: "baz" }];
```

Is, according to the specs referenced above, not valid protobuf syntax, which specifies options as:

```
option = "option" optionName  "=" constant ";"
optionName = ( ident | "(" fullIdent ")" ) { "." ident }
constant = fullIdent | ( [ "-" | "+" ] intLit ) | ( [ "-" | "+" ] floatLit ) | strLit | boolLit 
```

This matters because right now I've encountered a problem in the JavaScript protocol buffers support where it differs in its opinion of what is valid syntax for message literals in options from protoc, but where does the bug lie? In protoc, or in the JavaScript protobuf parser? And even if we establish which one the bug lies in, what is the correct behavior? Without a spec that specifies what the correct syntax is, neither has a bug, and there's no way to resolve it because there's no correct behavior defined.

nodes.body:
fwiw, I asked the same thing [on SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66766406/where-is-the-canonical-specification-for-proto3-that-allows-javascript-like-obje/66785006#66785006) and [in the Protocol Buffers group](https://groups.google.com/g/protobuf/c/uM5Z-wobd3g)

I don't know how "official" the answer that was posted on Groups is, but it said essentially: the [source code](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/master/src/google/protobuf/text_format.cc) is the spec :-/

You might have a look at the [pull request](https://github.com/protobufjs/protobuf.js/pull/1571) I submitted to protobufjs to accept optional semicolons along with the optional commas.  If you need optional colons too, you might add a second argument of `true` to the line that reads `skip(":");` in parseOptionValue() of parse.js.  I held off making that change because a) I didn't need it, and b) they seem to be optional only in certain circumstances based on what I saw in text_format.cc and protobufjs seems to have a more simplistic approach to parsing.  [disclaimer: my analysis was hardly exhaustive]
See also: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/6188

The original question refers to "Options [that] can be used in proto files, messages, enums and services."

Options for fields, however, are different. That syntax is here: https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/proto2-spec#normal_field

Message-typed custom option extensions are not actually included in that specification, but are covered in the language guide: https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto#customoptions

(Basically, message-typed custom option extensions are specified in TextFormat syntax.)

> (Basically, message-typed custom option extensions are specified in TextFormat syntax.)

For future readers, "TextFormat syntax" is referring to protobuf's `TextFormat`: https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/cpp/google.protobuf.text_format#TextFormat

From the stack trace, I wonder: do you have a `__destruct()` method that is creating a protobuf message?

title: PHP Segmentation Fault by calling serializeToJsonString()
body: **What version of protobuf and what language are you using?** Version: v3.15.7 (and earlier) Language: PHP **What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?** Ubuntu 20.04.2 LTS or Debian GNU/Linux 10 (buster) **What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)** PHP 7.3.27 **What did you do?** Steps to reproduce the behavior: Write the following to _Example.proto_: ``` syntax = "proto3"; package MyNamespace; message TestCaseMessage { SubMessage subMessage = 1; } message SubMessage { string something = 1; } ``` Compile with protoc: `protoc --proto_path="$SRC" --php_out="$DESTINATION" Example.proto` auto generated PHP File: ``` MyNamespace.TestCaseMessage */ class TestCaseMessage extends \Google\Protobuf\Internal\Message { /** * Generated from protobuf field .MyNamespace.SubMessage subMessage = 1; */ protected $subMessage = null; /** * Constructor. * * @param array $data { * Optional. Data for populating the Message object. * * @type \MyNamespace\SubMessage $subMessage * } */ public function __construct($data = NULL) { \GPBMetadata\Example::initOnce(); parent::__construct($data); } /** * Generated from protobuf field .MyNamespace.SubMessage subMessage = 1; * @return \MyNamespace\SubMessage|null */ public function getSubMessage() { return isset($this->subMessage) ? $this->subMessage : null; } public function hasSubMessage() { return isset($this->subMessage); } public function clearSubMessage() { unset($this->subMessage); } /** * Generated from protobuf field .MyNamespace.SubMessage subMessage = 1; * @param \MyNamespace\SubMessage $var * @return $this */ public function setSubMessage($var) { GPBUtil::checkMessage($var, \MyNamespace\SubMessage::class); $this->subMessage = $var; return $this; } } ``` Write some _test.php_: ``` $message = new \MyNamespace\TestCaseMessage(); $message->setSubMessage(null); $message->serializeToJsonString(); ``` **What did you expect to see** I expected a serialized json string by calling _serializeToJsonString()_ **What did you see instead?** _setSubMessage()_ allow null as value like its initial value, but we get a Segmentation Fault: `WARNING: [pool www] child 77 exited on signal 11 (SIGSEGV) after xxx seconds from start` **Anything else we should know about your project / environment** The reason for setting _null_ ist that we get this value from other objects which are generated dynamically (and sometimes they are _null_). But we don't want to check on every called setter if the given value is _null_. If you set explicitly null on native data types you get a real exception which you can handle. If you call _serializeToString()_ instead of _serializeToJsonString()_, everything is as expected: ``` $message = new \TravelRpc\Message\Hotel\TestCaseMessage(); $message->setSubMessage(null); $message->serializeToString(); ```

I found the problem:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/a00125024e9231d76746bd394fef8876f5cc15e2/src/google/protobuf/arena.cc#L424

The problem is that the `AllocationPolicy` struct has a couple pointers, so the size is different on 32 bit and 64 bit platforms. Since the size of the struct is subtracted the reported SpaceUsed gets higher on 32 bit platforms.

I think the test is broken in this case because it checks against a fixed size, regardless of platform.
seems like we should be able to use `sizeof(void*)` or similar.  Do you mind taking a crack at it?

The align8 thingy was introduced in 885b612f74, but there are no explanation in commit message why it needs to be aligned that way.

The sizeof(AllocPolicy) thingy - which likely broke it - seems to be introduced in commit 5c028d6cf4, without any good explanation in commit message.

I'm giving up. I'll let people who know this code deal with it.

title: Ruby `.decode_json` behavior change for oneof fields in 3.15.0
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v3.15.0
Language: Ruby

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
macOS Catalina 10.15.7

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
ruby 2.7.2p137 (2020-10-01 revision 5445e04352) [x86_64-darwin19]

**What did you do?**
Run the following Ruby script:
```ruby
require "google/protobuf"
require "json"

Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.build do
  add_file("foo.proto", :syntax => :proto3) do
    add_message "Foo" do
      oneof :details do
        optional :bar, :string, 1
        optional :baz, :string, 2
      end
    end
  end
end

Foo = ::Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup("Foo").msgclass

p Foo.new(bar: 'hello')
p Foo.new(bar: 'hello', baz: nil)
p Foo.decode_json({bar: 'hello'}.to_json)
p Foo.decode_json({bar: 'hello', baz: nil}.to_json)
```

**What did you expect to see**
With google-protobuf 3.14.0, the script returns:
```
<Foo: bar: "hello", baz: "">
<Foo: bar: "hello", baz: "">
<Foo: bar: "hello", baz: "">
<Foo: bar: "hello", baz: "">
```

**What did you see instead?**
With google-protobuf 3.15.0, the script returns:
```
<Foo: bar: "hello">
<Foo: bar: "hello">
<Foo: bar: "hello">
Traceback (most recent call last):
	1: from test.rb:20:in `<main>'
test.rb:20:in `decode_json': Error occurred during parsing: Error parsing JSON @1:21: More than one field for this oneof. (Google::Protobuf::ParseError)
```

The new behavior is arguably more correct, but it is sort of a breaking change :/

@haberman Curious to hear what you think about this. It seems like `.decode_json` now distinguishes between "absent" and "present but nil" for oneof fields, and raises an exception in the latter case.

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
N/A

nodes.body:
Hi @ob-stripe,

Sorry for the trouble. 3.15 did indeed move onto a new JSON parser that is more spec compliant than the parser used previously.

This is an interesting case. The spec and our conformance tests do clearly say that we must reject JSON if multiple oneof fields are set, see: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/0ef575beff5a627a4a1e8e15e462039d3aed2ad3/conformance/binary_json_conformance_suite.cc#L2329-L2331

However it's less clear whether this applies if one of the fields is `null`. In protobuf JSON `null` doesn't clear the field, it just means "default." So this is a grey area that the spec doesn't specifically cover.

Let me write a quick test to see what the other languages do for this case. We try to make sure that every language accepts/rejects the same things. If other languages accept this, we should definitely make Ruby accept it also. If other languages are rejecting it, it would be harder to change, since we would need to change all languages accordingly.
Makes sense! Thanks for looking into it.
@haberman Sorry for the ping, but have you had a chance to compare the behavior with other languages?
Hi @ob-stripe, sorry for the delay. I was able to try this and Java and C++ both allow this. So I think we should allow it in Ruby too.

Hi @haberman, no worries and thanks for looking into this! Is there anything I can do to help fixing this? I took a peek at the C extension code that throws the error: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/069f989b483e63005f87ab309de130677718bbec/ruby/ext/google/protobuf_c/ruby-upb.c#L7649-L7652
and I wonder simply moving the null check below: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/069f989b483e63005f87ab309de130677718bbec/ruby/ext/google/protobuf_c/ruby-upb.c#L7654-L7658
so that it happens before would be enough to fix the issue.
@ob-stripe, yes indeed, that code comes from here so I submitted a PR there first: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/pull/387
Wonderful! Thanks for the quick fix. We're eager to update to 3.15 :)
@haberman Sorry to bother you again, but do you have a timeline for releasing this fix?

@ob-stripe Sorry for the delay, I have been prioritizing the PHP memory leak in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/8525

This will release somewhere in the 3.17 series, I expect within the next two weeks or so.
Thanks for the update!

### What did you do?
Protoc: The `--grpc_out` module for php is not looking at path

### Steps to reproduce the issue

**Works:**
```
protoc -I=protofiles/ \
x.proto \
--php_out=generated \
--plugin=protoc-gen-grpc=grpc_php_plugin \
```

**Doesn't work**
When adding `--grpc_out` the code fails
```
protoc -I=protofiles/ \
x.proto \
--php_out=generated/ \
--grpc_out=generated// \
--plugin=protoc-gen-grpc=grpc_php_plugin \
```
Error:
```
grpc_php_plugin: program not found or is not executable
Please specify a program using absolute path or make sure the program is available in your PATH system variable
--grpc_out: protoc-gen-grpc: Plugin failed with status code 1.
```

**Workaround**
Specify full path
```
protoc -I=protofiles/ \
x.proto \
--php_out=generated/ \
--grpc_out=generated// \
--plugin=protoc-gen-grpc=`which grpc_php_plugin` \
```

nodes.body:
> check that MergeFrom copies if nonzero/nondefault only.

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/ee04809540c098718121e092107fbc0abc231725/src/google/protobuf/no_field_presence_test.cc#L463

> If you set a oneof field to the default value (such as setting an int32 oneof field to 0), the "case" of that oneof field will be set, and the value will be serialized on the wire.

https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#oneof_features

My new theory is that the test is failing because when merging messages which contain a Oneof, we must check for default values in the Oneof, because Oneof default values are serialized to the wire.

So if we have an old message with a Oneof field set to default, and then we merge a new message with the Oneof field set to default but with a different case, then the resulting merged message should get the new case, right? Is that how it's supposed to work? Or do we keep the case of the old message?

I'm not familiar with that particular conformance test, but to answer your last question, the merged question should get the new case. With merging or concatenating messages, later appearances generally supersede earlier ones.

What if we have an old message with a Oneof field set to non-default, and then we merge a new message with the Oneof field set to default value and with a different case?

Then the resulting message should have the case and default value of the new message, right?

Right, the resulting message should take one the case and value of the new message. (By the way, I could be missing something but I don't think it really matters whether the field in a oneof is set to its default value or not. The notion of _which_ field within the oneof is currently set is significant, but as far as merging goes there is nothing special about the default value.)

I think these are the tests which are failing.

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/0ef575beff5a627a4a1e8e15e462039d3aed2ad3/conformance/binary_json_conformance_suite.cc#L1228-L1231

Ok I solved it. I was neglecting to merge optional Oneof nested message fields, exactly as the conformance test was reporting. Also I made this thing http://jamesdbrock.github.io/protobuf-decoder-explainer/

We ran into the same problem.
If I try to compile libprotobuf into a dll, and compile the protoc executable that uses this dll with clang-cl, then I get an error like this from `plugin.pb.cc`:
```
error: variable does not have a constant initializer
PROTOBUF_ATTRIBUTE_NO_DESTROY PROTOBUF_CONSTINIT VersionDefaultTypeInternal _Version_default_instance_;
```

I tried using protobuf 3.15.2 and 3.17.1

It seems to be an interaction between `__declspec(dllimport)` and constant initialization.
I can't test with clang-cl, so my tests below are with MSVC.

If I write:
```
__declspec(dllimport) extern int x;
auto& p = x;
```
then `p` is dynamically initialized (at least in the latest MSVC)
If the symbol is not `dllimport`, then `p` is constant initialized as expected.

I think what's happening is that clang is following this behavior but since it also supports the `[[clang::require_constant_initialization]]` attribute it is failing there because it is indeed not constant initialized.

We might want to disable the attribute in clang-for-windows.
The attribute is not required for correctness. It is there mostly to make sure we really are constant initialized in the platforms that support it for code size efficiency.

I also checked that if I compile with clang in C++20 mode, then `constinit` is used, and the same error still appears.
I did not check what happens with MSVC, but if C++20 is enabled (using `/std:c++latest`) and `constinit` is used then I think it wouldn't compile either. (clang seems to be right, this is not supposed to work as constantly initialized on Windows)

I don't know about that.

This works fine:
```
__declspec(dllimport) extern int x;
constexpr auto& p = x;
```

So it can do constant initialization for it, but it just chooses not to when `constexpr` is not there.
tbh, I don't know enough about the semantics of `dllexport`/`dllimport`.

I can confirm this issue with clang 12 on Windows.
>  manualy remove PROTOBUF_CONSTINIT from pb.cc, it compiles fine.

This fixes the problem for me

> We might want to disable the attribute in clang-for-windows.

That was my solution. I changed line 571 of port_def.inc to:
