title: Python protobuf should refuse to serialize Infinity and NaN
body:
Since it doesn't roundtrip, we should refuse to serialize them, per [docs](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/google.protobuf#google.protobuf.Value):
> Note that attempting to serialize NaN or Infinity results in error. (We can't serialize these as string "NaN" or "Infinity" values like we do for regular fields, because they would parse as string_value, not number_value).

Trying with protobuf 4.21.11:
```python
import math

from google.protobuf import json_format, struct_pb2

inf_val = struct_pb2.Value(number_value=math.inf)
inf_json = json_format.MessageToJson(inf_val)
inf_val_roundtrip = json_format.Parse(inf_json, struct_pb2.Value())

print(inf_val)
print(inf_val_roundtrip)
```
outputs
```
number_value: inf
string_value: "Infinity"
```

See also https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/1182

title: Can we add additional service methods (e.g. Publish / Subscribe) to the Protobuf IDL?
body:
Hi,
If I understand the protobuf docs right, by today a protobuf service only supports the method rpc. However a lot of microservices these days are also using publish/subscribe mecanisms for async communication where protobuf is used for serialization / deserialization.

Is there an easy way to add additional methods like publish and subscribe to a Service definition in the protobuf IDL?

I was thinking about something like:

[omitting the message definitions]

service Greeter {
   rpc SayHello (HelloReq) returns (HelloResp); // as already implemented
   pub Announce (Announcement); // publish -> async fire & forget; does not return anything 
   sub Listen (Annoucement); // subcribe to async Annoucement events
}

I understand that this is probably not doable with HTTP(2), but including the puband sub methods in the IDL would allow us to autogenerate the server/client code through a plugin for the desired PubSub mecanism (e.g. NATS, NSQ...).

Any thoughts & ideas welcome!

title: CMake documentation doesn't work
body: @Tradias I've been trying to follow your CMake documentation [here](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/docs/cmake_protobuf_generate.md) but it falls over because the `generated` directory doesn't exist.  Is there a missing step to create it?  CMake seems to expect it at `/path/to/cmake/build/generated`.

nodes.body:
Yes, it appears that for certain kind of CMake generators it does not automatically create the ouput directory (e.g `NMake Makefiles`). As a workaround you can create the directory yourself, by adding the following somewhere in your CMakeLists:

```cmake
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${PROTO_BINARY_DIR}")
```

Or use a different generator, like [Ninja](https://ninja-build.org/) or "Visual Studio 17 2022".

-------------------------------

A proper solution inside protobuf-generate is unfortunately not so easy. Using the above approach would mean that the directory is not part of "CMake clean" and if it where added to [ADDITIONAL_CLEAN_FILES](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_dir/ADDITIONAL_CLEAN_FILES.html?highlight=clean) then it would not be recreated automatically whenever `proto-objects` are build. And the other approach of adding this to the `add_custom_command` inside `protobuf_generate` 

```cmake
COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E make_directory "${PROTO_BINARY_DIR}"
```

has the issue of introducing race conditions in some generators.
Thanks.  I'll take a look at those options.

title: protobuf workspace is undecided on how to reference utf8_range
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: main
 
**What did you do?**
The protobuf workspace declares utf8_range as a git submodule but also includes it in the WORKSPACE rules via protobuf_deps.bzl as a github_archive.

Since ut8_range is added as workspace, paths to this should always reference the workspace version of `@utf8_range`, but there is at least one reference to the local workspace copy `//third_party/utf8_range` in `pkg/BUILD.bazel`.

Alternatively, the workspace should not use a `github_archive` rule for utf8_range and should instead define a `local_repository` rule.

title: Bazel error: v3.21.12 archive checksum changed
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**

Version: v3.21.12
Language: N/A

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**

Linux 

**What did you do?**

I'm the maintainer of the grpc-gateway. We use MEND Renovate to keep our Bazel protoc dependency up to date. It updated to v3.21.12 in the 13th of December in https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/pull/3068. It seems that since then, the checksum for the archive served on this tag has changed, which is causing errors in our CI jobs (https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/actions/runs/3720083266/jobs/6309341191).

Please advise whether the checksum did indeed change and it is safe to update the stored checksum.

nodes.body:
tldr: Checksum is safe to update, and indeed changed

It seems during our release process, we repushed the 3.21.12 tag to a slightly different commit. The new and old commit should be functionally the same, but potentially at different commits from before/after we updated the CHANGES.txt file with our changelog. This step in our release should now be obsolete, and this should not happen again.

Note, you should probably be using v21.12 (not v3.21.12) which points to the same release commit. The per-language tag is only intended for objective-c and c++ specific releases and may be removed in the future.

title: Java: NoSuchMethodError on JRE 8
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: protobuf-java-3.21.7 (there were no problems with 3.21.1)
Language: Java

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Linux

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Build JDK 9+ and run with JRE 8

**What did you do?**
Build Protobuf with JDK 9+ and run with JRE 8.
Because `CodedOutputStream` uses `ByteBuffer.position(int)` that overrides the method in the superclass `Buffer` from JDK9+,
it produces `NoSuchMethodError` when it's run with JRE 8.
 as follow:
```

title: Request to add entry to extension registry
body:
I would like to add an entry to the extension registry: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/docs/options.md

This is for SAPIENT, a communication protocol standard for autonomous sensor systems.

Here is suggested text for the addition:

1. SAPIENT
   * Website: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/sapient-autonomous-sensor-system
   * Extension: 1181

(suggested text above previously said: ~~Extension: 1179~~)

I'd be happy with any extension number, I just picked 1179 because it appears to be the next one available. We are likely to use multiple option extensions, but as suggested in the docs we will nest them in a message so we will only need one extension number.

I would have preferred to open a pull request to save everyone some hassle, but unfortunately I can't sign the CLA.

nodes.body: The CLA is a strict legal requirement.  We cannot bend on that point.

@fowles  The CLA is a strict legal requirement for pull requests, I understand that. That's why I didn't open a pull request. But I thought it was not a requirement to add a feature in response to an issue, isn't that right?
still waiting on a clarification from legal.  Will likely have to wait till after the holidays

@joldf the CLA covers any contribution to an open source project - not required for creating an issue, but is required for any contributions such as code, documentation, etc. The CLA is the mechanism by which you license the use of your contribution to the project. If you have any other questions or concerns I'd be happy to speak with you more! I'm in the Google Open Source Programs Office. We have some information online about CLAs and the why/how of them that you might find helpful - https://opensource.google/documentation/reference/cla/policy

@thisisnotapril 

Thanks for that explanation April.

I think the confusion here is that I'm not actually trying to submit a contribution. I'm asking for some documentation to be changed but I've only specified the change should contain the technology name (which is the single word "SAPIENT"), a number (I've suggested one but feel free to use another), and a URL. Those three things are not a sufficiently creative work to be copyrightable. In fact, to use a URL you don't even need the permission of the owner let alone a license agreement. A Googler can compose those three things into the actual change, which would be a bullet point in a list (and I don't think even that is creative enough that it is copyrightable).

I can try to arrange for a CLA to be signed if you would still like that. But it would be a pity as it would set a precedent that CLAs should be signed in future even for requests that really do not require it.

Thanks for the clarification @joldf! You're correct, if you're not contributing the documentation change yourself then no need for a CLA. 

@fowles I think we treat this like a feature request, and it's open for whomever to make the change/contribution.
@fowles  Would you be kind enough to make this change? I realise it doesn't impact most customers of protobuf but it would be really helpful for us.

@fowles  Apologies for chasing but would you be able to make this change or find someone that could? I only expect it would take a few moments and would really help us out. If it's not done soon then we might just have to proceed with publication of proto files with the assumption that 1179 is available to us. This could cause confusion if someone else updates that page without noticing this issue.
Sorry for the noise but I've just seen that 1179 an 1180 are already used (they're just not at the end of the file) so it would need to be at least 1181.

Following on from my last comment: it appears others have had the same confusion as me because 1179 and 1180 are both now duplicated allocations (see the [current `options.md`](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/v23.1/docs/options.md)): 1179 is allocated to both ygot (entry 25) and Cybozu (entry 89) while 1180 is allocated to both ygot (entry 25) and Wire use_array (entry 90).
@fowles following up on the previous request to see if this is still something that can be done?

title: `--pyi_out` does not annotate `__slots__`
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**

Language: Python
protobuf 4.21.12
grpcio 1.51.1, grpcio-tools 1.51.1, 
Mypy 0.991

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**

macOS Ventura

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

Python 3.9.16

**What did you do?**

Run `python3 -m grpc_tools.protoc -pyi_out=...`

**What did you expect to see**

A .pyi that validates Mypy type checks.

**What did you see instead?**

A .pyi that has the following error:

    error: Need type annotation for "__slots__"

It seems `__slots__` is the only untyped field in the .pyi.

nodes.body: I think this is a [bug](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/7290) in Mypy (although the bug suggests the issue has been fixed).

@deannagarcia Changing to using a tuple for `__slots__` makes this error go away, which seems reasonable because tuples are immutable. Would you accept a PR that changes all generated `__slots__` to use tuples for the pyi generator?

I was going to ask to reopen because this is still broken, with protoc outputting lists instead of tuples as mentioned by @aiven-anton. But actually, Python's [docs on `__slots__`](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__slots__) do say

> [...] a string, iterable, or sequence of strings [...]

So protoc is not doing anything wrong, lists should be fine and this is just another Mypy bug: https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/10870

Maybe those affected can upvote there?

nodes.body:
This limitation is only on the precompiled binaries. Different platform gems have different ruby requirements:

* [`google-protobuf 3.21.12-x86_64-linux`](https://rubygems.org/gems/google-protobuf/versions/3.21.12-x86_64-linux)  Required Ruby Version: >= 2.5, < 3.2.dev
* [`google-protobuf 3.21.12`](https://rubygems.org/gems/google-protobuf/versions/3.21.12)  Required Ruby Version: >= 2.3 

The version that isn't compiled has no maximum version number so should be able to build. 

That works locally for me, but I'm also deploying with a buildpack and haven't succeeded in telling it to compile rather than fetch the precompiled version.

I have the same problem, I can install [google-protobuf 3.21.12](https://rubygems.org/gems/google-protobuf/versions/3.21.12) just fine, but specifying it as an explicit dependency in my Gemfile doesn't solve the problem because it looks for the precompiled version anyway. Is there a way to override this behavior?

Ah I just solved it. I accidentally ran `bundle install` before running `bundle update` and it installed an old version of Bundler (2.1.4) which has a bug that causes it to not fall back to the source version.

@tinco Have you managed to deploy it ? I have the same error when I try to deploy to github-pages. Even if I specify the gem [google-protobuf 3.21.12](https://rubygems.org/gems/google-protobuf/versions/3.21.12) in the Gemfile nothing seems to change. (I am using Bundler 2.4.1)

Eh also make sure you actually uninstall the old bundler with `gem uninstall bundler` it kept using the old one even after installing the new one.

This happens with every major release and will also require changes to the build process to ([similar to these changes for 3.1.0](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/commit/abdfd093aff2ec5bbc25c303c4206690a862f6c0)) so future releases will include 3.2.0 binaries. It usually takes 2-3 months before google-protobuf gets updated for the new version of Ruby.

We should reopen this issue, as it is not solved.

I have reopened a new issue, following the bug report template.
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/11538

I was experiencing the same problem with Heroku as well. What fixed it for me was running the following command to add the `x86_64-linux` platform to my Gemfile:

```
bundle lock --add-platform x86_64-linux
```

I already had the `ruby` platform so make sure you have that as well so it can fall back to that. If you don't have the ruby platform, add it by running:

```
bundle lock --add-platform ruby
```

title: well_known_types is deprecated and suggests using :descriptor_proto_srcs, which does not exist
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v21.12
Language: Python

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Try to build a thing that depends on `@com_google_proto//:well_known_types` after updating to v21.12
2. Get WARNING message `depends on deprecated target '@com_google_protobuf//:well_known_protos': Prefer :well_known_type_protos instead.`
3. Look in [BUILD.bazel](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/BUILD.bazel#L132-L145) to see that this "Prefer" is an incomplete message, and the full message in the comment says
    ```
    # DEPRECATED: Prefer :well_known_type_protos for the Well-Known Types
    # (https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/google.protobuf)
    # or :descriptor_proto(_srcs) for descriptor.proto (source), or
    # :compiler_plugin_proto for compiler/plugin.proto.
    ```
4. Try using variations of those to no avail.
5. Look in BUILD.bazel again, and see that there is no `:descriptor_proto_srcs` target (I see it in the `main` branch, but not in 21.12)

**What did you expect to see**
Some option that will work in the context where `deps=["@com_google_protobuf//:well_known_types"]` previously worked, without a deprecation warning. With `:descriptor_proto_srcs` the problem is the missing target. With the other three options as deps, there is a lengthy error message that I am not confident doesn't include NDA information so cannot include here. It seems reasonably clear that the issue is not including srcs, since that's the only difference between `deps=[":well_known_types"]` and `deps=[the three that exist]`.

**What did you see instead?**
No combination of the suggested alternatives will build that target.

My current workaround is to simply patch out the `deprecation` tag and continue to use `:well_known_types` for now.

nodes.body: It looks like 21.x went out while our Bazel refactoring was underway, and in 22.x these targets do exist.  Is ignoring the deprecation warning in 21.x a viable solution or should we just remove it in 21.x?

Ignoring it is pretty inconvenient in a large build environment - we get hundreds to thousands of instances of the warning, which could easily make us miss other build issues. (Hence patching it out in our http_archive targets.)
It's not a problem for me at this point because I already made that patch, but I'd say it's probably worth addressing for others if this is a supported branch.
K, I'll update 21.x to give a better deprecation message.  The targets it's *supposed* to be pointing to are `:well_known_type_protos`, `:compiler_plugin_proto`, and `:descriptor_proto`

I think this solution may not actually help if you have Python code that depends on (what is later) `:descriptor_proto_srcs`. I'm pretty sure I looked for any targets that provided the necessary files, and the deprecated target was the only one in this version.

I'm not following.  `:well_known_protos` is a deprecated filegroup containing both the WKT protos, descriptor.proto, and plugin.proto.  We have individual filegroups already that export all of those, so you can just switch to those.  `//:well_known_type_protos`, `//:compiler_plugin_proto`, and `//:descriptor_proto` are all in 21.12, and should give you the access you want.

Nothing in the protobuf repo depends on `:well_known_protos`, so if you're seeing the deprecation message the problem is coming from your code

Right, our code currently depends on `:well_known_protos`.

If we change the code to depend on all three of those other targets, it still doesn't build, because none of those targets include the `:descriptor_proto_srcs` content (that target is available on main but not on 21.12); that content is what (in some targets) `:well_known_protos` is included for.

i.e. the deprecation warning tells us to change our build rules in a way that we cannot, in fact, change the build rules while depending on this version.
`:descriptor_proto_srcs` is just a filegroup exporting `descriptor.proto` in 22.x (i.e. main).  In 21.x you can use `//:descriptor_proto`, which does the same thing...

No, `//:descriptor_proto` is [this proto library](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/src/google/protobuf/BUILD.bazel#L155) in both versions (unless you changed that in addition to changing documentation).
`//:descriptor_proto_srcs` is [this filegroup](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/src/google/protobuf/BUILD.bazel#L465).

They both have srcs="descriptor.proto", but `descriptor_proto_srcs` makes that proto file itself available to its clients, while `descriptor_proto`'s proto_library target makes only the generated code available.
Ah sorry, I missed that this was a `proto_library` rule in 21.x.  Let me update 21.x to properly export this similarly to what we've done on main

This problem has returned again in another new version - it was fixed by what you did, but "well_known_protos" now flags as deprecated and exposes
```
    srcs = [
        ":descriptor_proto_srcs",
        ":well_known_type_protos",
        "//src/google/protobuf/compiler:plugin.proto",
    ],
```

The comment says
```
# DEPRECATED: Prefer :well_known_type_protos for the Well-Known Types
# (https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/google.protobuf)
# or :descriptor_proto(_srcs) for descriptor.proto (source), or
# :compiler_plugin_proto for compiler/plugin.proto.
```

But the target `:compiler_plugin_proto` doesn't exist.

(Also, it would be nice if the `deprecated=` tag said all the same options the comment says, because otherwise when we update this our developers are going to get this warning telling them to switch to only `:well_known_type_protos` which may or may not actually work for their use-case.)
Turns out the issue doesn't reopen with a comment, so I've made a new issue for this "same problem different update".

title: Google.protobuf.BoolValue generates different variable type in auto generated code.
body:
I have a .proto file for my messages in which I have a variable of type **google.protobuf.BoolValue**.

When I compiled it using protoc, I got an autogenerated file(.cs), in which the field is mapped to a variable of type **FieldCodec<bool?>**.

When my colleague did the same, he got an autogenerated file(.cs), in which the field is mapped to a variable of type **Google.Protobuf.WellKnownTypes.BoolValue**.

I see that these two are different types, say one is **BoolValue** and other is **bool?**.

Can anyone please explain me why this difference.

nodes.body: @danyeaw My best guess is that your build is somehow mixing more than one version of the protobuf runtime library. For example, `GOOGLE_ABSL_DCHECK_NE` is defined [here](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/ade256e153ea7bfff85987a7f1bf2e9c9632cb10/src/google/protobuf/stubs/logging.h#L224) in logging.h, but if the compiler is using an old version of that header then that definition won't be there. I think that would explain the other errors as well. Are there maybe some old protobuf headers lying around on your system somewhere?

Thanks @acozzette! I thought I had a clean build before when I was getting those errors, but I just wiped everything and started over, and now everything is building successfully. Thanks for the help, and apologies for opening an issue when one didn't really exist.
No worries, I'm glad you got it sorted out!

title: Setting owner of files in archive to root:root
body:
Hello!

I noticed that even in latest releases of Protobuf 21.12 owner of files in archive set to person who actually did release.

For example for latests release:
```
tar -tvf ~/Downloads/protobuf-all-21.12.tar.gz |head -
drwxr-x--- kfm/primarygroup  0 2022-12-14 14:28 protobuf-21.12/
drwxr-x--- kfm/primarygroup  0 2022-12-14 14:28 protobuf-21.12/conformance/
-rw-r----- kfm/primarygroup 16475 2022-12-14 14:20 protobuf-21.12/conformance/conformance_test.cc
-rw-r----- kfm/primarygroup  6867 2022-12-14 14:20 protobuf-21.12/conformance/binary_json_conformance_suite.h
-rw-r----- kfm/primarygroup  5737 2022-12-14 14:20 protobuf-21.12/conformance/failure_list_ruby.txt
-rw-r----- kfm/primarygroup 12305 2022-12-14 14:20 protobuf-21.12/conformance/conformance_test.h
-rw-r----- kfm/primarygroup    86 2022-12-14 14:20 protobuf-21.12/conformance/failure_list_python-post26.txt
```
For quite old release many years ago owner was another but not root too:
```
tar -tvf ~/Downloads/protobuf-all-3.20.3.tar.gz | head
drwxr-xr-x shaod/primarygroup 0 2022-09-29 22:15 protobuf-3.20.3/
-rw-r--r-- shaod/primarygroup 271 2022-09-29 22:09 protobuf-3.20.3/protobuf.pc.in
-rwxr-xr-x shaod/primarygroup 1210 2022-09-29 22:09 protobuf-3.20.3/autogen.sh
-rwxr-xr-x shaod/primarygroup 49482 2022-09-29 22:10 protobuf-3.20.3/config.guess
-rw-r--r-- shaod/primarygroup  1474 2022-09-29 22:09 protobuf-3.20.3/protobuf_release.bzl
-rw-r--r-- shaod/primarygroup 46371 2022-09-29 22:10 protobuf-3.20.3/aclocal.m4
-rwxr-xr-x shaod/primarygroup  6878 2022-09-29 22:10 protobuf-3.20.3/missing
drwxr-xr-x shaod/primarygroup     0 2022-09-29 22:15 protobuf-3.20.3/editors/
```

It's definitely not a critical issue but it causes errors in environments where tar thinks that it's running as root but it's actually has no root permissions to make owner and it may happen quite often in hardened Docker environments.

In such cases it leads to errors like this one on Ubuntu 22.04
```
tar -xf protobuf-all-3.15.7.tar.gz call failed with code 512 and output: tar: protobuf-3.15.7/examples/add_person.py: Cannot change ownership to uid 231664, gid 89939: Invalid argument
tar: protobuf-3.15.7/examples/WORKSPACE: Cannot change ownership to uid 231664, gid 89939: Invalid argument
tar: protobuf-3.15.7/examples/list_people.dart: Cannot change ownership to uid 231664, gid 89939: Invalid argument
tar: protobuf-3.15.7/examples/add_person.cc: Cannot change ownership to uid 231664, gid 89939: Invalid argument
tar: protobuf-3.15.7/examples/AddPerson.java: Cannot change ownership to uid 231664, gid 89939: Invalid argument
tar: protobuf-3.15.7/examples/list_people.cc: Cannot change ownership to uid 231664, gid 89939: Invalid argument
```

Full reproduce:
```
wget https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/download/v21.12/protobuf-all-21.12.tar.gz
tar -xf protobuf-all-21.12.tar.gz; echo $?
```

It successfully unpacks everything but it fills screen with myriad of error messages / warnings and returns exit code 2 which means failure:
```
2
```

tar version:
```
tar --version
tar (GNU tar) 1.34
```
Example of failing chown:
```
chown 199791:199791 v1.2.3.tar.gz
chown: changing ownership of 'v1.2.3.tar.gz': Invalid argument
```

As workaround to suppress such errors following flag can be used:
```
tar --no-same-owner -xf protobuf-all-21.12.tar.gz; echo $?
```

Would be great to set owner of all files in archive to 0:0 root:root and it can be easily accomplished by using flag --owner=0.

Thank you for attention.

title: Inconsistent version in released zip packages
body:
Hi,
our team noticed that the naming of the generated .tar.gz and .zip files in inconsistent as of v21.x

For v20.3 all bundles were still named as expected:
```
protobuf-all-3.20.3.tar.gz
protobuf-all-3.20.3.zip
protobuf-cpp-3.20.3.tar.gz
protobuf-cpp-3.20.3.zip
protobuf-csharp-3.20.3.tar.gz
protobuf-csharp-3.20.3.zip
protobuf-java-3.20.3.tar.gz
protobuf-java-3.20.3.zip
protobuf-js-3.20.3.tar.gz
protobuf-js-3.20.3.zip
protobuf-objectivec-3.20.3.tar.gz
protobuf-objectivec-3.20.3.zip
protobuf-php-3.20.3.tar.gz
protobuf-php-3.20.3.zip
protobuf-python-3.20.3.tar.gz
protobuf-python-3.20.3.zip
protobuf-ruby-3.20.3.tar.gz
protobuf-ruby-3.20.3.zip
protoc-3.20.3-linux-aarch_64.zip
protoc-3.20.3-linux-ppcle_64.zip
protoc-3.20.3-linux-s390_64.zip
protoc-3.20.3-linux-x86_32.zip
protoc-3.20.3-linux-x86_64.zip
protoc-3.20.3-osx-x86_64.zip
protoc-3.20.3-win32.zip
protoc-3.20.3-win64.zip
```

However with the change to v3.21.7 and ever since this has changed. Since then protobuf-all is named with 21.x and the rest as 3.21.x also notice how python is 4.21.x since then.

Since v21.7 the version is different between languages:
```
protobuf-all-21.7.tar.gz
protobuf-all-21.7.zip
protobuf-cpp-3.21.7.tar.gz
protobuf-cpp-3.21.7.zip
...
protobuf-python-4.21.7.tar.gz
protobuf-python-4.21.7.zip
...
protoc-21.7-linux-aarch_64.zip
protoc-21.7-linux-ppcle_64.zip
protoc-21.7-linux-s390_64.zip
protoc-21.7-linux-x86_32.zip
protoc-21.7-linux-x86_64.zip
protoc-21.7-osx-aarch_64.zip
protoc-21.7-osx-universal_binary.zip
protoc-21.7-osx-x86_64.zip
protoc-21.7-win32.zip
protoc-21.7-win64.zip
```

After adding (for example) the protoc-21.12-win64.zip to path it still returns its version number as 3.21.12 so it seems this is unintentional on your side. Autogenerated Changelogs on your [release page](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases) now also use "Protocol Buffers v21.x" as header text.

This becomes an issue with 3rd party libraries such as @protobuf-ts/protoc which has trouble finding the installer for 3.21.x because of this naming and fails.

nodes.body:
This is an intentional change to our versioning scheme to decouple per-language major versions as announced in https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/news/2022-05-06#versioning.

Releases can now largely be referred to using the minor version (aka v21.x release) which will be the same for all languages though each language will have its own major version (3.21.x, 4.21.x). I believe the major version number for protoc continues to follow the C++ major version.

title: Missing JsonPrintOptions for bytes to debug communication
body:
To print messages as json is a create feature to debug the communication in detail, but to see a big binary blob within a message string is not very help full at this point. 

A big advantage over string based json communication is, that one can very easy embed images or generally binary data.
The full binary blob is self-contained and usually another construction site. Clarity is lost when the entire binary data is printed.  "To debug message with binary data, is more like watching at the header info of a file".

Really helpful would be to print only the size of the binary data.
`{ "name": "text",
   "data": "[212 bytes]" }`

instead of the base64 encoding string:

`{ "name": "text",
   "data": "ChBoYW4udmZuLmxhbjo0NTM5ElJ...." }`

With an extra option `print_simple_size_info_for_bytes` in JsonPrintOptions, the user can change the print behavior for that.
The flag is then only need to handle in JsonObjectWriter::RenderBytes, to support this great feature.

---
Christian

title: Service definition with same name in different packages causes duplicate internal struct definition
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only.
For questions or troubleshooting, please post on the protobuf mailing list:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf 
Stack Overflow is also a useful if unofficial resource https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/protocol-buffers
-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v3.19.4 
Language: C++

**What operating system**
Windows 10

**What runtime / compiler are you using**
gcc 11.2 

**What did you do?**
See also example [PlcNextGrpcTest.zip](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/files/10345315/PlcNextGrpcTest.zip)
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create 2 proto files with same name in different directories. Content is the same or similar. Package is different for different namespaces. At least the service names in both files should be the same. See example: `PlcNextGrpcTest\protos\Sample\world1\helloworld.proto` and `PlcNextGrpcTest\protos\Sample\world2\helloworld.proto`
2. use protobuf and C++ plugin to generate C++ stub code. Please find already generated code at `PlcNextGrpcTest\GrpcSimpleClient\src\GrpcStubs`
3. Compile and link C++ code
4. See error

**What did you expect to see**
Compile should succeed. No naming conflicts

**What did you see instead?**
```
error : CMakeFiles/GrpcSimpleClient.dir/src/GrpcStubs/world2/helloworld.pb.cc.o:(protodesc_cold+0x0): multiple definition of `TableStruct_helloworld_2eproto::offsets'; CMakeFiles/GrpcSimpleClient.dir/src/GrpcStubs/world1/helloworld.pb.cc.o:(protodesc_cold+0x0): first defined here(message from c:/sdks/.../11.2.0/real-ld.exe)
error : CMakeFiles/GrpcSimpleClient.dir/src/GrpcStubs/world2/helloworld.pb.cc.o:C:/m_git/PlcNextGrpcTest/GrpcSimpleClient/src/GrpcStubs/world2/helloworld.pb.cc:87: multiple definition of `descriptor_table_helloworld_2eproto'; CMakeFiles/GrpcSimpleClient.dir/src/GrpcStubs/world1/helloworld.pb.cc.o:C:/.../PlcNextGrpcTest/GrpcSimpleClient/src/GrpcStubs/world1/helloworld.pb.cc:87: first defined here(message from c:/.../11.2.0/real-ld.exe)
```
I wonder if the struct declaration and definition of `TableStruct_helloworld_2eproto` and definition of `descriptor_table_helloworld_2eproto` should be included in a namespace or its name should contain information of the package to make it unique.

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
* Attached example proto files are written as easy as possible. In our implementation we have different services with same name because of their purpose. But the messages inside are different. 
* Since the service names are defined as interface before we cannot simply change the names to make them unambiguously and avoid this problem. 
* Attached VS project uses a specific cross compile toolchain. You can use your gnu compiler instead if you need to compile the code.

nodes.body: I think you might want to file this with https://github.com/grpc/grpc project, as the service definitions are generated using grpc plugins, typically.

We found a solution to let the protobuf compiler generate unique names for the structure definition. The key for the solution is in starting the protobuf compiler not defining the proto_path in that in our real project (not this sample) beside the source *.proto further .proto files exist that include each other.

Generating the stub code by these commands leads to the naming conflict
```
protoc.exe --proto_path=.\world1 --grpc_out=..\..\GrpcSimpleClient\src\GrpcStubs\world1 --plugin=protoc-gen-grpc=grpc_cpp_plugin.exe .\world1\*.proto
protoc.exe --proto_path=.\world1 --cpp_out=..\..\GrpcSimpleClient\src\GrpcStubs\world1 .\world1\*.proto
protoc.exe --proto_path=.\world2 --grpc_out=..\..\GrpcSimpleClient\src\GrpcStubs\world2 --plugin=protoc-gen-grpc=grpc_cpp_plugin.exe .\world2\*.proto
protoc.exe --proto_path=.\world2 --cpp_out=..\..\GrpcSimpleClient\src\GrpcStubs\world2 .\world2\*.proto
```
Generating the stub code by these commands solves above problem
```
protoc.exe  --grpc_out=..\..\GrpcSimpleClient\src\GrpcStubs --plugin=protoc-gen-grpc=grpc_cpp_plugin.exe .\world1\*.proto
protoc.exe  --cpp_out=..\..\GrpcSimpleClient\src\GrpcStubs .\world1\*.proto
protoc.exe  --grpc_out=..\..\GrpcSimpleClient\src\GrpcStubs --plugin=protoc-gen-grpc=grpc_cpp_plugin.exe .\world2\*.proto
protoc.exe  --cpp_out=..\..\GrpcSimpleClient\src\GrpcStubs .\world2\*.proto
```
By the fix the issue is solved for us and can remain closed

It looks like you are using our Automake build. The Automake build is being removed in our upcoming 22.x release, and is unlikely to get any more fixes or changes.

What happens if you try using CMake instead?

Hello!

Thank you so much for prompt reply. I did not know about plan to remove make but I think it's really good idea to replace it by cmake.

I've tried building Protobuf with it and it worked just fine, I've used following steps:
```
wget https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/download/v21.12/protobuf-all-21.12.tar.gz
tar -xf protobuf-all-21.12.tar.gz 
cd protobuf-21.12/
mkdir build
cd build
cmake -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/fastnetmon-community/libraries/gcc1210/bin/gcc -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/fastnetmon-community/libraries/gcc1210/bin/g++ -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/protobuf -Dprotobuf_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON ..

LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/fastnetmon-community/libraries/gcc1210/lib64 make -j 4
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/fastnetmon-community/libraries/gcc1210/lib64 make install
```

it was built without having any gcc or g++ compiler in system.

title: Missing Linux wheels for protobuf==4.21.x for Python 3.8, 3.9, 3.10?
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 4.21.12
Language: Python

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Ubuntu 22.04.1 LTS

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Python 3.9.16 or Python 3.10.6

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a virtualenv: `virtualenv .venv --python 3.10.6` (or similar)
2. Activate virtualenv: `source .venv/bin/activate`
3. Install protobuf==4.21.12: `pip install protobuf==4.21.12 --no-cache-dir`
4. See that it installs `protobuf-4.21.12-cp37-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl`
```
❯ pip install protobuf==4.21.12 --no-cache-dir
Collecting protobuf==4.21.12
  Downloading protobuf-4.21.12-cp37-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl (409 kB)
...
Installing collected packages: protobuf
Successfully installed protobuf-4.21.12
```

**What did you expect to see**

That it would install a version of protobuf that's not tied to CPython 3.7.

**What did you see instead?**

It installs a manylinux wheel of Protobuf tied to CPython 3.7 (protobuf-4.21.12-cp37-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl). This is causing issues for me. Why is there no corresponding manylinux wheel for CPython 3.8, CPython 3.9, CPython 3.10? I see there's a wheel called protobuf-4.21.12-py3-none-any.whl and there are Windows wheels for them, but no such wheels for CPython 3.8, 3.9, 3.10 (See here: https://pypi.org/project/protobuf/4.21.12/#files).

Additionally, if you revert to 3.20.3, you do have wheels for those platforms, like: protobuf-3.20.3-cp310-cp310-manylinux_2_12_x86_64.manylinux2010_x86_64.whl (See here: https://pypi.org/project/protobuf/3.20.3/#files).

nodes.body:
We recently changed the artifacts a bit to use the python limited API which should make that artifact (protobuf-4.21.12-cp37-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl) compatible with any version of python >= 3.7.

Are you seeing any failures when using newer versions of python with that wheel?

@deannagarcia it seems my issue is actually with the upb implementation of the Python packages, in that the python implementation works fine. I'll open a separate issue with that hopefully soon. Thanks for the clarification on why there's no specific wheels for python > 3.7.

> But it should be possible to also build tests, no? :) Os is `CMakeLists.txt` not actively maintained?

We do actively support and maintain `CMakeLists.txt`, but we do not test nor guarantee that it works for _development_ in our repo. For development, we only officially support `bazel`. But for _releases_, we do officially support CMake.

However, if you want to build directly from the repo with cmake, it _should_ work if you specify `cmake -DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=17 ...` (or 14) in your configure step.

Hope that helps, or at least clears up the confusion. Re-open the issue if there's more.

title: Couldn't build proto file into descriptor pool: duplicate file name when using upb python implementation
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 4.21.12
Language: Python

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
python: 3.10
buf: 1.11.0
libprotoc: 3.21.12

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to https://github.com/Atheuz/test-protobuf-schema-error
2. Clone the repo
3. Cd into the repo directory
4. Create a virtualenv: `virtualenv .venv --python=3.10`
5. Activate the virtualenv: `source .venv/bin/activate`
6. Install dependencies: `pip install -r requirements.txt`
7. Run pytest: `pytest`
8. See that when `PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=upb`, `pytest` fails to run.
9. Change `PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=upb` to `PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python` in `pytest.ini`.
10. Run pytest: `pytest`
11. See that when `PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python`, `pytest` runs without issue.
12. Similarly, if you downgrade to `protobuf==3.20.3` and run the test using `PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=cpp` or `PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python`, it also succeeds: Only `PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=upb` which became available in 4.x fails.

**What did you expect to see**

I expected the behaviour for `upb` to be the same as the `python` implementation. I.e. it works without issue.

**What did you see instead?**

The basic error that I get is: `TypeError: Couldn't build proto file into descriptor pool: duplicate file name (google/protobuf/descriptor.proto)`

More detail can be seen in the error.txt file here: https://github.com/Atheuz/test-protobuf-schema-error/blob/master/error.txt

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**

What's happening is that we are going into `common/terms_pb2.py` and manually replacing `from google.protobuf import descriptor_pb2 as google_dot_protobuf_dot_descriptor__pb2` with `from google_test.protobuf import descriptor_pb2 as google_dot_protobuf_dot_descriptor__pb2`.

Note that we are not doing this replacement in `common/options_pb2.py`, having this conflict of 2 different imports is necessary for the error to appear: i.e. if we do the replacement in `common/options_pb2.py`, then the error disappears and everything works fine, but this is not what we're doing on our end, in that we only do the replacement in one file and not all files.

The `descriptor_pb2.py` file was generated using `buf` version 1.11.0 and `protoc` version 3.21.12 using the following commands:

```
cd build
buf generate --config=buf.yaml --template=buf.gen.yaml
cp google/protobuf/descriptor_pb2.py ../google_test/protobuf/descriptor_pb2.py
```

The reason our organization does this replacement in the `common/terms_pb2.py` file is related to the Confluent Kafka Schema Registry, where apparently if we don't do this replacement the schema doesn't match what we have in our Confluent Kafka Schema Registry.

**Note** that it works fine in protobuf 3.20.3 using the cpp implementation, and the python implementation. It also works fine in protobuf 4.21.12 using the python implementation. The only implementation that has an issue with this edit is the upb implementation.

nodes.body:
One quirk of 4.21.x is that python proto code generated with older versions of protoc aren't compatible with it.  I followed your repro steps but instead regenerated the `*_pb2.py` files, and it passes.  Doing a diff I found:
```
-#from google.protobuf import descriptor_pb2 as google_dot_protobuf_dot_descriptor__pb2  # works
-from google_test.protobuf import descriptor_pb2 as google_dot_protobuf_dot_descriptor__pb2  # broken
+from google.protobuf import descriptor_pb2 as google_dot_protobuf_dot_descriptor__pb2
```
It looks like you're trying to insert your own descriptor into generated code?  I'm kind of surprised this ever worked..  What are you trying to do?

@mkruskal-google yes, we're inserting our own descriptor into the generated code. My understanding is that this is something that's necessary for our confluent kafka schema registry lookups to work correctly.

But the base issue is that this works fine in the python implementation and the cpp implementation on 3.20.3, and it works fine on the python implementation on 4.21.12 as well. It's only the upb implementation that it fails on.

Note: this also seems to build just fine if you insert your custom descriptor into *both* generated files.  I can't explain why upb is *different* than the other implementations, but using two different descriptor files in two different protos that reference each other seems like it's asking for trouble

Yes, I'm aware.

The problem is that different implementations other than upb do not have an issue with this. I'm also trying to see if we can get rid of this internally, but for years this has worked fine for both cpp and python implementations and only with the 4.21 release has it broken with the switch over to upb as the default.

@mkruskal-google do you know of a way to force protoc/buf to not use the google/protobuf/descriptor_pb2.py but instead use our custom generated one without doing this hacky replacement? Maybe that'll fix our issue.

Here's the internal user story:

"I want to ensure our users can pick up their code bindings and be able to use them without any modifications
So that our developer experience is as seamless as possible, and communication with Kafka and the schema registry works correctly.

Notes:
We currently need to do some adjustment to our python code bindings before these are pushed to local PyPi. This will ensure producers/consumers will use matching schemas with the ones produced in the schema registry.

The main issue is that the protobuf library for python includes the google common code bindings as well, taking precedence over our own descriptor.proto. Unfortunately, the internal descriptor field seem to be different, and schema registry doesn't like that.

By doing some tweaks to our produced code bindings, however, we can make this work. Steps to modify the code bindings:

AFTER generating the python code bindings, we should:
- rename the google/protobuf folder into google_test/protobuf 
- any generated code binding importing from our google.protobuf needs to have their import changed, by pointing to google_test/protobuf - only the import of a file we own needs to be changed"
I'm not aware of any feature that supports swapping out descriptor.proto (other than a post-generation find/replace).  What are you trying to change in it?

Here are the descriptors in a zip file, ours is called `our_descriptor_pb2.py`, google one is called `your_descriptor_pb2.py`.
[descriptors.zip](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/files/10499593/descriptors.zip)
Note that the Google descriptor is 107 KB and our descriptor is 119 KB.

Our descriptor was generated using `buf 1.1.0` and `protoc 3.21.12` as seen here: https://github.com/Atheuz/test-protobuf-schema-error/tree/master/build.

Note that if you generate it with `protoc 3.21.12` in the `build/external/google/protobuf` directory using the command `protoc -I=. --python_out=. descriptor.proto` you end up with a small `descriptor_pb2.py` file of like 16 KB, compared to when you generate it using `buf` in the `build` directory using the command `buf generate --config=buf.yaml --template=buf.gen.yaml` where you end up with the 119 KB `descriptor_pb2.py` file.

> I'm not aware of any feature that supports swapping out descriptor.proto (other than a post-generation find/replace). What are you trying to change in it?

Hi, I also have the same issue here. I have a project that needs to be updated with proto schema, so I have a job for updating and replacing the schema. when the proto changes, I get the following error but if it does not change, its works fine!
```
TypeError: Couldn't build proto file into descriptor pool: duplicate symbol
```

title: Support for Ruby 3.2.0 in prebuilt binaries
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: main
Language: Ruby

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
All

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Any

**What did you do?**
Install latest rubygem.

**What did you expect to see**
Prebuilt binary for Ruby 3.2.0 to be installed

**What did you see instead?**
It is installing `with native extensions` (ie. compiling)

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
Reopening #11407 with proper template, and because the issue has been closed.

Virtually, the rubygem needs to explicitly support and build for Ruby 3.2.0 as well as the others.
Currently the native prebuilt gems are build for `>= 2.5, < 3.2.DEV`
 (see https://rubygems.org/gems/google-protobuf/versions/3.21.12-x86_64-linux for instance)

We should add support for 3.2.0 as it has been released in December.

nodes.body:
As stated in the bug you linked to, the workaround for this is to use the ruby source gem instead of the compiled binary. We are working on 22.0 currently, which will only release ruby source gems making them default compatible with ruby 3.2.

Unfortunately I don't think we will be updating the ruby gem binary for 21.x given the impending release.

@deannagarcia and how long until that is released?

Bundler does not like keeping `ruby` under `PLATFORMS` these days and tends to want to force in specific architectures; and some of the components in our gem stack, including `grpc`, have _extremely_ long build times when built from source - which costs us a fortune in CI time. Compilation can also be fragile. So - we don't want to keep the hack we have in our CI `Dockerfile` forcing Bundler into a `ruby` platform any longer than we must.

We are currently aiming to release next week.

When we release only source gems will that solve your problem or will you still have the same issue?

@deannagarcia Oh cool, that's not long to wait at all, thanks.

Source-only gems should be OK for protobuf since it builds fairly quickly (GRPC is around 10 minutes or more!). There's always a risk of failure when building native components but it sounds like you don't want to have to manage a wide range of pre-built binaries or have to keep the builds on a Ruby treadmill and that definitely makes sense.

We're also in the position of wanting this - building from source takes way to long on CI/CD - plus much more bloated images with the build tools. Looking forward to an officially supported gem - we're not going to go production without it and really want to test YJIT. Thanks for all the hard work everyone involved.

While source-only gems will mitigate the problem, it is in my opinion a suboptimal solution.
I do not have build-times for protobuf, but there IS some overhead, and as @mrmason mentions (As I am writing this), the low-resource CI/CD pipelines, will produce a overhead both in image-bloating as well as build times for us as well.

I will **strongly** suggest, that we keep up the support for prebuilt gems. If not with the existing CI pipeline, then maybe we could rethink the build-setup a bit, to make it easier in the future, to support future Ruby versions (And maybe architectures etc.)?
PR raised for supporting fat binaries on Ruby 3.2: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/11592

From what I can tell the build time for protobuf is negligible. It seems like precompiled binaries add extra maintenance overhead and delay our ability to upgrade Ruby, so I'm totally in favor of removing them. It's easy to cache things on CI, and there are loads of other gems that take much longer to compile.

I note that it was estimated there'd be 3.22 within the week, but it's been more than two weeks and there is still no 3.22 other than a release candidate from Feb-2, which other Google gems do not select via their gemspec, so we are *still* unable to use this in CI.

Is there an update, please, on when this will be done? It's kinda dragging and the maintenance burden and extra CI time required by being forced into a `ruby` platform is really expensive.

Why aren't you able to use 3.22-rc2?

Unfortunately our release process often takes multiple release candidate iterations and we are actually trying to get support for binary gems into 3.22. We are aiming to get the full release out next week, but if we see issues with release candidates it could get pushed back.
We don't use protobuf directly. It's pulled in as a dependency of GRPC, which uses `~> 3.21` AFAICT and that won't select RCs.
@pond you can add `protobuf  3.22-rc2` to your Gemfile for now.

@johnnyshields I appreciate the suggestion, but then I have to add a task to my backlog to remove it again, and/or keep watching Google Protobuf every day, just so I can remove the hack.

We don't hack our software and we don't put alpha, beta or release candidate gems into Production.

> We don't hack our software and we don't put alpha, beta or release candidate gems into Production.

Then you're doing it wrong 😆
I see 3.22.0 has now been released - thanks; we've updated to that and the CI builds are running again. Yay!

title: Type mismatch when using MessageFactory().GetPrototype in Python using protobuf 3.20.3 when using the cpp implementation
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: protobuf==3.20.3 (issue does not exist in 4.21.12).
Language: Python

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Ubuntu 22.04.1 LTS

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Python 3.9.15

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a virtualenv: `virtualenv .venv --python=3.9`
2. Activate the virtualenv: `source .venv/bin/activate`
3. Install protobuf==3.20.3: `pip install protobuf==3.20.3`
4. Save the following Python script to a file called `type-issue.py`: 
```
from google.protobuf.timestamp_pb2 import Timestamp
from google.protobuf.message_factory import MessageFactory

def main():
    msg_class = MessageFactory().GetPrototype(Timestamp.DESCRIPTOR)
    print(isinstance(msg_class(seconds=1, nanos=0), Timestamp))
    print(isinstance(Timestamp(seconds=1, nanos=0), msg_class))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```
5. Run the command: (export PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=cpp; python types-issue.py)
6. Observe that both print statements output False.
7. Run the command (export PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python; python types-issue.py)
8. Observe that both print statements output True

**What did you expect to see**
When using protobuf==3.20.3, using the cpp implementation: That messages constructed using `MessageFactory().GetPrototype` are of the same type as the directly imported message class.

**What did you see instead?**
When using protobuf==3.20.3, using the cpp implementation: That messages constructed using `MessageFactory().GetPrototype` are of a different type than the directly imported message class.

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
Note that in protobuf==4.21.12, this is no longer an issue, because the cpp implementation has been replaced with the upb implementation and it doesn't have this problem. However, we can't update to protobuf 4.21 because of a different issue.

This is how confluent-kafka constructs messages using its protobuf DeserializingConsumer, and we're having issues with comparing types that come from that vs the imported class type. We're using type checks in utility functions, and these break because of the type mismatch.

Because the issue is already resolved in 4.21, is this a "won't fix" kind of thing or is 3.20 still being supported with active development for bugfixes like this?

title: CMake files are not installed when built with autoconf
body:
<!--

For questions or troubleshooting, please post on the protobuf mailing list:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf 
Stack Overflow is also a useful if unofficial resource https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/protocol-buffers
-->

CMake is planning to deprecated `FindProtobuf in favour of the cmake files provided by protobuf, because it is difficult to maintain compatibility with protobuf's cmake files, see [[1]](https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/23037#note_1288748) and [[2]](https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/merge_requests/8045) But that relies on distributions shipping these cmake files. Some distributions, like Debian or Fedora, don't ship the files, yet, because the distributions are using autoconf to build protobuf.

Please install CMake files when using autoconf+*make install* or remove autoconf files from release tarballs to force distributions to provide protobuf's CMake files.

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v21.12
Language: C++/Java/Python/C#/Ruby/PHP/Objective-C/Javascript

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Arch Linux

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Extract protobuf tarball (https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/download/v21.12/protobuf-cpp-3.21.12.tar.gz)
2. `./configure`
3. `make`
4. `make install` 

**What did you expect to see**
CMake files installed, like it is done when using CMake to build protobuf.

**What did you see instead?**
No cmake files installed.

Make sure you include information that can help us debug (full error message, exception listing, stack trace, logs).

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**

nodes.body:
We've removed autotools support as of https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/10132 and will no longer be shipping those configs.  The only supported mechanism for system installation in 22.x and beyond will be cmake.  Note, you can *also* use cmake to install protobuf in 21.x, in which case the cmake files should get set up properly.

Given that we plan to release 22.x in the next few weeks, I'm going to close this.  Let me know if you have some more specific need for this in 21.x w/ autotools though.
Thanks, that information helps.

title: Unable to compile all protofiles in directory tree with `protoc`.
body:
**Environment**
Protobufs Version: 3.21.9 (Installed and compiled from Conan Center)
Operating System: MacOS Ventura 13.1
Shell: zsh

Apple clang version 14.0.0 (clang-1400.0.29.202)
Target: arm64-apple-darwin22.2.0
Thread model: posix

**Problem Statement**
Passing recursive directory expansion (aka "globbing" or "globstar" or "wildcard") to `protoc` is not working for me. Furthermore it does not match the globbing behavior of my shell. As a result I am unable to write a `protoc` script that will not require maintenance as the directory structure changes.

[This StackOverflow post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59314322/protobuf-build-protoc-select-all-proto-files-in-a-directory) seems to be demonstrating the same problem, and suggests this is a system-specific problem, as one of the respondants is experiencing the desired behavior. But the post does not provide resolution. The comments suggest it might be due to differing shell behaviors, but as demonstrated below my native shell behavior is as expected.

**Example Setup**
My protofiles are in a structure like this:

```
protofiles/
  cheese.proto
  crackers.proto
  subdirectory/
    beans.proto
    cornbread.proto
    extrasubdirectory/
      pickles.proto
```

**Test of Native Shell Behavior**

```bash
$ find protofiles/**/*.proto
protofiles/cheese.proto
protofiles/crackers.proto
protofiles/subdirectory/beans.proto
protofiles/subdirectory/cornbread.proto
protofiles/subdirectory/extrasubdirectory/pickles.proto
```

**Results of `protoc` Command**

This is the command I would like to use:

```bash
$ protoc -I=protofiles --cpp_out=src protofiles/**/*.proto

$ find src/**  
src/subdirectory
src/subdirectory/cornbread.pb.h
src/subdirectory/cornbread.pb.cc
src/subdirectory/beans.pb.cc
src/subdirectory/beans.pb.h
```

As you can see it is treating the globstar `**` as a "exactly one directory level". In order to compile the top-level directory, I must run:

```bash
$ protoc -I=protofiles --cpp_out=src protofiles/*.proto

$ find src/**
src/cheese.pb.cc
src/cheese.pb.h
src/crackers.pb.cc
src/crackers.pb.h
```

And to get the bottom level directory:

```bash
$ protoc -I=protofiles --cpp_out=src protofiles/**/**/*.proto

$ find src/**
src/subdirectory
src/subdirectory/extrasubdirectory
src/subdirectory/extrasubdirectory/pickles.pb.h
src/subdirectory/extrasubdirectory/pickles.pb.cc
```

The only way to get my whole tree to compile is to manually specify as many levels of the tree as there are, which is messy and brittle:

```bash
$ protoc -I=protofiles --cpp_out=src protofiles/*.proto protofiles/**/*.proto protofiles/**/**/*.proto

$ find src/**
src/cheese.pb.cc
src/cheese.pb.h
src/crackers.pb.cc
src/crackers.pb.h
src/subdirectory
src/subdirectory/cornbread.pb.h
src/subdirectory/cornbread.pb.cc
src/subdirectory/extrasubdirectory
src/subdirectory/extrasubdirectory/pickles.pb.h
src/subdirectory/extrasubdirectory/pickles.pb.cc
src/subdirectory/beans.pb.cc
src/subdirectory/beans.pb.h
```

nodes.body: Instead of sticking with `**`, I was thinking about attaching the results of `find` into protoc? Something like `protoc -I=protofiles --cpp_out=src $(find protofiles/**/*.proto)`.

Hi @shaod2. This was good thinking and has helped me identify that `protoc` is not actually the source of my problem.

I didn't mention it in my original post because I did not think it was relevant, but I am running the `protoc` command from a Python function in my Conanfile. I naively assumed this function would simply be passing my command string to the shell unaltered but it appears either Conan or Python is changing the behavior of the globstar before it reaches my shell. (Pretty abysmal behavior in my humble opinion.)

I discovered this because using the method you described resulted in the same behavior as in my original post, which was very surprising since we know that the `find` command is returning all the desired files. Indeed hand-writing the files returned by `find` into the `protoc` command works as desired, so it's clear something else is going on before my command is reaching the shell. I've verified this with a couple of other simple tests.

I will close this issue. Thanks very much for your help.

nodes.body: I suspect the problem is that our CMake build is not currently set up in a way that would allow cross compiles to just work out of the box. To do a cross-compile, I believe you would want to build protoc normally for your host platform, and then build for your target platform (i.e. Android) but using `-DWITH_PROTOC=path/to/protoc` to tell CMake where to find a protoc binary built for your host machine.

Thanks for your reply, I guess this issue becomes a feature request for this to be supported then.

The rationale is that it would make creating Android apps with JNI components using Protobuf significantly easier since the builders will not have to manually configure anything (like pre-compiling protoc in this case).

title: "unified_protos" or "Unified Python/C++ support": Python protobuf backed by generated C++ protos reducing cross-language serialization cost
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
Python, though it affects compilation for C++ protos when the flag is enabled.

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
When using Python C-extensions, such as via pybind11, and passing a protobuf from Python to C++ (or vice versa) the "best" way is to serialize the protobuf in the source language then pass it as a buffer across the barrier, and deserialize from the buffer. This means passing large protos across the barrier can be more expensive than implementing the C++ function in Python.

However, if the Python protobuf was actually backed by a C++ generated protobuf, then when passing the object the C++ message could be pulled out and passed to C++ directly. And when passed back to Python, a protobuf could be created that either took ownership of the C++ proto or knew that the C++ proto was owned externally.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
This could all be done by using the `PyProto_API` object and either building a CPython entrypoint with the protos all statically linked in, or (as I managed to get working) by building shared libraries for every C++ proto and loading them before loading every Python proto.

I'd like to propose, and eventually merge, the shared library solution, with the documented caveat that all the shared libraries need to be generated and built by the same version of libprotobuf that is loaded as well. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

There is a path where `py_binary` is replaced/implemented by a `cc_binary` entrypoint that statically (or dynamically) links in all protos used directly or indirectly, and possibly all C extensions. However, that requires modifying the users codebase and cannot be done within the protobuf codebase itself. It also is non-optimal if users want to use or ship multiple py_binary's that use an overlapping set of protos, since every proto would necessarily be loaded into memory more than once while in the shared library implementation they would be loaded once by the OS and shared across binaries.

**Additional context**
I got this working internally in my codebase by implementing a custom bazel flag (as opposed to the define-based flag that protobuf uses for `use_fast_cpp_protos`) and by altering both `py_proto_library` and `cc_proto_library`, and by depending on undocumented protoc C++ generator options and protoc plugin options.

However, I would be happy to alter that approach as necessary to get this feature upstreamed, as I think it would be a big boon to the Python protobuf community to be able to use pybind11 or other C extensions with "zero-overhead" protobuf passing. It would definitely make protobufs more useful in performance sensitive applications, such as my use-case.

nodes.body:
We want to support better sharing between Python and C/C++, but not through the old bindings code in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/tree/main/python/google/protobuf/pyext

The future is the Python/upb bindings in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/tree/main/python  You might notice that we no longer ship the old extension in our PyPI packages. Ever since 4.21 we are shipping the upb-based extension instead.

Unfortunately upb's user-level C++ API is still in its infancy. It lives in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/tree/main/protos, but it is not mature enough yet for us to offer it generally to users. But that is the way forward.
So there's no interest in the working solution while we wait for the future solution? I've literally done all the work already for internal use, and am willing to port it to upstream.
@haberman Is the plan for upb's C++ API to replace the current C++ protobuf API entirely? Or would it just be used in interoperability contexts like this?

> So there's no interest in the working solution while we wait for the future solution?

If it was a minimally-intrusive change that did not increase our support burden, we could review a change. However based on the discussion in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/11669 it looks like your design relies on insertion points, which we are strongly moving away from.

I would echo the comment on https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/11669 which suggests engaging with us early if you are interested in contributing a behavior or API change. I understand the frustration if you have something that's working for you already, but we need to make sure that contributions align with our intended future directions.

> Is the plan for upb's C++ API to replace the current C++ protobuf API entirely? Or would it just be used in interoperability contexts like this?

There are a lot of unknowns in this space. The existing C++ API has a lot of legacy warts that we would like to deprecate. However it also has a very large body of existing users, and migrating those users to something new is a very large task.

title: Silent data corruption when writing a message exceeding 2GB in size
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v21.12
Language: Java

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Ubuntu 20.04.5 LTS

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

**What did you do?**
1. Create a (huge) message greater than 2GB.
2. Write the message to a file.
3. Read back the message from the file.

https://github.com/zabetak/protobuf-large-message is simple project reproducing the problem with a reduced message model from the protobuf tutorial.

**What did you expect to see**
I was expecting the message creation (Step 1) or write (Step 2) to fail with a meaningful message or the message to be read correctly from the file.

**What did you see instead?**
I got the following exception while attempting to read the message from the file.
```
Exception in thread "main" com.google.protobuf.InvalidProtocolBufferException: Protocol message was too large.  May be malicious.  Use CodedInputStream.setSizeLimit() to increase the size limit.
	at com.google.protobuf.InvalidProtocolBufferException.sizeLimitExceeded(InvalidProtocolBufferException.java:162)
	at com.google.protobuf.CodedInputStream$StreamDecoder.refillBuffer(CodedInputStream.java:2781)
	at com.google.protobuf.CodedInputStream$StreamDecoder.readRawByte(CodedInputStream.java:2859)
	at com.google.protobuf.CodedInputStream$StreamDecoder.readRawVarint64SlowPath(CodedInputStream.java:2648)
	at com.google.protobuf.CodedInputStream$StreamDecoder.readRawVarint32(CodedInputStream.java:2542)
	at com.google.protobuf.CodedInputStream$StreamDecoder.readMessage(CodedInputStream.java:2405)
	at com.github.zabetak.protobuf.bugs.protos.AddressBook$Builder.mergeFrom(AddressBook.java:440)
	at com.github.zabetak.protobuf.bugs.protos.AddressBook$1.parsePartialFrom(AddressBook.java:742)
	at com.github.zabetak.protobuf.bugs.protos.AddressBook$1.parsePartialFrom(AddressBook.java:734)
	at com.google.protobuf.AbstractParser.parseFrom(AbstractParser.java:86)
	at com.google.protobuf.AbstractParser.parseFrom(AbstractParser.java:91)
	at com.google.protobuf.AbstractParser.parseFrom(AbstractParser.java:48)
	at com.google.protobuf.GeneratedMessageV3.parseWithIOException(GeneratedMessageV3.java:364)
	at com.github.zabetak.protobuf.bugs.protos.AddressBook.parseFrom(AddressBook.java:219)
	at com.github.zabetak.protobuf.bugs.serde.WriteReadBook.readBooks(WriteReadBook.java:63)
	at com.github.zabetak.protobuf.bugs.serde.WriteReadBook.main(WriteReadBook.java:35)
```
The reason for the exception is clear and understood but now that the file is (permanently?) corrupted there is not much we can do.

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
I understand that it is not a good practice to write huge messages but there should be some kind of guard against data corruption. 

This problem came up in actual deployments of Apache Hive, Spark, etc, due to [ORC metadata](https://github.com/apache/orc/blob/2ff9001ddef082eaa30e21cbb034f266e0721664/proto/orc_proto.proto#L268) that are stored as protobuf messages.

Probably the ORC team will reconsider the message layout in future versions but it may be a good idea to find a way to prevent this from within the protobuf library.

Relevant tickets:
* https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HIVE-11268
* https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HIVE-11592
* https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HIVE-26987
* https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ORC-1361

title: `optional` is not working, it doesn't allow me to set a field to null
body:
As I tested out, the Python, Javascript/Typescript, Rust, Dart, they all support or about to support optional filed to null.

Why Java and Cpp can't do that?

https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/issues/9868

nodes.body: I'm not a maintainer, but everything works as designed here, `null` values are not allowed. `optional` instructs the compiler to generate the `has*` methods for the corresponding fields.

Then why `python,javascript,rust`, they support `null`?

If `java` do not support it, then nobody would use `java` to communicate with `python,javascript/typescript,rust,dart` by using `grpc`

Null fields do not exist in protobuf. Getters, for example, should never return null, irrespective of the language. Please note that a similar question has already been asked [before](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/8781) and the official advice is to rely on the `clear*` methods to get a consistent behaviour.

Could you guys make a simple logic check like this:

```
def a_set_function(value):
    if value == null:
        call clear* method, so that property won't exist in the response (return value)
```

And in the client side, the program will do this:

```
if protocol optional definition fields not exists in the return value, it sets that field to null
```
This is working as intended. Feel free to create a PR with your intended changes where we can review.
This is so weird. Some language implementations treat `optional` as `nullable` but some is not.

title: [PHP] JSON serialization fails for negative durations
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: `3.19.4` and tested with `21.12` for this issue
Language: PHP

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Tested on **Debian Buster** (Docker) and **macOS Ventura 13.01**

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
`protoc` binary from [the Github releases](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases)

**What did you do?**
Serializing a `Duration` with negative seconds fails [despite being authorized](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/373d8225af42e9dbfc01431b46ff48be0eabae90/src/google/protobuf/duration.proto#L104-L106):

```php
$d = new \Google\Protobuf\Duration();
$d->setSeconds(3600);
$d->serializeToJsonString(); // OK
$d->setSeconds(-3600);
$d->serializeToJsonString(); // Error occurred during JSON serialization: bad duration
```

However, deserialization works:

```php
$d = new \Google\Protobuf\Duration();
$d->mergeFromJsonString('"-3600s"')
$d->getSeconds(); // returns `-3600`
```

**What did you expect to see**

Serialization shouldn't fail and should return `"-3600s"`.

**What did you see instead?**

```
Fatal error: Uncaught Exception: Error occurred during JSON serialization: bad duration in /path/to/project/index.php:9
Stack trace:
#0 /path/to/project/index.php(9): Google\Protobuf\Internal\Message->serializeToJsonString()
#1 {main}
  thrown in /path/to/project/index.php on line 9
```

title: Remove `ProtoPreconditions.CheckNotNull` from setters C# .NET
body:
In proto3 all non-basic fields are optional and should treated as nullable. Nullability is not supported #6632 and probably won't be, but right now working with generated files is a mess.

Generated types project does not support `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`, so compiler allows assigning nulls
```csharp
new FooType 
{
FooField = null // no warning in IDE
}
```

But there is null checking in setter
https://github.dev/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/3becebb82a745b1a50e4cd2c5d44b4d22c15d4be/src/google/protobuf/compiler/csharp/csharp_primitive_field.cc#L143
which will throw an exception if we try to set value to null.

Current solution to make it working is to **NOT SET THE FIELD**.

```csharp
new FooType 
{
//FooField = null // do not assign null!!1
}
```

I would like to see either nullability which was introduced in C#8 in 2019 or at least being able to consciously and purposely assign a null.

nodes.body: No, just ignoring invalid values instead of failing on them seems like a very bad idea to me. Just don't set the properties to null. (Note that message type properties *can* be set to null.)

Ah, I think I misunderstood the proposal. If you want setting the value to null to be equivalent to Clear, I think that would be confusing - because calling the getter would then still return an empty string or byte string. (Note that this really only applies to string and bytestring fields anyway. As I said before, message type fields can already be set to null.)

Ok, I now see my problem. Thanks :) So now I only wait for #6632, because this will protect guys like me from assigning a `null` to a `string`.

> If you want setting the value to null to be equivalent to Clear

What do you mean?

> > If you want setting the value to null to be equivalent to Clear

> What do you mean?

I mean that if the field is marked as optional in proto3, there will be a `Clear` method, e.g. `ClearName()`. I had thought that you'd wanted `message.Name = null;` to be equivalent to `message.ClearName();` - but `message.Name` will be an empty string (not a null reference) after that. (If we were designing everything from scratch, we *might* take a different approach to that, but I'm not sure. At the moment changing it would be a massively breaking change.)

Yeah, I would expect that any `optional` field will be mapped to sth like
```csharp
public string? Name { get; set;}
```

and then being able to assign a value
```csharp
new FooType 
{
   Name = input.Any() ? Translate(input.First) : null
}
```

Ok, I can set `string.Empty` though in my mind `optional` == `nullable`

> Ok, I can set string.Empty though in my mind optional == nullable

I can see why, but that's not how it's generally represented - and in particular, it's *definitely* not how it's represented for primitive numeric fields; even if we started from scratch, we'd need to very carefully consider whether we wanted to do that... because it means adding field presence (by making an existing field optional) becomes a breaking change, where it's not at the moment.

I'm going to close this issue now as we're *definitely* not going to make the change given where we are today. While it might be interesting to speculate what we'd do in a completely green-field environment, unfortunately it's also time-consuming :(

Regarding the issue of null checking in the setter & fallback to a default value in the getter, there is issue:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9352

If you want to be able to directly get & set null values on a property, the best solution seems to be replacing optional scalar types with well known wrapper types, e.g. `optional string` -> `google.protobuf.StringValue`.

title: Cannot parse from byte like objects (like bytearray) from python
body:
We upgraded the python protobuf implementation and suddenly found it throwing an error saying expected bytes object not a bytearray object. A little digging found that the underlying protobuf library had changed from google C++ protobuf to upb and we were passing a bytearray object in. Investigating upb resulted in the following suggestion:

Change https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/blob/main/python/message.c#L1225

From
```C
 if (PyMemoryView_Check(arg)) {
```
to
```C
  if (PyObject_CheckBuffer(arg)) {
```

The very next method called on arg is `PyBytes_FromObject` which is documented as `Return the bytes representation of object o that implements the buffer protocol.`  In essence, change things so that the input just has to implement the buffer protocol, not *be* a memory view object.

Additional error checks or something might need to be made, all I know about the python C API is what I've read of the python documentation.

A little unclear about your exact question here. If you could clarify that would appreciated.

I know what is in the docs.
However im saying that the docs are wrong or the code for a Map is wrong.
As i said  MapField<TKey, TValue> already implements:
IDeepCloneable<MapField<TKey, TValue>>,
IDictionary<TKey, TValue>,
ICollection<KeyValuePair<TKey, TValue>>,
IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<TKey, TValue>>,
IEnumerable,
IEquatable<MapField<TKey, TValue>>,
IDictionary,

Im using, successfully, a message that contains a Map. "It acts like a duck, quacks like a duck, therefore is a duck". In this case a duck is a dictionary, a list, a collection with no need to wrap it with a repeated field.

No, I'm afraid you are just wrong. There's a difference between a dictionary and a list of dictionaries - where the latter is what a repeated map in proto would represent. Note that sticking to just C#, `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` implements `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<TKey,TValue>>` - but is still not a list of dictionaries.

If you believe the docs say a custom type is needed for a *single* dictionary, please quote that part of the docs.

title: Weakref to protobuf objects broken in protobuf v4+
