title: Message factory broken for files with message extensions in upb impl
body:
The Python `message_factory.GetMessages` and related functions/methods fail when registering an extension, since the upb library currently [does not implement `RegisterExtension`](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/blob/b747edb830b0fab524e0063fb2e156c390405dfa/python/message.c#L1630-L1633) (see https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/13743).

The Python and C++ message implementations work as expected.

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: protobuf==4.21.12 from PyPI
Language: Python

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**

macOS 12.1

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

Python library, upb message implementation.

**What did you do?**

Example proto file: `microext.proto`

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package microext;

import "google/protobuf/descriptor.proto";

extend google.protobuf.MessageOptions {
  MicroExtension micro_extension = 50001;
}

message MicroExtension {
  string ext_a = 1;
  uint32 ext_b = 2;
}

message MicroTestMessage {
  string field_a = 1;
  bool field_b = 2;

  option (microext.micro_extension) = {
    ext_a: "extension-test"
    ext_b: 1234
  };
}
```

Generate a file descriptor set from `protoc`:
```sh
protoc -I ./ microext.proto --include_imports --descriptor_set_out ./microext.fds
```

Python code to read the file descriptor set and create dynamic message types: `test_msg_factory.py`

```python
from google.protobuf.descriptor_pb2 import FileDescriptorSet
from google.protobuf.message_factory import GetMessages

with open("microext.fds", "rb") as f:
    fds = FileDescriptorSet.FromString(f.read())

classes = GetMessages(fds.file)
MicroTestMessage = classes["microext.MicroTestMessage"]

msg = MicroTestMessage(field_a="test", field_b=True)
print(msg)
```

**What did you expect to see**

```
field_a: "test"
field_b: true
```

Note that when running with the Python message impl, or the C++ impl (properly installed), this ^ is the result I get from running e.g.
```
$ PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python python test_msg_factory.py
```

**What did you see instead?**

```
$ python test_msg_factory.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/alkasm/prog/upb-proto-extensions/test_msg_factory.py", line 7, in <module>
    classes = GetMessages(fds.file)
  File "/Users/alkasm/prog/upb-proto-extensions/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/google/protobuf/message_factory.py", line 189, in GetMessages
    return _FACTORY.GetMessages([file_proto.name for file_proto in file_protos])
  File "/Users/alkasm/prog/upb-proto-extensions/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/google/protobuf/message_factory.py", line 158, in GetMessages
    extended_class.RegisterExtension(extension)
  File "/Users/alkasm/prog/upb-proto-extensions/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/google/protobuf/message.py", line 371, in RegisterExtension
    raise NotImplementedError
NotImplementedError
```

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**

Note that there's a related change between main and the latest release on PyPI: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/commit/c80e7efac72510a2bc3e9365520055f6d6656c1d, but I don't believe that affects this problem in either direction (neither causes or solves it).

nodes.body: @esorot Is there anybody working on it ? Could you please inform us. Thanks!
@anandolee it looks like our unit tests don't cover this case. Could you add a unit test for this and fix upb accordingly?

Very happy to see that an issue is already created for this !

I run into the exact same problem while trying to load protobuf classes from a descriptor set. A workaround that worked for me in the **4.21.12** version was to simply catch the exception in the `_FACTORY.GetMessages` function:
```python
from types import MethodType
from google.protobuf.descriptor_pb2 import FileDescriptorSet
from google.protobuf.message_factory import _FACTORY, GetMessages

def patch_get_messages(self, files):
    result = {}
    for file_name in files:
        file_desc = self.pool.FindFileByName(file_name)
        for desc in file_desc.message_types_by_name.values():
            result[desc.full_name] = self.GetPrototype(desc)

    for extension in file_desc.extensions_by_name.values():
        if extension.containing_type not in self._classes: #pylint: disable=protected-access
            self.GetPrototype(extension.containing_type)
        extended_class = self._classes[extension.containing_type] #pylint: disable=protected-access

        # === PATCH STARTS HERE ===

        try:
            extended_class.RegisterExtension(extension)
        except NotImplementedError:
            pass

        # === PATCH ENDS HERE ===

        if extension.message_type:
            self.GetPrototype(extension.message_type)
    return result

# Monkey-patching the `GetMessages` function to prevent `NotImplementedError` exceptions
_FACTORY.GetMessages = MethodType(patch_get_messages, _FACTORY)

# Use `GetMessages` normally
with open('protos.desc', 'rb') as proto_desc:
    descriptor_set = FileDescriptorSet.FromString(proto_desc.read())
print(GetMessages(descriptor_set.file))
```

That seemed to do the trick to be able to use `GetMessages`.

Upgrading to version **4.22.0** with the `_FACTORY` removed, we can apply the same patch to the [`GetMessageClassesForFiles`](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/python/google/protobuf/message_factory.py#L76) function:
```python
import google.protobuf.message_factory
from google.protobuf.descriptor_pb2 import FileDescriptorSet

def patch_get_messages_classes_for_files(files, pool):
    result = {}
    for file_name in files:
        file_desc = pool.FindFileByName(file_name)
        for desc in file_desc.message_types_by_name.values():
            result[desc.full_name] = google.protobuf.message_factory.GetMessageClass(desc)

    for extension in file_desc.extensions_by_name.values():
        extended_class = google.protobuf.message_factory.GetMessageClass(extension.containing_type)
        
        # === PATCH STARTS HERE ===

        try:
            extended_class.RegisterExtension(extension)
        except NotImplementedError:
            pass

        # === PATCH ENDS HERE ===

        if extension.message_type:
            google.protobuf.message_factory.GetMessageClass(extension.message_type)
    return result

# Monkey-patching the `GetMessages` function to prevent `NotImplementedError` exceptions
google.protobuf.message_factory.GetMessageClassesForFiles = patch_get_messages_classes_for_files

# Use `GetMessages` normally
with open('protos.desc', 'rb') as proto_desc:
    descriptor_set = FileDescriptorSet.FromString(proto_desc.read())
print(google.protobuf.message_factory.GetMessages(descriptor_set.file))
```
And it seems to hold fine when I test it alone. 

**However for my use case, this results in a `Segmentation fault` later on.** Not sure exactly why, I tried to profile it a little bit using `sys.settrace` and it seems to fail for subsequent calls to `MessageToJSON` using the loaded classes.

So to summarize, I'm not sure if the *segfaults* are related to this issue but fixing it would definitely eliminate the "monkey-patching business" out of the equation for me to be able to test it further. Until then, keeping to **4.21.12** seems to be the easiest option.

*PS: If you want to checkout the project I'm working on, it's available [here](https://github.com/pinax-network/substreams_firehose/).*
I've the same issue. Do you at which version the issue has been introduced in the first place?

> I've the same issue. Do you at which version the issue has been introduced in the first place?

upb was introduced with the jump from protobuf 3.2 to 4.2. More here: https://protobuf.dev/news/2022-05-06/
Has anyone been able to create a repro for this yet?

Note that support ends for python protobuf 3.20.x **this quarter**: https://protobuf.dev/support/version-support/#python

This is a breaking change that was introduced bumping from 3.20 to 4.21 which has not been remedied. Support for 3.20.x should be extended accordingly, or a fix should be included in 4.21 and 4.22 asap, before the quarter ends.

After more evaluation, we discovered that `RegisterExtension()` is no longer necessary unless you use the `Add*Descriptor()` functions, but those functions have been deprecated since August 2019: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/commit/4f02f056b5cea99052bfdfb6698afe47a3cf2964#diff-c0e7fb116209fdc80b3d84c68595eb3158a72bb031a2e673fa04fbf88bf8db2b

If you use `AddSerializedFile()` instead, `RegisterExtension()` is not necessary.

Since upb does not support `Add*Descriptor()`, there is no need to add support for `RegisterExtension()`.  If you are using upb, you should be able to just remove any `RegisterExtension()` calls.

Oh, I see now that the problem is coming from `RegisterExtension()` calls in the core library: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/183521a07204e4132368399bd4865fe26404eea9/python/google/protobuf/message_factory.py#L107

Yes, we should definitely fix that.
A fix is on the way.
Any updates here?
@anandolee @haberman what's the status on the fix? This issue is blocking us from parsing protobufs correctly
RegisterExtension() has been removed from message_factory.py. The issue should been fixed

title: RegisterExtension not yet implemented for Python, causing errors in the protobuf library
body:
See the issue filed on protobuf for more specifics: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/11863

TLDR, `Message.RegisterExtension` is [not yet implemented](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/blob/b747edb830b0fab524e0063fb2e156c390405dfa/python/message.c#L1630-L1633), though is expected in many places in the upstream protobuf library, for example when constructing dynamic message types with the [message factory](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/1d744d40c89fd1b4e36444c9de15a609425ac29e/python/google/protobuf/message_factory.py#L76-L113) module.

nodes.body: Note that general message extensions were [deprecated in proto3](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#customoptions), but they are still explicitly allowed for custom options. So realistically, only the built-in options types (message, field, enum, etc) need `RegisterExtension` implemented.

title: Build Error with c++20
body:
I am trying to build gRPC from source and I get the following error message:
```
external/upb/upbc/names.cc:89:26: error: ISO C++20 considers use of overloaded operator '!=' (with operand types 'upb::MessageDefPtr::FieldIter' and 'upb::MessageDefPtr::FieldIter') to be ambiguous despite there being a unique best viable function with non-reversed arguments [-Werror,-Wambiguous-reversed-operator]
  for (const auto& field : message.fields()) {
                         ^
external/upb/upb/reflection/def.hpp:321:10: note: candidate function with non-reversed arguments
    bool operator!=(const FieldIter& other) { return i_ != other.i_; }
         ^
external/upb/upb/reflection/def.hpp:322:10: note: ambiguous candidate function with reversed arguments
    bool operator==(const FieldIter& other) { return i_ == other.i_; }
         ^
```

I tried several different ways to disable this error using my bazel env, but it looks like the actual build target for names.cc is specifying the flags:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/blob/main/bazel/build_defs.bzl#L35

Any suggestions on a work around or a fix?

Thanks!

nodes.body: Example fix: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/pull/1169/files
Or better yet, consider turning off "-Werror" by default, and only enabling it internally.
Better would be to just fix the code (turn `operator==` and `operator!=` into friend nonmember functions taking both arguments by reference-to-const).

I like the idea of fixing the code, but that also means that any new warnings added by compilers in the future will break any libraries depending on this one. I wonder if the "-Werror" could conditionally be added, based on if the upb is the main repo vs being imported (by gRPC for example). The current set up seems quite fragile, for example, `deprecated-enum-enum-conversion` also needs fixing.

I encountered also C++20 build errors by just adding Bazel gRPC rules into my project, and those errors are:
```cpp
external/upb/upb/mini_table.hpp:63:22: note: add explicit 'this' or '*this' capture
external/upb/upb/mini_table.hpp: In lambda function:
external/upb/upb/mini_table.hpp:71:22: error: implicit capture of 'this' via '[=]' is deprecated in C++20 [-Werror=deprecated]
   71 |     return appender_([=](char* buf) {
```

I found a **stupid** way to circumvent that by using the C++17 standard by adding the flag to the `.bazelrc` file
```shell
build --action_env=BAZEL_CXXOPTS="-std=c++17"
```

Solves the issue but not a solution.

Environment:
* Linux Ubuntu 22.04
* Bazel 5.4.0
* Gcc/G++ 11.3.0
* Proto gRPC rules 4.3.0
* Proto rules 5.3.0-21.7
I got rid of the direct errors by patching the build file, but the warning still persist in all the generated code, and this gets rid of both.

I was able to fix the implicit `this`. Not sure why I am not able to publish a branch to do a pull request, but the change was fairly straightforward. 

Any input onto the restriction would be great to get the change pushed up.

> Not sure why I am not able to publish a branch to do a pull request, but the change was fairly straightforward.

Can you clarify? What prevents you from publishing a branch for a PR?

One potential idea for solving this would be to remove the -Werror flag from the build_defs.bzl file, but pass it as a commandline arg in your CI. That way new, unknowable compiler warnings won't cause the build to break for external users in the future, but CI will still treat warnings as errors for its configured workflows.

For those finding this from a google search, here is the work-around I found. This disables all warnings for external projects by adding `-w` to the copts for any targets under external.

Put these lines in your `.bazelrc`

```
# Disable warnings for targets that are outside the workspace.
build --per_file_copt=external/.*@-w
build --host_per_file_copt=external/.*@-w
```

title: Severe presentation issues in C++ documentation
body:
Documentation has recently been redirected from developers.google.com to protobuf.dev. This has caused a massive regression in usability:

- The main page of the documentation is structured by namespace and file - the overview is gone
- All links that reference a code entity are broken
- There is no longer a summary TOC on the side
- Very long, hard to read lines
- The very top of the page is obscured by the header
- Incorrect vertical alignment of return types in class summaries
- Low contrast color scheme that breaks accessibility guidelines (yellow on gray)
- Code block formatting is gone
- Font sizes are random
- Vertical spacing is random, there's excessive space around lists and paragraphs but no space between classes
- and many more.

Please consider restoring the old documentation site until the new one is usable.

nodes.body: Bazel 7 is not officially supported by upb (as it is not out).  If you have a PR to offer (or better yet a cl), we would be happy to review it.

Looking through the Bazel source code, the problem might be that `cc_common.create_linking_context_from_compilation_outputs` always creates a "nodeps" dynamic library that never depends on the transitive dependencies, which I guess can't work on macOS without `-undefined dynamic_lookup`. So maybe this should rather use `cc_common.link` instead?

[Fedora has enabled LTO when building Ruby](https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/ruby/c/1170d812fe0cd43aeddf7f15a63c2e6db3af8059), so its `RbConfig::CONFIG["CFLAGS"]` includes `-flto` as well.

If this is expected behavior, and there actually is a simple rule for how a service definition gets turned into a java class, I'd like to see that documented somewhere. Otherwise it results in me having to manually inspect the generated JAR files which is a pain in the butt.

Iterating over Protobuf objects in threads causes a segfault.

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: 3.21.12

Language: Ruby

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
OSX darwin19 (Catalina) and darwin22 (Ventura) -- probably others, I've only been able to test these.

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

**What did you do?**

Iterating over Protobuf objects in threads causes a segfault. Here's the minimal reproduction:

```ruby
require 'json'
require 'google/protobuf'

Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.build do
  add_message 'example.Config' do
    repeated :rows, :message, 1, 'example.ConfigRow'
  end

  add_message 'example.ConfigRow' do
    repeated :values, :message, 1, 'example.Value'
  end

  add_message 'example.Value' do
    optional :string, :string, 1
  end
end

module Example
  Config = Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup('example.Config').msgclass
  ConfigRow = Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup('example.ConfigRow').msgclass
  Value = Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup('example.Value').msgclass
end

content = { "rows": [{ "values": [{ "string": 'hello' }, { "string": 'world' }] },
                     { "values": [{ "string": 'thanks' },
                                  { "string": 'again' }] }] }.to_json

config = Example::Config.decode_json(content)

thread_count = 500
iterations_per_thread = 1000

threads = []
(1..thread_count).each do |i|
  threads << Thread.new do
    (1..iterations_per_thread).each do |iter|
      config.rows.each do |row|
        row.values.each do |conditional_value|
          conditional_value
        end
      end

      puts "assert #{i} #{iter}"
    end
  end
end

threads.map(&:join)

puts 'DONE!'
```

**What did you expect to see**

No segfault.

The segfault.

  end

  ConfigRow = Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool.generated_pool.lookup('example.ConfigRow').msgclass

end

thread_count = 2
iterations_per_thread = 100
    
GC.stress = 0x01 | 0x04

Oddly enough, calling `row.json` in the inner loop instead of `row.values.size` does **not** trigger a segfault.

The weak map implementation of the object cache introduced [here](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/commit/a00125024e9231d76746bd394fef8876f5cc15e2) is not thread safe.


Here's a timeline of the relevant commits and the results on Mac OS.
```
a0012502 (v3.15.0)
introduce weak map, which has a concurrency bug
ruby 2.6 works
ruby 2.7 SEGV
ruby 2.7 works if USE_WEAK_MAP=0

9879f423 (v3.15.3)
extend weak map to ruby 2.6. remove strong map. replace USE_WEAK_MAP with USE_SECONDARY_MAP (its inverse)
ruby 2.6 SEGV
ruby 2.6 breaks with ArgumentError if USE_SECONDARY_MAP=0
ruby 2.7 SEGV regardless of USE_SECONDARY_MAP

f0d6fcb2 (v3.15.7)
add mutex for secondary map
ruby 2.6 SEGV
ruby 2.6 breaks with ArgumentError if USE_SECONDARY_MAP=0
ruby 2.7 SEGV

2fe27d87 (v3.15.7)
fix mutex usage
ruby 2.6 works
ruby 2.6 breaks with ArgumentError if USE_SECONDARY_MAP=0
ruby 2.7 SEGV
ruby 2.7 works if USE_SECONDARY_MAP=1
```

We could do one of these 3:
1) Make `USE_SECONDARY_MAP` configurable at build time so that the user can set it to 1. This is the easiest fix
2) Restore strong cache implementation removed in `9879f423`
3) Fix weak map
If `USE_SECONDARY_MAP` fixes the problem, and we don't have any other fix available at the moment, we should just do that for now (by default).
The problem is that if I'm not mistaken `USE_SECONDARY_MAP` tend to cause "leaks" (not per say but IIRC the memory use is severely increased).

Hmm, I don't want to make users choose between much higher memory usage and SEGV race conditions.

title: Code generated w/ protobuf-java 3.22.0 broken in Quarkus
body:
Code that is generated with the new protobuf release 3.22.0 does not work in Quarkus (basically all current releases).

The exception looks somewhat like this:
```
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalAccessError: class <some-generated-protobuf-code> tried to access method 'com.google.protobuf.LazyStringArrayList com.google.protobuf.LazyStringArrayList.emptyList()' (<some-generated-protobuf-code> is in unnamed module of loader io.quarkus.bootstrap.classloading.QuarkusClassLoader @4f5c30b1; com.google.protobuf.LazyStringArrayList is in unnamed module of loader io.quarkus.bootstrap.classloading.QuarkusClassLoader @6d4a65c6)
```

protobuf code generated w/ versions < 3.22.0 referenced the `public static` field `com.google.protobuf.LazyStringArrayList#EMPTY`, the static method `emptyList()` is package-protected before 3.22.0.

In 3.22.0 `emptyList()` became `public static` and code generated w/ 3.22.0 references that method.

However, the Quarkus bom enforces protobuf-java to 3.21.9, so code generated w/ 3.22.0 won't be able to access the package-protected method `emptyList()`.

Would it be possible to let the generated code reference the `EMPTY` field at least for a while before switching to `emptyList()`?

Opened an issue on the Quarkus as well: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/31240

hi, I have same error without quarkus, just generating code from protobuf in Kotlin app:

`error: emptyList() is not public in LazyStringArrayList; cannot be accessed from outside package
            com.google.protobuf.LazyStringArrayList.emptyList();`

```
    api(group = "io.grpc", name = "grpc-protobuf", version = "1.53.0")
    api(group = "io.grpc", name = "grpc-stub", version = "1.53.0")
    api(group = "com.google.protobuf", name = "protobuf-kotlin", version = "3.22.0")

```

```

```

@snazy @piotrantosik If I understand correctly, you are creating gencode with protoc 3.22 and attempting to use that with a runtime that predates the 3.22 release? If that is the case, unfortunately, that is not a supported configuration. Gencode from any protobuf release can only be used with its contemporary runtime or a later runtime within the same major version.

If you need to use an older protobuf runtime, you'll need to generate your proto bindings using the protoc from that same release.

Yes, that's exactly the situation. code-gen w/ 3.22.0 and runtime on 3.21.9 (forced dependency).

I see the "supported combination constraint". OTOH it's a tricky situation for users - providing generated classes, but runtimes can do "their own thing" and (forcefully) pin dependencies.

A workaround (that I don't like in general), would be to let people build uber-jars with a relocated protobuf runtime. But then, beside that it's unnecessarily complicated, you get into ugly situations, that users of your shaded runtime cannot "just" bump the runtime (there might be bugfixes or security constraints).

Of course, there is a very tight relationship between the generated code and the runtime (no doubt, it's necessary).
However there are necessarily breaking changes and changes that don't need to break things. In this case (removing the `public` modifier) it wouldn't have to be a breaking change.

The bump to 3.22.0 was merged for Quarkus (not yet released).

We'd love to make this easier but we end up with requests for constraints in both directions:
1. Old gencode + new runtime
2. New gencode + old runtime

If we satisfy both, we can never clean up anything and certain fixes cannot be done.
We settled on supporting old gencode with new runtimes in the same major version line since that enables forward progress while still allowing proto bindings to be pre-compiled as a part of library APIs.  

New gencode with old runtimes really doesn't make as much sense from a support standpoint. It becomes very difficult to reason about what functionality is actually available to the gencode. In most cases, it is ok to stick with a slightly stale protoc for gencode until the runtime can be updated for all the components in the system.

Over the next year or so, we plan to formalize this with a minimum required runtime check in the gencode -- this will cause a breakage whenever there is an attempt to use new gencode with an old runtime (rather than having it appear to work only to fail in mysterious ways later). Mismatches are simply too much of a support burden.

Sorry for the friction, but hopefully this information can be used to plan going forward.
FYI: grpc-java is looking at downgrading to 3.21 to avoid this issue. https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/issues/10202

@RCRedWu No, this is working as intended. You cannot use gencode from a later version of protoc with an older runtime. If you do, the behavior is undefined and likely broken. We are adding explicit checks to prevent unintentional mixing of this type so that you get clear error messages.

@googleberg I think, the above requirement needs to be weakened. title: C# possible incorrect implementation of CreateJsonFieldMap causes JSON data corruption during parse

nodes.body:
Java does the same thing:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/6d776dfed52e36a58f318c0ba3acc93445ed710e/java/util/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/util/JsonFormat.java#L1465-L1476

C# copied a lot from Java so that's not surprising.

Golang appears to always prefer the JSON name:

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go/blob/246af0d153cae8ef4e2915a8d212167ad0751985/encoding/protojson/decode.go#L177-L181

Yes, this looks like a bug to me. I don't know whether protoc catches the situation where there's genuine ambiguity (either with duplicate json_name annotations for different fields, or a json_name that conflicts with an un-annotated field). But where there's a clearly unambiguous mapping (e.g. with your pathological case) it would make sense to follow that. It looks like we probably need to fix this in both C# and Java, and *possibly* do something in protoc.

nodes.body:
Technically `assert` is a macro and not a keyword.  http://go/cppref/cpp/error/assert

This means we have two approaches we could use to solve this.

1) treat it like other macros that have frequent collisions (https://cs.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/cffde99fc6195ca108f320c16a6ded41c42a3317/src/google/protobuf/port_def.inc?q=path%3Aport_def.inc#L950-L953)
2) treat it as a keyword (https://cs.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/cffde99fc6195ca108f320c16a6ded41c42a3317/src/google/protobuf/compiler/cpp/helpers.cc?q=path%3Acpp%2Fhelpers.cc#L89)

I don't particularly love either option.  (1) feels more principled, but users will have a hard time accessing such fields.

Just out of curiosity, what makes the `assert` macro different from the other macros that are being undefined? (https://cs.github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/cffde99fc6195ca108f320c16a6ded41c42a3317/src/google/protobuf/port_def.inc?q=path%3Aport_def.inc#L950-L953)

As in, what makes it more troublesome to undefine `assert` as opposed to the `min` and `max` example?

We actually talked about whether to handle it like a macro or a keyword in the team chat.  We ended up deciding on keyword because the `assert` macro is pulled into a great many headers transitively.  `min` and `max` on the other hand are only defined as macros on windows, so the magnitude of their scope is significantly smaller.

title: descriptor.proto: add cpp_namespace to FileOptions
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
C++

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
There is a way to control the namespace/package for generated code in most languages. But for C++, it always uses the protobuf package as the C++ namespace. This can be problematic when someone wants to generate C++ code for a file they didn't write, and whose author did not pick an appropriate proto package.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Consistent with how code gen works for other languages, I think a `cpp_namespace` field on `google.protobuf.FileOptions` would be sufficient. If present, this would be used _instead of_ the protobuf package. Its value is interpreted the same as protobuf packages: a dot-delimited sequence of identifiers, where each identifier is a namespace enclosed in the namespace for its preceding identifier.

This would be trivial to implement and would be 100% backwards compatible.

**Additional context**
In addition to cases where proto source author chose an inappropriate package (or omitted one), there are other potential reasons to be able to separate the C++ namespace and protobuf package. For example, it is often the advice to _not_ put "proto" or "pb" in the protobuf package name, as that is generally redundant (since it's a protobuf source and a protobuf package). But it also often advised to not mix generated code and hand-written code in the same package/namespace. Since the C++ namespace currently is always equal to the protobuf package, there is an inclination to add "proto" or "pb" to the protobuf package name, just to avoid such mixing. Ideally, the C++ namespace could be de-coupled from the protobuf package, just as (for example) the Go and Java packages are de-coupled from it.

title: Please detect support for large-file-support related build flags and set them automatically
body:
When building for 32-bit architectures like ARM on Linux, off_t is not big enough to represent large files. This leads to system calls like stat and seek failing when called on a large file. If the proper build flags are set, the system calls are replaced with alternatives that support large files.

While this likely won't have an immediate impact on the maximum serialized protobuf, it ought to make the error messages better with respect to large files, and remove an obstacle toward supporting larger maximum protobufs.

nodes.body: Can you say more about what this change would look like? We have not thought a lot about large files on 32-bit architectures. One thing to note is that even if we do this, we're probably not going to support a larger maximum protobuf size any time soon. That would be a big change affecting all languages and would require a lot of thought and planning, and I'm not even sure that it's a feature we would want to pursue.

There is a good explanation of with an example from wireshark on how to enable large file support with CMake: https://stackoverflow.com/a/61343213/1549171

It pretty much just detects if certain compile-time flags are available and if they are, sets them. The consequences of this are off_t is a different size for 32-bit architectures and different system calls are used like lseek64 instead of lseek and fstat64 instead of fstat.

I'm seeing a very similar problem with a slightly different setup. I don't _quite_ have a concise repro yet, but thought it would be worth sharing my investigation in case it helps.

## Environment Details

* Python Environment: `conda` environment with 3.8.16
    * We've seen it against `3.9` and `3.10` as well in Github Actions
* Protobuf Version: `4.23.1`
* Architecture: Running natively on an M1 (arm) Mac
    * I _believe_ the GH Actions workers where we also saw it are x86, so I don't _think_ it's architecture specific

In order to get the segfault to trigger consistently, I slapped (`@pytest.mark.parametrize("run_num", range(100))`) on my offending unit test. With 100 runs, it reliably triggered at _some_ point, but running the test a single time usually did not trigger the fault.

## Setup Details

We're using custom `DescriptorPool` objects in unit tests in order to isolate some dynamic message generation and avoid name collisions. The main difference between our usecase and the OP is that rather than a submessage, we're using a standard message (`struct_pb2.Struct`) that gets copied over to the temporary pool.

The `pytest` fixture looks like this:

```py
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def temp_dpool():
    """Fixture to isolate the descriptor pool used in each test"""
    dpool = descriptor_pool.DescriptorPool()
    global_dpool = descriptor_pool._DEFAULT
    descriptor_pool._DEFAULT = dpool
    fd = descriptor_pb2.FileDescriptorProto()
    struct_pb2.DESCRIPTOR.CopyToProto(fd)
    dpool.Add(fd)
    yield dpool
    descriptor_pool._DEFAULT = global_dpool
```

If I add the following lines before `yield dpool`, the segfault goes away (very similar to OP's commented line)

```py
    mf = MessageFactory(dpool)
    msgs = mf.GetMessages([fd.name])
    _ = msgs["google.protobuf.Struct"]
    _ = msgs["google.protobuf.Value"]
    _ = msgs["google.protobuf.ListValue"]
```

The dynamically generated message that triggers the segfault has a descriptor that looks like:

```
name: "Foo"
field {
  name: "js_dict"
  number: 1
  label: LABEL_OPTIONAL
  type: TYPE_MESSAGE
  type_name: ".google.protobuf.Struct"
}
```

The segfault is triggered when performing a `Foo.js_dict` (`getattr`).

## Investigation Details

In trying to get to the bottom of this, I started poking around in `upb`'s C implementation. This lead to [the implementation of `PyUpb_Message_NewStub`](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/blob/main/python/message.c#L543). Specifically, the call to `PyUpb_Descriptor_GetClass` is returning `NULL`, causing the subsequent line (`(void*)PyType_GenericAlloc((PyTypeObject*)cls, 0)`) to segfault.

What I have yet to figure out is _why_ that class lookup fails. Given the workaround fix suggested by the post and the comments [here](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/blob/main/python/message.c#L186) related to the recursively triggered "present" / "non-present" state of the concrete class, my gut feeling is that somehow the fact that `Struct` is "copied" to the temporary pool can trigger a logic bug where the recursive presence setup doesn't trigger correctly.

Some additional information that _might_ help track down the issue: The current workaround I'm using in our tests looks like the following:

    _ = msgs["google.protobuf.Value"]
    _ = msgs["google.protobuf.ListValue"]
    yield dpool
    descriptor_pool._DEFAULT = global_dpool
```

If I scoop the workaround out of the body of this `fixture` and put it in a standalone function, the segfault returns somewhat-reliably. I say "somewhat" because even with 500x repeats on the offending test, I can only still only rarely get it to repeat on my laptop (M1 Mac), but it somehow seems to trigger very reliably in GitHub Actions (see [these runs](https://github.com/caikit/caikit/actions/runs/5146459517))

```py
def proto_segfault_workaround(fd, dpool):
    mf = MessageFactory(dpool)
    msgs = mf.GetMessages([fd.name])
    _ = msgs["google.protobuf.Struct"]
    _ = msgs["google.protobuf.Value"]
    _ = msgs["google.protobuf.ListValue"]

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def temp_dpool():
    """Fixture to isolate the descriptor pool used in each test"""
    dpool = descriptor_pool.DescriptorPool()

    descriptor_pool._DEFAULT = dpool
    fd = descriptor_pb2.FileDescriptorProto()

    dpool.Add(fd)

    proto_segfault_workaround(fd, dpool)
    yield dpool

```

title: Can't access custom FieldOptions in Python

nodes.body: This most likely indicates that your plugin doesn't know about the custom options and is therefore treating them as unknown fields. If you have your plugin take a dependency on the generated code for `my_opt` then it should be able to parse that option successfully.

Custom options (`my_opt` in this case) are declared in the proto file and come inside the same request, I can see them on the FileDescriptorProto level. They are parsed by the same `plugin_pb2.CodeGeneratorRequest.FromString` call as the rest of the request. 

Standard python plugin somehow manages to put options inside the message descriptor, but apparently it parses the request, registers all extensions, and then re-parses it. I'm not 100% sure I can do this in pure python. Probably it's possible to create `FieldDescriptor` from each `FieldDescriptorProto`, but this doesn't feel like a correct way of doing this. 

>If you have your plugin take a dependency on the generated code for my_opt

There is no generated code at that point, only the protoc request. Otherwise it will require first generating classes using the standard generator, and then re-generating same classes using the custom generator.

Why does the plugin need to know about this option? I was assuming it configured some aspect of the plugin's behavior, but if the plugin doesn't know about it until runtime then presumably that is not the case. If you just need to include the option in the generated code then you can include the serialized bytes without needing to interpret them.

If for some reason you do need to interact with the fully-parsed options, I think the way to do it would be to do the equivalent of `DynamicMessage` from C++ and Java. I'm less familiar with Python but I believe the Python way to do it is with `message_factory.GetMessageClass(descriptor)`, which allows you to generate a message based on a descriptor which is not known until runtime. If you then parse the options using that dynamic message (built from descriptors from the CodeGeneratorRequest), then you should be able to see the custom options there.

>Why does the plugin need to know about this option

To give more context, I'm trying to write an alternative codegen plugin to generate proto-plus code. So far it all works well except for custom options. For my current case, option values will be static, but I still need to know them beforehand to generate the code properly.

So far the only working solution I've found is kinda similar to the standard codegen - parse, register, re-parse.

```python3
req = plugin_pb2.CodeGeneratorRequest.FromString(data)
for file in req.proto_file:
    for ext in file.extension:
        descriptor_pb2.FieldOptions.RegisterExtension(FieldDescriptor(...))
req = plugin_pb2.CodeGeneratorRequest.FromString(data)
```

I'll try to check if it'd look better with dynamic messages, but I guess in the end the mechanism would be pretty similar to just re-parsing the proto file.

To summarize, I guess my issue is resolved, i'll stick with the parse-register-reparse solution as it makes the plugin code easy to understand (with some comments added).

Still, imo from the user perspective it's not immediately obvious why some things like messages are being parsed properly on the first run, and some other things like extensions require some extra steps, so it honestly feels like a bug, or at least an undocumented design decision.

title: Provide access to unknown field information when parsing text format
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
No syntax wouldn't change, but the text format parsers and the representation of unknown fields for all languages would be changed.

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**

I am trying to give code the ability to introspect unknown field information after parsing a proto text format. Currently, that information is at most logged when parsing text format, whereas when ingesting wire format the unknown fields are available for introspection.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I would like unknown field structs to be augmented with fields for the field name and value as read from the text proto and for this information to be populated when parsing text protos when unknown fields are encountered. The "value" could be strongly-typed to the one that the text proto parsers currently "guess"; although perhaps it should be less strongly-typed to one of {string, list<string>, map<string, object>}.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

A mode in which a text proto can be parsed without a schema into a map/dictionary.

**Additional context**

None

nodes.body: This would require keeping two distinct flavors of "unknown fields" (text and number based) on all of our platforms.  It would further lead to ambiguities if both are set and the name and number were for the same field (had one known the schema).  Given the volume of ambiguities to resolve and that it would need to be implemented in many languages I don't think this is a feature we are likely to add

@fowles, what do you think about providing access to the unknown fields from a getter on the TextFormat Parser object? This would not be the same "unknown field" type that's part of messages today; it would be the one used internally to the TextFormat parser, augmented to also contain the value of the field. Thoughts?
That is a very interesting proposal, that I would be willing to entertain on a per language basis.

It was determined that this would not be a good idea, because it would essentially allow textproto to function like an unstructured markup language. There is other work in motion that should better address my original use case.

title: Complicated versioning schema between various languages
body:
As I see, at the time the following rules apply:

* C++ protobuf releases version numbered `{major}.{minor}`
* Python protobuf adds `4.` prefix to the versions (so git tag `v21.12` becomes [4.21.12](https://pypi.org/project/protobuf/4.21.12/) on pypi).
* Java add `3.` prefix to the versions (hence git tag `v21.12` becomes [3.21.12](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/com.google.protobuf/protobuf-java/3.21.12).

In order to correspond to various versioning schemas, git tags also get multiplied, i. e. [v22.0](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/tree/v22.0), [v3.22.0](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/tree/v3.22.0) and [v4.22.0](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/tree/v4.22.0) do actually point to the same commit [a847a8d](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/commit/a847a8dc4ba1d99e7ba917146c84438b4de7d085).

Is there any rationale behind this schema?
Do you have plans to unify the versioning?

nodes.body:
This was a deliberate shift to allow language bindings to evolve independently.  This was announced at https://protobuf.dev/news/2022-05-06/#versioning

The alternatives were 

* bump major versions when *any* language needed a breaking change 
* not bump major versions when *some* language did have a breaking change.
* never making breaking changes

All of these were unacceptable for various reasons, so here we are.

We should give this a dedicated space in our docs (not just the announcement section), so I will leave this bug open to track that.

The problem is that making per-language versioning independent actually did not achieved this.

Code generation is still being done by C++ version of protoc which get released according to C++ versioning schema (i. e. _every release is a breaking change_).

Python bindings for protobuf still depend on a pyext (and have harsh performance if build without one).
As I am maintaining protobuf updates in our monorepo, I will indeed appreciate a doc section on this .

https://protobuf.dev/support/version-support/ covers our versioning schema. If this doesn't fully address the things raised in this issue, please reopen this and provide a delta so that I know what you'd like to see added/changed. Thanks.

Doing the following in a M1 mac:
```
curl -LO https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/download/v23.3/protoc-23.3-osx-universal_binary.zip
unzip protoc-23.3-osx-universal_binary.zip -d protobuf
./protobuf/bin/protoc --version
```

Results in:
```
libprotoc 23.3
```

@Logofile is this expected?
That output seems correct, yes. Were you expecting something different? If so, what and why?

@Logofile, it is out internal problem, everything is correct with the protobuf.
However it would be more convenient for us, if `protoc` binary was produced by the linker, and `protoc-${version}` would be symlinked to it.

title: Fast conversion RepeatedScalarFieldContainer to numpy array
body:

NOTE: this form is for feature requests (including cleanup requests) only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->


**What language does this apply to?**
this is about the generated code change for python.

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
Fast conversion from RepeatedScalarFieldContainer to numpy array

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I want a fast conversion from RepeatedScalarFieldContainer to a numpy array. I have several messages which contain repeated data int32 array. Example of how I convert to a numpy array:

`data_array = np.array(person.data)`

title: The behavior that emit fields with default values in JSON encoding has discrepancy between proto2 optional and proto3 optional
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only.
For questions or troubleshooting, please post on the protobuf mailing list:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf 
Stack Overflow is also a useful if unofficial resource https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/protocol-buffers
-->

Related to https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/1525.

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v3.21.12
Language: Go/C++/Java

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Mac

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Go: 1.20.1
C++: Apple clang version 14.0.0 (clang-1400.0.29.202)
Java: openjdk version "19.0.2"

**What did you do?**

Marshal proto message contains optional fields to json.

proto2:
```protobuf
syntax = "proto2";

package com.example.foo;

option go_package = "example.com/main";

option java_package = "com.example.foo";
option java_outer_classname = "FooProtos2";

message Foo2 {
  optional string foo = 1;
}
```

proto3:
```protobuf
syntax = "proto3";

package com.example.foo;

option go_package = "example.com/main";

option java_package = "com.example.foo";
option java_outer_classname = "FooProtos3";

message Foo3 {
  optional string foo = 1;
}
```

Generate sources:
```
protoc *.proto --go_out . --go_opt paths=source_relative --java_out=app/src/main/java --cpp_out=.
```

Go:
```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"
)

func main() {
	marshaller := &protojson.MarshalOptions{EmitUnpopulated: true}

	foo2 := &Foo2{}
	b2, _ := marshaller.Marshal(foo2)
	fmt.Printf("%s\n", b2)

	foo3 := &Foo3{}
	b3, _ := marshaller.Marshal(foo3)
	fmt.Printf("%s\n", b3)
}

```

C++:
```c++
#include <google/protobuf/util/json_util.h>
#include "foo_proto2.pb.h"
#include "foo_proto3.pb.h"

int main()
{
  google::protobuf::util::JsonPrintOptions options;
  options.always_print_primitive_fields = true;

  std::string json2;
  com::example::foo::Foo2 foo2;
  MessageToJsonString(foo2, &json2, options);
  std::cout << json2 << std::endl;

  std::string json3;
  com::example::foo::Foo3 foo3;
  MessageToJsonString(foo3, &json3, options);
  std::cout << json3 << std::endl;
}
```

Java:
```java
package com.example.foo;

import com.example.foo.FooProtos2.Foo2;
import com.example.foo.FooProtos3.Foo3;
import com.google.protobuf.util.JsonFormat;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        JsonFormat.Printer printer = JsonFormat.printer().includingDefaultValueFields().omittingInsignificantWhitespace();

        Foo2 foo2 = Foo2.newBuilder().build();
        System.out.println(printer.print(foo2));

        Foo3 foo3 = Foo3.newBuilder().build();
        System.out.println(printer.print(foo3));
    }
}
```

Run All.


**What did you expect to see**

```
{"foo":null}
{"foo":null}
```

**What did you see instead?**

```
{"foo":null}
{}
```

This behavior seems to be due to that proto3 optional is implemented as oneof with a single type, but there is discrepancy between proto2 and proto3. Is this intended behavior?

nodes.body:
+1 I'd love it if messagetodict/json would include unset optional fields, e.g. in python the field would be in the dict/json but would be set to `None` (null).

The docs (https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/proto3/#specifying_field_rules) say:

> the field is unset, and will return the default value.

Except, with message to json does not return the default value, it returns nothing at all!

I am also facing the same problem and as a work around, I am removing the `omitempty` tag and using `encoding/json` package to marshal the GO proto struct to JSON. This work around is an antipattern as mentioned by @dsnet in some of thread but there is no other solution to be able to include `null` value fields in the output JSON.

This behavior causes confusion among API users and hinders data processing on the front end. 

I would greatly appreciate guidance or updates from the Protocol Buffers team to resolve this issue, as it aligns with the specifications of protobuf.

title: protoc: trailing comment on last line of file (with no subsequent newline) ignored
body:
Apparently I introduced a bug in #10660. 🤦

If the last line in the file has a trailing comment and no trailing newline, that comment is effectively ignored (it gets interpreted as a detached comment before the EOF instead of a trailing comment on the preceding token).

Here's a simple example:

```protobuf
syntax = "proto3";
package foo.bar; // trailing comment on package.
```

Importantly, if the file above _has no trailing newline_ (i.e. the last byte in the file is the period of the trailing comment), then that comment does not make it into source code info. One would expect it to be a trailing comment for the package statement.

title: [c++] SerializeAsString() generates a string containing non-UTF8 chars. How to solve it?

nodes.body: I believe that this behaviour is expected. `std::string` doesn't know anything about UTF8, it's just a glorified array of `char`s, and `char` is guaranteed to be single-byte. `SerializeToString` writes binary data, `std::string` is simply used as a convenient container for it.

You completely missed the part where I said that the data produced by the method is binary. You should pick an appropriate data type for the table columns too, `text` won't work.

Alternatively, if a human-readable representation is absolutely necessary, then look into the [JSON utilities](https://protobuf.dev/reference/cpp/api-docs/google.protobuf.util.json_util/).

> You should pick an appropriate data type for the table columns too, `text` won't work.

@v-chernyshev - I see. So what data type should I choose for `private_pb` field of `xms_service_config` table?

The following is my SQL statement of creating `xms_service_config` table:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `xms_service_config`
(
    `id`            INT AUTO_INCREMENT,
    `service_name`  VARCHAR(16),
    `service_port`  INT,
    `service_ip`    VARCHAR(16),
    `private_pb`    VARCHAR(4096),

Any idea or suggestion?

That `TypeError` probably turns into a `DeprecationWarning` if you update to a more recent 3.12 that contains https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/103972.  it'll become an actual error in Python 3.14.  The metaclasses `tp_new` is ignored.

IMO, the DeprecationWarning is correct, because the behaviour in Python 3.11 is buggy -- though the bug might be harmless in protobuf's case.

protobuf uses `PyType_FromSpecWithBases` to create [`ScalarMapContainer`](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/242771ad159927cf731f30c1379aaef1913d7b1e/python/google/protobuf/pyext/map_container.cc#L919) and [`MessageMapContainer`](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/242771ad159927cf731f30c1379aaef1913d7b1e/python/google/protobuf/pyext/map_container.cc#L926), which derive from `collections.abc.MutableMapping`, so their metaclass is `abc.ABCMeta`.

I believe (but didn't check, compiling/testing `protobuf` is out of my league at the moment) that `abc.ABCMeta.__new__` was not called on these container types, even in Python 3.11.
They seem to be abstract bases that are never instantiated, so the setup that `abc.ABCMeta.__new__` does *could* turn to to not be necessary -- but that would be a fragile assumption to make.
So, the current (3.11) behaviour is unsafe, hence, a `DeprecationWarning` for it.

What to do? I wish I had a good answer.
I guess the correct workaround for `protobuf` is to derive a `ScalarMapContainerBase_Type` from `object` (using `PyType_FromSpecWithBases`), and derive then `ScalarMapContainer_Type` from that *and* `MutableMapping` (with a call to the metaclass, that is, `Py_TYPE(mutable_mapping)`). That should work correctly (that is, set the ABC metadata) even in Python 3.11.

Or, if you're sure you're not skipping anything important, temporarily set `Py_TYPE(mutable_mapping)->tp_new = Py_TYPE(&PyType_Type)->tp_new;`. That's a nasty hack, but... if you do want the previous nasty behaviour, it rather clearly shows what that is.

You might want to follow https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/103968 for a bit before implementing my suggestions.

```
I looked at protobuf.
...
I don't know what the correct general solution is, but IMO, the current behaviour is worth deprecating.
```

And as the TypeError has turned into DeprecationWarning in more recent 3.12. We may want to wait until https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/103968 is resolved and have a correct general solution before get rid of the Warning. Please correct me if I was wrong, @encukou

That's right.
Unfortunately, it looks like the general solution is pretty vague, with several options that all have downsides :(
The draft is here: https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/105698/files

I didn't include the ideas from above, one is specific to protobuf (ABCs) and the other is too hacky. But they should work.

I left some thoughts about this in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/103968#issuecomment-1589928055

TL;DR: I don't think we want to actually run `tp_new` from `abc.ABCMeta` on `{Scalar,Message}MapContainer`, because we do not want our classes to have a `register()` method.

We just want to mix in `MutableMapping` without adding any class methods. We may just want to remove the inheritance and do something like:

class ScalarMapContainer:

I think this python/cpython#98963

The only docstrings ever set via a `_FieldProperty` constructor in `python_message.py` are of the generic form:

```python
doc = 'Magic attribute generated for "%s" proto field.' % proto_field_name
```

which does not sound meaningfully informative.

I suspect we could just stop passing doc=doc to the property super class constructor in [the `_FieldProperty` constructor](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/python/google/protobuf/internal/python_message.py#L611)?

```diff
-    property.__init__(self, getter, setter, doc=doc)
+    super().__init__(getter, setter)
```

For whatever reasons... that doesn't really work. What I think I'm seeing so far is that 3.12 a class inheriting from property cannot use `__slots__`. I'm narrowing this down and if that is true will file an upstream issue.
Okay, we've restored the no-AttributeError behavior upstream, 3.12beta2 should include [the fix](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/105297).

As _FieldProperty instance docstrings are silently never set anyways, I do recommend that the protobuf code simplify itself and not bother constructing and passing the meaningless doc= parameter in python_message.py:

```diff
-  doc = 'Magic attribute generated for "%s" proto field.' % proto_field_name
-  setattr(cls, property_name, _FieldProperty(field, getter, setter, doc=doc))
+  setattr(cls, property_name, _FieldProperty(field, getter, setter))
```

I tried to remove doc=doc but it raises:
```
  File "/third_party/py/google/protobuf/internal/python_message.py", line 651, in _AddPropertiesForRepeatedField
    setattr(cls, property_name, _FieldProperty(field, getter, setter))
  File "/third_party/py/google/protobuf/internal/python_message.py", line 607, in __init__
    property.__init__(self, getter, setter)
AttributeError: '_FieldProperty' object attribute '__doc__' is read-only
```

Will close this issue as python team has restored the no-AttributeError behavior upstream. Python 3.12beta2 and above will not have this issue.

Feel free to reopen if this is not fixed after Python 3.12beta2

title: Service descriptor cross-contamination in UPB implementation

nodes.body:
Confirmed. We are looking up symbol names in the `upb_DefPool`, but not checking to make sure they match this file: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/upb/blob/df93cf65a2957bd0921462cb9d055c5b82a6d68b/python/descriptor.c#L1126-L1148

This should be relatively easy to fix. We just need to add checks that the returned symbols are from this file.

We triage inactive PRs and issues in order to make it easier to find active work. If this issue should remain active or becomes active again, please add a comment.

This issue is labeled `inactive` because the last activity was over 90 days ago.
This is for sure still an open issue!

Because of this issue (and other problems linking against protobuf 22.x which now depends on abseil) I'll be packaging v21.12 for [Chimera Linux](https://chimera-linux.org/). From what I could test all v22.x (including v22.3) releases have a broken system-wide installation as of today.

I hope these protobuf/abseil issues are solved in a future release so system-wide installations (like in any Linux distribution packaging) work without requiring hacks like starting to define various `abseil` libraries to link manually without explicitly using them in some project, packagers having to hack on `protobuf.pc.cmake` to attempt bringing in the now required abseil stuff etc.

Fwiw https://github.com/nmeum/android-tools is what required bringing in protobuf in my case.

I should note that other distributions also seem to be stuck on the older version 21.12 presumably due to seeing similar problems, see [Arch Linux](https://archlinux.org/packages/extra/x86_64/protobuf/), [Alpine Linux](https://pkgs.alpinelinux.org/package/edge/main/x86_64/protobuf), [Void Linux](https://voidlinux.org/packages/?arch=x86_64&q=protobuf), [Debian](https://packages.debian.org/source/sid/protobuf), [openSUSE](https://software.opensuse.org/package/protobuf)

title: Question: How to compile protobuf at runtime in Java?
body:
I am dynamically fetching a protobuf in my application. I have the protobuf as a String. Now I want to compile it and get a Java class object corresponding to this protobuf. i.e., I am looking to do the equivalent of:

```
$ protoc --java_out=core/src/main/java -I../src
../src/google/protobuf/descriptor.proto
```

inside my Java application. I am looking for a method:

```
Class<> c = compileProto(protoAsString);
```

Thanks.

title: text format's "expanded Any syntax" does not accept all valid messages

nodes.body:
One thing possibly interesting to note is that many implementations allow whitespace (and comments) in between components of the URL. For example, the following is allowed:
```
[ type . googleapis . com /  google . protobuf . FileDescriptorSet ]: <
  file: [ <name: "foo.proto"> ]
>
```
Given how many of the tokenizer implementations work, an implementation of the above grammar would similarly allow whitespace and comments around all characters that are punctuation. This might be worth changing, as it is confusing that whitespace (and comments) can be freely inserted in so many places where it would not be allowed by an actual URL parser. However, such a change would not be backwards compatible, so maybe not worth thinking about.

Thanks for the detailed write-up and all of the research and testing that went into putting it together. This is really helpful. I'll work with mcy@ to address this discrepancy in the docs and/or upstream in the language code.

title: v1.29.0 contains a breaking change to encoding/protowire.Number.IsValid
body:
In v1.29.0, the `IsValid()` method on `encoding/protowire.Number` was changed to no longer return `false` for tag values between `FirstReservedNumber` and `LastReservedNumber`, inclusive.  See [this commit](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go/commit/31a59208116ee2cacd5b3e4f64cf17ad733e18db).  This change in exported behavior triggered test failures in my code.

When I checked the release notes for v1.29.0 there was no mention of this breaking change.

I was able to change my code because I didn't have anything that actually relied on the previous behavior (the tests were for completeness more than functional requirements) but I thought it worth calling out the lack of mention.

nodes.body: Did you intend this issue to be in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go rather than https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf?

I did.  In my defense, there's no _Issues_ tab available for me there so I clicked the _Create Project Issue_ link on [protobuf.dev](https://protobuf.dev), which brought me here.

Do you know how I can create the issue in the correct place?
I don't, I'm afraid - it may even be that this repo *is* the right place. I'll contact one of the Protobuf Go team and ask them to weigh in.

Thanks for reporting this issue.

Sorry for the breakage. We were not aware that this would break code. This change was necessary to allign with the protobuf language specification. 

I updated the release notes to include this as a breaking change (it was mentioned under Alignment with protobuf so far).
fwiw - issues should be reported in the old repo - https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues as per the readme, https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go#reporting-issues

> This change was necessary to allign with the protobuf language specification.

From the proto3 guide on protobuf.dev: "You also cannot use the numbers 19000 through 19999."  One could argue that it was correct before where `IsValid()` was returning `false` for tag values in that range.  I realize I'm splitting hairs a bit, but from a Semantic Versioning and API compatibility standpoint this was 100% a breaking change.

Like I said before, I was able to fix my code because the failing tests were there for completeness (those values were not allowed so I had tests that verified that constraint held) so it's not really a big deal.
I see. Thanks for the feedback. I'll bring this up with the team and figure out if we can do better in the future.

I discussed this with the team and we came up with the following conclusion.

You are right and if we would follow semantic versioning strictly this would require a new version.

However, we think that the costs of a new version are not worth the benefits.
There are [very few users](https://cs.github.com/?scopeName=All+repos&scope=&q=google.golang.org%2Fprotobuf%2Fencoding%2Fprotowire+lang%3Ago+%2FNumber.*%5C.IsValid%5C%28%2F) of this API.
Introducing a new major version requires users to update their code to depend on the new major version or they are stuck with the old version.
Since we do not have the capacity to maintain two version we would only maintain the newer version.

In other words, we think that the current decision is a net-positive for the Go protobuf ecosystem as whole even if it means we do not strictly adhere to semantic version.  We will follow this principle for future will submit minor breaking changes without declaring a new major version.

That's certainly your decision to make.  I just wanted to bring it up because it is, in fact, a breaking change and the kind of thing that the Go Modules guidance tells us should be a major version bump.  It's also a subtle breaking change because it won't cause any build failures, it will just behave differently at runtime.

At the very least it needs to be called out in the release notes.

title: Regression: Latest protobuf version doesn't work with unittest.mock. Older versions work.
body:
I have created a repo containing all of the files and a couple of scripts to reproduce this [here](https://github.com/BenWhetton/protobuf-mocks). You'll see that `run.py` in v3.19.4 works whereas the one in v4.22.1 doesn't

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v4.22.1
Language: Python

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Ubuntu 20.04

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
Python 3.8.10 (but also seen on 3.9.5, 3.9.9)

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Mock at protobuf class using `unittest.mock.Mock` and try to access
```
a = Mock(MessageType)
a.<someattribute>
```

**What did you expect to see**
The attribute should be present on the mock.

**What did you see instead?**
AttributeError: Mock object has no attribute 'someattribute'

nodes.body: This also happens for me when upgrading protobuf from v3.20.3 to v4.21.12. So it must be something introduced in v4.21 that cause this regression.

Sorry for the lack of response on this issue.

This appears to arise because Protobuf 4.21+ now implements field access via `msg.__getatttr__` rather than using descriptors (`msg.field.__get__`) like the previous implementation did.

The new design saves memory by creating fewer objects, but one side effect is that it can no longer be mocked through `unittest.mock`.

We don't generally recommend that people mock protobuf objects. Protos are dumb data containers, not objects with behavior. It's best to just treat them as dumb containers.

Thanks for the info.

I think this design decision might have had another very unergonomic side-effect: since this change was made, message fields can no longer be inspected in the debugger (at least in pycharm), the only way to see what a field contains is to execute `msg.some_field.some_nested_field` etc., and auto-complete no longer works, so we have to remember/copy-paste/cross-reference the names of all nested fields. In pdb, running `dir(msg)` no longer includes the field names, so I doubt this issue is PyCharm specific.

This is very very painful compared to before. I imagine your internal users probably have tooling to help with this? Is there any way that it can be improved for those of us who are on the outside?

Perhaps I should open another ticket for that issue?

Is pycharm able to use `.pyi` files to discover attribute names?

Generally our strategy has been to optimize the core library and generated code primarily for performance (CPU, memory, etc) and rely on the `.pyi` files to give good DevX (autocomplete, etc).

> Is pycharm able to use `.pyi` files to discover attribute names?

I imagine it could, and I will probably open a request for this, but there will inevitably be a delay in this kind of change making it into users hands, assuming it gets prioritised.

> Generally our strategy has been to optimize the core library and generated code primarily for performance (CPU, memory, etc) and rely on the `.pyi` files to give good DevX (autocomplete, etc).

I see the logic behind that; however, there are trade-offs involved, and different stakeholders might choose different trade-offs in cases like this. Python is a language that is typically chosen for being easy to use and learn. Users accept that they are not getting C performance when they pick the language, and that features generally are not cost-free. I obviously don't know what the exact rationale was behind this choice, and how much of a performance benefit it provides, but I doubt it's a trade-off I would choose without having access to tooling which maintains a good developer experience. In this particular case, it feels to me like google's incentives (at least 7/11 of the listed members of the protocol buffers project) may be a bit misaligned with a large proportion of the external users.

Do you/have you considered informing/collaborating with tooling providers to ensure that they can adapt to significant changes like this to avoid deteriorating the developer experience of many external users?

Optimization of the core library is in response to user feedback. Some users process large payloads in Python, and they expect to get good performance even when querying large datasets.

We use SemVer so that users are in control of when they are exposed to breaking changes like this. This change occurred between 3.x and 4.x; users who are affected can stay on 3.x until the tooling catches up wrt. `.pyi` support.

title: 21.x and 22.x versions are missing from maven central
body: I see from #9725, #10568 and others that this seems to be a recurring issue.

nodes.body: The issues you linked are old and I thought they were fixed. Can you provide more details here? Which package/version is missing?

According to mvnrepository for [protobuf-java](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/com.google.protobuf/protobuf-java) and [protoc](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/com.google.protobuf/protoc) the last available version is 3.22.2. The entire 21.x and 22.x branches seems to be missing.

This may be a misunderstanding of our new [versioning system](https://protobuf.dev/support/version-support/). The newest version of java is 3.22.0. The 22 in 22.x refers to the minor version since we have moved to language-specific major versions.

title: MessageToDict BUG
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for bug reports only.
For questions or troubleshooting, please post on the protobuf mailing list:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf 
Stack Overflow is also a useful if unofficial resource https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/protocol-buffers
-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: google.protobuf.json_format __version__ = '4.22.1'
Language: Python 3.9.6

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**

macOS 13.2 (22D49) (M2)

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

Python 3.9.6

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. `demo.proto`

```protobuf
syntax = "proto3";

package demo.v1;

service Demo {
  rpc Get(Req) returns (Spec) {}
}

message Req {}

message Spec {
  int64 a = 1;
  string b = 3;
  int32  c = 4;
  double d = 5;
}
```

2. gen python code

> grpcio                  1.51.3
> grpcio-tools            1.51.3

```bash
python3 -m grpc_tools.protoc -I . --python_out=. --grpc_python_out=. ./*.proto
```

3. `server.py`

```python
from concurrent import futures
import time

import grpc

import demo_pb2
import demo_pb2_grpc


class DemoServicer(demo_pb2_grpc.DemoServicer):
    def Get(self, request, context):
        return demo_pb2.Spec(a=11, b="22", c=33, d=44.3)


def serve():
    server = grpc.server(futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10))
    demo_pb2_grpc.add_DemoServicer_to_server(DemoServicer(), server)
    server.add_insecure_port('[::]:50051')
    print("start on 50051...")
    server.start()
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(3600)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        server.stop(0)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    serve()
```

4. `client.py`

```python
import grpc
from google.protobuf.json_format import MessageToDict

import demo_pb2
import demo_pb2_grpc


def run():
    channel = grpc.insecure_channel('localhost:50051')
    stub = demo_pb2_grpc.DemoStub(channel)
    req = demo_pb2.Req()
    response = stub.Get(req)
    print(
        {
            'resp.a': response.a,
            'type': type(response.a),
        },
        {
            'resp.b': response.b,
            'type': type(response.b),
        },
        {
            'resp.c': response.c,
            'type': type(response.c),
        },
        {
            'resp.d': response.d,
            'type': type(response.d),
        }
    )
    d = MessageToDict(response, including_default_value_fields=True)
    print(
        {
            'dict.a': d['a'],
            'type': type(d['a']),
        },
        {
            'dict.b': d['b'],
            'type': type(d['b']),
        },
        {
            'dict.c': d['c'],
            'type': type(d['c']),
        },
        {
            'dict.d': d['d'],
            'type': type(d['d']),
        }
    )


if __name__ == '__main__':
    run()
```

5. `python3 server.py` -> `python3 client.py` -> output:

```bash
{'resp.a': 11, 'type': <class 'int'>} {'resp.b': '22', 'type': <class 'str'>} {'resp.c': 33, 'type': <class 'int'>} {'resp.d': 44.3, 'type': <class 'float'>}
{'dict.a': '11', 'type': <class 'str'>} {'dict.b': '22', 'type': <class 'str'>} {'dict.c': 33, 'type': <class 'int'>} {'dict.d': 44.3, 'type': <class 'float'>}
```

6. the variable `a` is of type `str`.

```
{'dict.a': '11', 'type': <class 'str'>}
```

**What did you expect to see**

```
{'dict.a': '11', 'type': <class 'int'>}
```

`a` should be of type `int`, so `MessageToDict` function has a bug.

I think the bug is here:

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/244b245002270ee699dce8d80b8984844d7fc97f/python/google/protobuf/json_format.py#L304

title: The "cmake/CMakeLists.txt -> CMakeLists.txt" redirection deactivates some policies silently.
body:
The "cmake/CMakeLists.txt" is now deprecated, but there are some hidden problems with how it's forwarding to /CMakeLists.txt (in the repo root).

I found that some cmake policies get silently deactivated if one uses cmake/CMakeLists.txt

E.g. here:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/244b245002270ee699dce8d80b8984844d7fc97f/CMakeLists.txt#L10

Since `CMP0091` needs to be set before languages are initialized, but https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/244b245002270ee699dce8d80b8984844d7fc97f/cmake/CMakeLists.txt#L5 is reached first, the policy won't be active (which is quite counterintuitive)
and settings made here https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/244b245002270ee699dce8d80b8984844d7fc97f/CMakeLists.txt#L233 will be overridden by e.g. `/MD` still being present in CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_*

(at least this is my interpretation of what happens, but I've observed `/MD` flag being present when it should not).

nodes.body: Yes, protobuf now requires abseil as announced [here](https://protobuf.dev/news/2022-08-03/#abseil-dep). You need to install absl and set the `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` flag to where you have absl installed.

@deannagarcia Yes, I know and installed abseil before the protobuf build. Protobuf installs successfully, but problems come when I try to build an execution target with a link to a shared library that uses protobuf:

`execution querySubmiter` -> `shared libdrillClient.so` -> `static libprotobuf.a`

During `querySubmiter` linking to `drillClient` there are occurs `undefined reference to` errors, that I already mentioned above:
```

...
```

All those errors are related with `abseil` and `utf8_range` (`utf8_validity`). 
I'm not familiar with cmake and c++ build, so I'm not sure how actually works linking, but do I need to add links on `abseil` and `ut8_range` to my shared library that uses protobuf to make it work correctly?

I was able to solve errors when linked `drillClient` to `abseil` and `utf8_range` in the following way:
```

...

But it doesn't look like it is a right way of how it should be fixed. 
Could you, please, explain, are `utf8_range` and `abseil` required to be linked to now in a shared library that uses rpotobuf?

Yes, if you use a shared library that uses protobuf you will need to provide an `abseil` dependency. Your solution of packaging the shared library with `abseil` would fix it, but if you want to keep the library without any statically linked dependencies you will need to add the `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` flag to your cmake build as mentioned earlier with the path to where you installed abseil.

body:

-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
