Hello, I have a issue about the generated java codes.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?
Yes. The problem is caused by the builder method naming convention in the jar file that created. As you know, the repeated fields in the proto file take "List" suffix at the end of the getter method. But the adder methods doesn't have this suffix. Because of this naming convention mapstruct cannot map the classes if there are more than one lists of the same type (if there is only one list of the same type, it can be match by the type). 

We can look with some sample codes:
![image](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/assets/86795767/cf3f87e6-2fae-49f1-9fcc-c97fd1e93592)
Using this proto file I compiled a jar. And the jar contains following codes.
![image](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/assets/86795767/fb990019-f30c-43c7-b5b5-6d0c74152e4b)
![image](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/assets/86795767/5aa9c199-2805-4305-96bb-3ba2cdd15741)
(Also, same methods for items2List and samplesList)

Then I created this java class:
![image](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/assets/86795767/d60ce8c9-4dec-4e9b-92f0-75f4087d3c55)

Now, when I try to map HelloRequestInboundDto to ExternalProto.HelloRequest as the following:
![image](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/assets/86795767/f28dab3d-f32d-4d2c-a0cd-b449e406a783)

The generated code:
![image](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/assets/86795767/4fd22b3f-0637-4859-aa0f-f577c00bb761)

The problem here is this. Because of the naming convention of grpc-java builder methods adder methods of the fields doesn't match (fields have "List" suffix like items1List, items2List, samplesList but the adder methods doesn't have List suffix like addItems1, addItems2, addSamples and they don't match). When add methods and the fields don't match it tries to get the list and add all items to that list. But this mapping throws exception because getter method of the list returns unmodifiableList and when it tries to add items to that list it throws UnsupportedOperationException. Notice the samplesList mapping is what is suppose to be (it uses adder method of the class not getter) because there is only one kind of adder method that accepts Sample type.


### Describe the solution you'd like
To solve that problem the first thing comes to mind add "List" suffix to add method names. This way field names and the adder method names match and there would be no problem. For example, the filed name is items1List, getter method is already named getItems1List so we can change addItems1 to addItems1List. I copied the jar contents and made this change and it works.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
Also, there is another alternative. If you wouldn't want to change existing method names, this solves the problem too. It's about setter methods. Currently, builder methods only have setter for single item in the list. 
Example:
![image](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/assets/86795767/6958d7e2-8ba6-4db4-9532-da487b85258a)

But also there could be setter for the whole list in the builder. Since builder methods only used in the creation of the object, it would totally be okay to have such method. Also, it has to named with "List" suffix.
It could be something like this:
![image](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/assets/86795767/cc5c3c2c-fc24-4d33-8418-f133212dc173)

### Additional context
There are issues opened for this in mapstruct but it uses exact match for field name (getter method) and setter or adder method so, I think this issue suppose to be handled here. There is a inconsistency here and "List" suffix could be added adder and setter methods or it could be removed from the getter methods altogether.

nodes.body:
Making that syntax change for a core feature like list setters would break way too many users, so that unfortunately isn't really an option.

However, protobuf does already provide a setter that allows you to set the whole list with the `addAlll` prefix. You can see that documented, along with the other repeated methods [here](https://protobuf.dev/reference/java/java-generated/#repeated). Can you use that?

Yes I have seen those addAll methods but they also doesn't have "List" suffix like addAllItems1List(). If we write custom mappings we can use any add or addAll methods but in default protoc and mapstuct doesn't compatible in multiple list scenario. Both libraries are used widely. So, I think they should be compatible by default. 

Making that syntax change on existing methods would be a breaking change that I agree. However, I think adding setter for list methods should be okey (see the Describe alternatives you've considered section). Currently there is addAll for manipulation for whole list but there is no setter available for this. There is only setter for elements of the list. If a setter method were added with "List" suffix at the end that would fix the issue. And since we don't change anything already existed, it wouldn't break anything.

When adding new methods, protobuf would need to add them for all languages as we try to keep languages as similar as possible. While this naming might not be ideal for java in the specific context of mapstructs, overall our naming works best for the set of languages we support and adding a new setter to every repeated field isn't feasible.

I found this [issue](https://github.com/mapstruct/mapstruct/issues/743) in mapstruct that details this issue and provides workarounds that may be helpful.

title: Y10K timestamp issue
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for feature requests (including cleanup requests) only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->


**What language does this apply to?**
proto3

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
Note that the timestamp supported by google.protobuf.Timestamp only goes up to the year 9999:

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/src/google/protobuf/timestamp.proto#L53-L55

We have some time to fix this, but I believe it's responsible to open an issue for it. As we continue to assume years have 4 digits this problem will become exponentially harder to solve (i.e. the Y2K problem).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Since timestamp already internally encodes an int64 for seconds, we should remove the RFC3339 compatibility requirement. For example ISO8601 can support more than 4-digit years by prior agreement between sender and receiver. 

Note that 64-bit time should suffice until the year 292,277,026,596. By then we are likely to be long into the degenerate era (no star formation) so it probably won't matter when we roll over to negative time then.

nodes.body:
Thanks for raising this. I agree that this will eventually be a problem when Y10K rolls around, but its likely too early for us to prioritize addressing this anytime soon.

I'm don't know that we're ready to drop RFC3339 standard yet, and should likely revisit this closer to when this rolls around.

title: well_known_types is deprecated and suggests using :compiler_plugin_proto, which does not exist
body:
Version: HEAD
Language: bazel build rules

See https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/11430 for a prior incarnation of the same problem.

`well_known_protos` now flags as deprecated and exposes

```
    srcs = [
        ":descriptor_proto_srcs",
        ":well_known_type_protos",
        "//src/google/protobuf/compiler:plugin.proto",
    ],
```

The comment says

```
# DEPRECATED: Prefer :well_known_type_protos for the Well-Known Types
# (https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/google.protobuf)
# or :descriptor_proto(_srcs) for descriptor.proto (source), or
# :compiler_plugin_proto for compiler/plugin.proto.
```

But the target `:compiler_plugin_proto` doesn't exist, and there's no visibility to the inner target.

(Also, it would be nice if the `deprecated=` tag said all the same options the comment says, because otherwise when we update this our developers are going to get this warning telling them to switch to only `:well_known_type_protos` which may or may not actually work for any given use-case.)

nodes.body: //:compiler_plugin_proto does exist as an alias at the top level, is that not sufficient (granted, we could clean up our comments here)

Weird, I must have made a *whole series* of mistakes to think that wasn't there (both in code search and in a build rule trying to depend on it, somehow). Sorry about that!
(But yes, would still be good to make the dependency here on the alias instead of directly, and to make the deprecated= string mention all three things. Not as critical of an issue as I somehow thought though!)

Ah! It wasn't just me making a mistake, it was literally the same problem as last time, and you've said the equivalent thing to what you said last time!

```
alias(
    name = "descriptor_proto",
    actual = "//src/google/protobuf:descriptor_proto",  # proto_library
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)

alias(
    name = "descriptor_proto_srcs",
    actual = "//src/google/protobuf:descriptor_proto_srcs",  # filegroup
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)

alias(
    name = "compiler_plugin_proto",
    actual = "//src/google/protobuf/compiler:plugin_proto",  # proto_library
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)
```

```
filegroup(
    name = "well_known_protos",
    srcs = [
        ":descriptor_proto_srcs",
        ":well_known_type_protos",
        "//src/google/protobuf/compiler:plugin.proto",
    ],
    deprecation = "Prefer :well_known_type_protos instead.",
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)
```
The alias is for `plugin_proto` not for `plugin.proto`, i.e. it's like `descriptor_proto` not like `descriptor_proto_srcs`.
(And there is no alias for `plugin_proto_srcs`)

Just to make life extra awkward, over in the compiler build file there *is* a `plugin_proto_srcs` but it's got cpp and h files in it too, and a `plugin_proto_src` that has the file we actually need but lacks visibility.

My patch that makes this usable is:
```
--- a/BUILD.bazel
+++ b/BUILD.bazel
@@ -129,6 +129,12 @@ alias(
     visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
 )

+alias(
+    name = "compiler_plugin_proto_srcs",
+    actual = "//src/google/protobuf/compiler:plugin_proto_src",  # filegroup
+    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
+)
+
 cc_library(
     name = "cc_wkt_protos",
     deprecation = "Only for backward compatibility. Do not use.",
@@ -148,7 +154,7 @@ filegroup(
         ":well_known_type_protos",
         "//src/google/protobuf/compiler:plugin.proto",
     ],
-    deprecation = "Prefer :well_known_type_protos instead.",
+    deprecation = "Prefer :well_known_type_protos, :descriptor_proto_srcs and/or :compiler_plugin_proto_srcs instead.",
     visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
 )


--- a/src/google/protobuf/compiler/BUILD.bazel
+++ b/src/google/protobuf/compiler/BUILD.bazel
@@ -188,7 +188,10 @@ filegroup(
 filegroup(
     name = "plugin_proto_src",
     srcs = ["plugin.proto"],
-    visibility = ["@upb//:__subpackages__"],
+    visibility = [
+        "@upb//:__subpackages__",
+        "//:__subpackages__",
+    ],
 )

 exports_files(
```

lol deja vu 🤦‍♂️.  Why do you need the source file at all?  I think we ideally *would* want that to be private..

Anyway, if you send me a PR with those changes we can sort it out there

I think we're processing the source file in order to have access to the descriptors in python. Maybe there's a more modern way to do that with a python genfile from the proto library target or something, but when I'm struggling to update the version of protobuf used by a monorepo, the less gigantic refactorings of everything that depends on it the better!

(This time I've already removed all reliance on javascript protobufs from our entire monorepo because the google-protobuf-javascript github repo had been broken for over a year - then a few days after I'd done that it finally got an unbreaking update, of course.)

title: `-Werror` by default can break downstream Bazel builds
body:
**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**

Version: main and v24.x
Language: C++

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**

Linux, but probably all of them.

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**

In this case GCC 13.2:

```
gcc (Debian 13.2.0-4) 13.2.0
Copyright (C) 2023 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions.  There is NO
warranty; not even for MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
```


**What did you do?**

1. I was compiling Protobuf with GCC 13 and Address Sanitizer, as part of a different project (googleapis/google-cloud-cpp)
2. This project uses slightly different options in its `asan` configuration, and the build breaks.
3. To reproduce, you can apply this patch to the Protobuf source:
```diff
diff --git a/.bazelrc b/.bazelrc
index fb29fe10d..39e7120e0 100644

Linux: `go version go1.20.11 linux/amd64`

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Have a JSON string containing the following Unicode escape sequence `\udca0`, e.g. `{"name":"'unsafe-eval'; object?src\udca0'none'"}`.
2. Unmarshal byte slice of JSON string in question to protobuf message using `google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson` package.
3. See error `proto: syntax error (line 1:9): invalid escape code "'none'" in string`.

**What did you expect to see**
Unmarshalled value `name:"'unsafe-eval'; object?src�'none'"`. I.e. same unmarshalled string value as in Golang core JSON lib.

**What did you see instead?**
Unpopulated message and an error message `proto: syntax error (line 1:9): invalid escape code "'none'" in string`.

Code snippet for reproducing issue:
```golang
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"
	
	"pkg.my.package/microservices/models"
)

func main() {
	j1 := []byte(`{"name":"'unsafe-eval'; object?src\uc2a0'none'"}`)	# unmarshal is OK
	j2 := []byte(`{"name":"'unsafe-eval'; object?src\udca0'none'"}`)	# unmarshal error in protojson

	// protojson lib

	// models.Client is a golang struct compiled using `protoc` binary, from Client protobuf message.
	// Protobuf message for the sake of reproducing has 1 string field:
	//   Name       string       `protobuf:"bytes,1,opt,name=name,proto3" json:"name"`
	outProto1 := &models.Client{}
	outProto2 := &models.Client{}

	unmarshaler := protojson.UnmarshalOptions{DiscardUnknown: true}

	err1 := unmarshaler.Unmarshal(j1, outProto1)
	err2 := unmarshaler.Unmarshal(j2, outProto2)

	fmt.Println("protojson lib")
	fmt.Println(string(j1), err1, outProto1)
	fmt.Println(string(j2), err2, outProto2)

	// core lib
	outCore1 := make(map[string]interface{})
	outCore2 := make(map[string]interface{})

	err1 = json.Unmarshal(j1, &outCore1)
	err2 = json.Unmarshal(j2, &outCore2)

	fmt.Println("core lib")
	fmt.Println(string(j1), err1, outCore1)
	fmt.Println(string(j2), err2, outCore2)
}
```

Produces the following output:
```
protojson lib
{"name":"'unsafe-eval'; object?src\uc2a0'none'"} <nil> name:"'unsafe-eval'; object?src슠'none'"
{"name":"'unsafe-eval'; object?src\udca0'none'"} proto: syntax error (line 1:9): invalid escape code "'none'" in string 
core lib
{"name":"'unsafe-eval'; object?src\uc2a0'none'"} <nil> map[name:'unsafe-eval'; object?src슠'none']
{"name":"'unsafe-eval'; object?src\udca0'none'"} <nil> map[name:'unsafe-eval'; object?src�'none']
```

title: PLEASE make Protobuf backwards compatible.
body: Whenever you release a new version of Protobuf, it should be compatible with code written for the last Protobuf.  As it is currently, Protobuf 4 introduces changes that break scripts written for Protobuf 3.  That is such a huge pain to find and fix, and have to rewrite my scripts every time a new version comes out.  Please be considerate of the people who use your software, and make sure that each new version is compatible with scripts written using the previous version.

nodes.body:
Thanks for the feedback. Note that our versioning scheme is explained in https://engdoc.corp.google.com/eng/doc/devguide/proto/news/2022-05-06.md#versioning. We only increment major versions (e.g. 3.x.x to 4.x.x) for a language when we have breaking changes, following [SemVer](https://semver.org/) convention.

These breaks are important to allow Protobuf to evolve (e.g. deprecate old APIs after deprecation warnings). We pre-announce breaking changes in our [News](https://protobuf.dev/news/) page so you should be able to plan for these accordingly.

Minor releases with the same major version (e.g. v24.x -> v25.x) should remain backwards compatible. Please file issues if you see compatibility issues like this in a minor release.

You can also see https://protobuf.dev/support/cross-version-runtime-guarantee/ for our cross version runtime guarantees.

MSVC 2022 Community with cl.exe version "19.37.32825"

**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install git, bazel, MSVC
2. Clone the protobuf repository locally
3. Open the x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS 2022
4. Attempt to build with Bazel: bazel build //src/google/protobuf/compiler:protoc_lib
5. Note the frequent repeated compiler warning "cl : Command line warning D9002 : ignoring unknown option '-std=c++17'"
6. Edit the repository's .bazelrc and update the --cxxopt and --host_cxxopt options on line 1 so they are both '/std:c17'
7. Attempt to build with Bazel: bazel build //src/google/protobuf/compiler:protoc_lib
8. Notice the warning condition is remedied


**What did you expect to see**
I expected the C++17 support to be activated for the MSVC compiler without warnings.

**What did you see instead?**
Warnings about an incorrect flag and a failure to activate the compiler's c++17 support.

The compiler parameter specified in protobuf's .bazelrc file, added via commit d99134f6f8e3, is incompatible with the MSVC compiler, which uses the flag '/std:c17'. The options should be specified in a platform independent manner so both MSVC and linux based compilers read it properly.

title: add native Optional API for languages which support it
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for feature requests (including cleanup requests) only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->


**What language does this apply to?**
(focused on proto3, but might also apply to proto2 - i have no experience with proto2, though)

this applies to all programming languages which have a built-in notion of optional values, e.g. Java ([`java.lang.Optional`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Optional.html)) or Rust ([`std::option::Option`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html)). the examples below are given in java.

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
currently it is hard to deal with optional values in an idiomatic way in languages which would support this.

stripped-down example (extracted from a real-world example):
`example.proto`:
```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package example;

message Foo {
  sint64 example = 1;
}

message Example {
  optional sint64 example = 1;
  Foo foo = 2;
}
```

currently the java code to then access this data looks something like this:
```java
  public void foo(final Example example) {
    // directly:
    final long someDefaultValue = 42;
    final long bar = example.hasExample() ? example.getExample() : someDefaultValue;
    final long foo = example.hasFoo() ? example.getFoo().getExample() : someDefaultValue;

    // as optional:
    final Optional<Long> optionalBar = example.hasExample() ? Optional.of(example.getExample()) : Optional.empty();
    final Optional<Long> optionalFoo = example.hasFoo() ? Optional.of(example.getFoo().getExample()) : Optional.empty();
  }
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
it should be possible to tell protoc that the generated classes (or equivalents thereof in other languages) should generate APIs with `Optional` (or its equivalent) instead of `has[..]` & `get[...]` so that it can be used directly:
```java
  public void foo(final Example example) {
    // directly:
    final long someDefaultValue = 42;
    final long bar = example.getExample().orElse(someDefaultValue);
    final long foo = example.getFoo().map(Foo::getExample).orElse(someDefaultValue);

    // as optional:
    final Optional<Long> optionalBar = example.getExample();
    final Optional<Long> foo = example.getFoo().map(Foo::getExample);

    // you can still check for presence:
    final bool hasBar = example.getExample().isPresent();
    final bool hasFoo = example.getFoo().isPresent();
  }
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
manually writing this code all the time is very cumbersome and makes it harder to generalise the handling of optional values which are present in multiple messages (you can't just pass the `Optional` directly from the message to the handler, you have to manually convert it to an `Optional` first or have an ugly API which accepts both a presence indicator and a value).

making this the default behaviour would be a breaking change, accordingly i propose to introduce this as an optional feature which can be enabled when triggering the code generation (_maybe_ this could be turned into the default at some point in the future with a major release, though the ripple effects would probably be too big as all consuming code dealing with optional values would have to deal with this).

**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

nodes.body:
Thanks for the suggestion. While this could be nice in some languages like Java, the use of optionals in this manner isn't necessarily as idiomatic in other languages and we should preserve consistency in our APIs across different languages.

Furthermore, I don't think we want to put ourselves in a situation to maintain both existing `has/get` APIs and a new `Optional` one longterm. Per [our contribution doc](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#what-we-accept), breaking API changes  need to be rolled out to internally first. I could see [Editions features](https://protobuf.dev/editions/overview/) being used to roll changes like this out, but this particular API change would have a very large blast radius at likely minimal value. 

Note that if an optional field is not present, doing `get` on a field is still safe and simply returns the default value, so the current "// directly:" example can likely be simplified.

thanks for your feedback!

> While this could be nice in some languages like Java, the use of optionals in this manner isn't necessarily as idiomatic in other languages and we should preserve consistency in our APIs across different languages.

what is the rationale behind this guideline? i tend to value idiomatic usage within a language higher than consistency across languages - you seldom switch languages within a project but often interact with the data structures. there's a reason why there are e.g. idiomatic rust wrappers around native C/C++ APIs (so that you get a `Result<..>` back instead of having to deal with pointers and return values as by-reference parameters).

> Furthermore, I don't think we want to put ourselves in a situation to maintain both existing `has/get` APIs and a new `Optional` one longterm.

on one hand i can understand this, on the other hand i think that the benefits gained from a usability point of view would be very high (possibly leading to wide spread adaptation even if it has to be explicitly enabled) - so if most consumers switch over then you could safely remove the old has/get APIs.
but rolling it out as a big-bang breaking change would just cause a lot of forced effort for consumers which they might not be ready to do at the time where they have to do the upgrade (but i come from an environment where you can't just do breaking changes like that but instead have to do things gradually - if you're allowed to do something like this in a more breaking manner then go for it 😉)

> I could see [Editions features](https://protobuf.dev/editions/overview/) being used to roll changes like this out

i only briefly looked at the linked page, but my gut feeling is that this might not be the correct place to do this: the requested feature here is purely about the generated code, so whoever triggers the generator should be able to decide whether to use this (either by setting a generator flag if it's an optional feature or by just using an older generator). if you put it into the proto source then you need to adapt all consumers of this proto file at the same time (presuming they're sharing the proto file as an API definition and don't have individually modified versions).

> Note that if an optional field is not present, doing `get` on a field is still safe and simply returns the default value, so the current "// directly:" example can likely be simplified.

not if you want a default value which differs from what protobuf picks as a default value (often there's a business meaning behind the field, where e.g. 0 (in case of numbers) isn't the correct value).

this is IMHO still a desirable feature

Hi rursprung,

As Sandy says, we tend to be very careful about adding new features or new idioms that can only be represented in a single language. What she did not spell out explicitly is that Optional APIs are problematic for Java lite on Android where creating an Optional wrapper around the field value incurs an allocation of an Optional object. While this may not be a big performance penalty on the server side, it can add up to be enough to cause a problem on the mobile side.

You might then ask, "why can't Android code call the non-Optional APIs but have the Optional ones for those that can use them?". And the answer is that on Android, generating unused methods is not good -- code size is a real problem there. Whole program optimization like ProGuard can remove unused methods, but if a few callsites are introduced, you can't remove those methods.

The next logical question is then, "how about an option to generate these methods?" and the answer there is that every option expands the support surface and increases the combinatorial complexity of testing the ecosystem.

What about "just in Java not in JavaLIte". We try to avoid divergence of the Java and JavaLite API. In addtion to the combinatorial complexity / maintenance argument, there is also the migration path: the less divergence, the more likely an Android App can migrate from Full to LIte.

If a sufficient argument for the impact of `Optional` comes along that overrides the problems of mobile performance, code size, and maintenance complexity we will absolutely reconsider. But for now, the `has` + `get` API provides a workable solution.

title: [C#] Ensure enum members are preserved with trimming
body:
Note: I haven't seen anything broken by this issue. These are my thoughts in the area in case it does become a problem in the future.

---

AOT and trimming will remove unused members. That can include enum fields. I have tested places that use enum fields with reflection (e.g. JSON parser with enum values) and it appears to work, but I don't think that is a guarantee it will work forever.

The typical fix to this problem is to use `DynamicallyAccessedMembersAttribute` (DAM) to explicitly preserve values. However, that isn't possible when enum descriptors are registered because [GeneratedClrTypeInfo](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/b0d7441f83a4cc79d3937f65f8cc2b46931ea639/csharp/src/Google.Protobuf/Reflection/GeneratedClrTypeInfo.cs) accepts enum types in an array, and an array can't be annotated.

I see two ways to fix this:

One way is generate a dummy method that has a `Type` parameter and returns `Type`. The method parameter would have the DAM attribute on it:

```cs
private Type EnsureEnumMembers([DynamicallyAccessedMembers(PublicFields)] Type t) => t;
```

And then call it when values are passed to `GeneratedClrTypeInfo`. e.g.

```cs
new pbr::GeneratedClrTypeInfo(
    new[] { EnsureEnumMembers(typeof(global::Conformance.WireFormat)), EnsureEnumMembers(typeof(global::Conformance.TestCategory)) },
    ...);
```

That would signal to the linker that public fields for these enum types should never be trimmed.

Or have an `AddEnumType` method on `GeneratedClrTypeInfo` used to add enum types. That method can be annotated with the DAM attribute. The downside here is `GeneratedClrTypeInfo` is designed to be immutable (mostly, the arrays can be set, but they're not intended to be.

		return NewNumberValue(float64(v)), nil`   This convert is wrong,will case uint64  precision loss

**What did you expect to see**
This conversion is wrong,uint64 is used more frequently than the double type, which makes me return the wrong data, You may say, why not use string type instead, I use pb.struct is because of its dynamic, if I know what field is what type, I will not use pb.struct this, hope to support uint64 conversion of pb.value will not cause precision loss

nodes.body:
Hi, I'm interested in contributing to OSS and came across this issue. I could reproduce the situation by running the following code.

```go
func main() {
	originalObject := make(map[string]interface{})
	originalObject["id"] = uint64(math.MaxUint64)
	fmt.Println("original object:", originalObject)
	fmt.Println("the type of id is:", reflect.TypeOf(originalObject["id"]))

	pbStruct, err := structpb.NewStruct(originalObject)
	m := pbStruct.AsMap()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println(err)
	}
	fmt.Println("pb struct:", m)
	fmt.Println("the type of id is:", reflect.TypeOf(m["id"]))
}
```

and output is: 

```
original object: map[id:18446744073709551615]
the type of id is: uint64
pb struct: map[id:1.8446744073709552e+19]
the type of id is: float64
```

Obviously, the type of `id` set in the `structpb` object was changed to float64, so it couldn't express the entire range of uint64. However, the [document of strcutpb](https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb#pkg-overview) says that:

> The messages (i.e., Value, Struct, and ListValue) defined in struct.proto are used to represent arbitrary JSON. The Value message represents a JSON value, the Struct message represents a JSON object,

so, I think the purpose of the struct `strcutpb` is to express a JSON object, and the behavior above was intentional. I hope this helps you. Thanks,

nodes.body: If you enable `protobuf_BUILD_SHARED_LIBS` does it work?  It looks like somehow you're in a mixed state where it's linking in both the absl dll and the statically linked libraries...

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/assets/13501663/d7af6c11-d801-471d-bc14-c8bb233268cd

It got closer, but still had one linker error, video of the build shown here after doing a clean git clone and submodule update.

Note: gRPC gives clear warnings about statically linking it vs using a DLL, so I may prefer to use a static library if possible. I believe these issues should be reproducible and fix-able? (fingers crossed)
Correction: I guess it wasn't a linker error, some other compiler error.

hmm that's odd, I have seen that error before and we do set /bigobj in some of our tests config (see [here](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/842f56b57a9e825d6cdd6c00947f6c19c18fe466/cmake/tests.cmake#L107)).  It looks like it's failing to build descriptor_unittest.cc, so disabling `protobuf_BUILD_TESTS` might get around this.

FWIW neither of these "fixes" should be necessary.  We build with both static and dynamic linkage on windows, and we always build tests.  Our CI basically does your reproduction steps, so I'm not sure what the issue could be here.  In our closest build we use:
```
-Dprotobuf_WITH_ZLIB=OFF -Dprotobuf_BUILD_CONFORMANCE=OFF
-Dprotobuf_BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -Dprotobuf_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
```

What version of MSVC are you using?
![image](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/assets/13501663/ff4903a0-fb62-4a07-8c9f-977da029b44f)

I'm able to reproduce the `/bigobj` error on main, so I can fix that one.  As a workaround just don't build our tests?  I'm still not sure what the original issue is though, it really seems like you're *both* statically and dynamically linking Abseil.

Can you provide the full CLI reproduction steps?  Following the ones you gave worked fine except for the `/bigobj` error building our test suite

```

php -v
```

```

@northmule what is the problem you're seeing? 

For clarification, this issue is a feature request for the extension to produce better debugging info. It has not yet been implemented.

The problem is that when connecting the .so library in the php.ini file, the ability to view the class object inherited from the parent class \Google\Protobuf\Internal\Message disappears.
I have prepared two visual screenshots from the Phpstorm IDE and the configured xDebug debugger.
In one screenshot in php.ini, the library connection is disabled - ;extension=protobuf.so
In another screenshot, the library connection is enabled - extension=protobuf.so

The library is connected here
```
extension=protobuf.so
```
![Screenshot_20231212_084650](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/assets/33060300/cba1db80-16cb-4bb6-a8d9-56546b54f8db)


The library is not connected here
```
;extension=protobuf.so
```
![Screenshot_20231212_084512](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/assets/33060300/53a7a7c0-0fe4-4e78-8be3-3afcfe430316)

I highlighted the object in red.

If the library is not connected, I can view the object, it is filled with data

If the library is connected, I cannot view the object.

For simplicity, I took the \Google\Protobuf\Timestamp class, but this is reproduced on any other object from any class with inheritance from  \Google\Protobuf\Internal\Message

I assume this is because in the first example, the object is implemented in the C extension, and so is not visible by the IDE. This feature request is to implement a hook in the message class implemented in C++ which, similar to `__debugInfo` in PHP, when `var_dump` is called, it prints the properties inside the C object.

I think this is a reasonable feature request, and we'd be happy to accept a contribution.

This would involve implementing [`get_debug_info`](https://wiki.php.net/internals/engine/objects#get_debug_info) for `Message`, `RepeatedField`, and `MapField`.

There was previously a PR to return an empty hash table for `get_debug_info`, which is a good example of how this might look, except that we'd want the returned hash table to be fully populated: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/7562/files

I just noticed that we have a test for debug info that is disabled for the C extension: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/6f1d88107f268b8ebdad6690d116e74c403e366e/php/tests/DebugInfoTest.php#L37-L42

So we essentially already have a spec for how the C extension should work in this regard.

@haberman This isn't a justification for the existing behavior, it's just confirming that it isn't currently supported.

I added that test (and the feature). It was required to skip since this hasn't been implemented in the C extension yet.

See https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/12718

**EDIT**: I think I misunderstood your comment to mean this was WAD, but after rereading it, I think you're just saying that the C-extension's implementation can follow the "spec" of the native implementation (and pass the tests), and I totally agree. Sorry for the confusion.

> I think you're just saying that the C-extension's implementation can follow the "spec" of the native implementation (and pass the tests), and I totally agree.

Exactly. I meant it as a hint/pointer for whoever ends up implementing this for C. The easiest way to start is to re-enable the test, and code a solution until the test passes.

title: [Ruby] Provide Ruby wrapper classes for ServiceDescriptor and MethodDescriptor
body:
**What language does this apply to?**

Ruby

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**

The Ruby runtime library provides several Ruby classes `Google::Protobuf::Descriptor`, `Google::Protobuf::FileDescriptor`, etc. that wrap the underlying descriptor objects, along with `Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool` that wraps the defpool and provides a way to look up needed descriptors. These objects are sometimes critical for understanding protobuf descriptors, especially when implementing protoc plugins.

However, two objects have no corresponding Ruby class: the service and method descriptors. Hence, it is not possible to access service descriptor information from Ruby.

For example, this makes it extremely difficult to get option extensions for services and methods, as the computation of that information happens on the descriptors. This makes it difficult to write client library generators in Ruby. #1198 was recently closed as complete to address this, but it covered only the descriptor types already existing; there is still no way to get custom option info for services and methods.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

We propose creating the classes `Google::Protobuf::ServiceDescriptor` and `Google::Protobuf::MethodDescriptor`, implemented similarly to the existing descriptor wrapper classes (i.e. a C implementation in `ruby/ext/google/protobuf_c/defs.[ch]`, FFI implementations in `ruby/lib/google/protobuf/ffi/`, and JRuby implementations in `src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/jruby/`.) Appropriate accessor methods on those classes would need to be determined and designed.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

We currently do not seem to have a good alternative for getting runtime descriptor information in Ruby. I currently maintain a client library generator, and we had to resort to [directly decoding](https://github.com/googleapis/gapic-generator-ruby/blob/main/gapic-generator/lib/gapic/schema/proto_tools.rb) the encoded form of `ServiceOptions` and `MethodOptions` data, and hard-coding field numbers, in order to get the information we need.

**Additional context**

Other languages do seem to have these classes. [Example from Python](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/v25.1/python/google/protobuf/descriptor.py#L859)

nodes.body:
I think this makes sense to do. We would welcome a contribution. An easy start would be:

- Extend `DescriptorPool#lookup` to allow looking up services/methods by fully-qualified name
- Implement `ServiceDescriptor` with `#name`, `#methods`, and `#options`
- Implement `MethodDescriptor` with `#name` and `#options`
I'm unassigning myself as I have no immediate plans to work on this, but we would welcome a contribution.

I had a need for this (for generating RPC stubs from the proto descriptors, without having to write a protoc plugin), so I implemented I think what you had in mind in https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/15817
Hey folks. I see that #15817 was closed/merged, but has it been released into a stable version yet? Is it slated for v27.x?
This change indeed made the cut for 27.x, and is announced in the release notes for 27.0-rc1: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v27.0-rc1

nodes.body: Why do you want the generated code to use `memset_s` and `memcpy_s`?  These are bounds-checked functions which will incur runtime overhead. The C++ proto library relies on its own internal logic to ensure that bounds are safe. Changing these functions would add little safety overall, while introducing extra CPU overhead.

Win11

Java21

**What did you do?**
proto file：
```
message WxMsg
{
    uint64 id      = 3;  // message id
    uint32 type    = 4;  // message type
    uint32 ts      = 5;  // 
    string content = 7;  // text message
    string sender  = 8;  // message sender
    string sign    = 9;  // 
    string xml     = 12; // 
}
```
java code：
```java
size = rpcMsgSocket.receive(bb, true);
long Wcf.WxMsg wxmsg = Wcf.Response.parseFrom(bb.slice(0, (int) size)).getWxmsg();
log.info("收到消息=\n{}", wxmsg);
```

**What did you expect to see**
```
收到消息=
id: 6308366405297852584
type: 1
ts: 1701855847
content: "我很帅"
sender: "id_1111111"
sign: "8ff4459eda0e9e60ec79015fbd58be07"
xml: "<msgsource>\n\t<pua>1</pua>\n\t<signature>v1_kJkAX+8v</signature>\n\t<tmp_node>\n\t\t<publisher-id></publisher-id>\n\t</tmp_node>\n</msgsource>\n"
```
**What did you see instead?**
```
收到消息=
id: 6308366405297852584
type: 1
ts: 1701855847
content: "\346\210\221\345\276\210\345\270\205"
sender: "id_1111111"
sign: "8ff4459eda0e9e60ec79015fbd58be07"
xml: "<msgsource>\n\t<pua>1</pua>\n\t<signature>v1_kJkAX+8v</signature>\n\t<tmp_node>\n\t\t<publisher-id></publisher-id>\n\t</tmp_node>\n</msgsource>\n"
```

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**
Look at the content attribute.
When calling the object's toString() method, if the content of the object's String type field is in Chinese, it will be directly output in octal, Inconvenient to read when debugging

nodes.body:
I believe this is handled in escapeText(): https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/adacf6d0e17bb90d37965a5901478ddce23656c6/java/core/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/TextFormatEscaper.java#L130.

The comment here indicates that only ASCII characters between 0x20 and 0x7e are printable which is probably why you are getting this outputted in octal. Looks like this is WAI.

body:
<!--

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf 
Stack Overflow is also a useful if unofficial resource https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/protocol-buffers
-->

**What version of protobuf and what language are you using?**
Version: v25.1 (actually a bit after, main from 20231123. Relevant code hasn't changed since then) 
Language: C++

**What operating system (Linux, Windows, ...) and version?**
Windows 11 Pro 22H2

**What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g., python version or gcc version)**
MS Visual Studio 17.8.0 (tool version 14.37.32822)

**What did you do?**
Compile something that makes use of include/google/protobuf/map.h

**What did you expect to see**
Warning-free compilation

**What did you see instead?**
Warnings from Abseil : include\absl\log\internal\check_op.h(340,1): warning C4018: '>=': signed/unsigned mismatch
This is from an Abseil macro that generates Check_GEImpl(), used in map.h

**Anything else we should know about your project / environment**

`map.h` line 1041 (in current main) invokes

`ABSL_DCHECK_GE(new_num_buckets, kMinTableSize);`

the first arg is `map_index_t` which resolves to `uint32_t`, whereas the second is defined
at line 528 as

`enum { kMinTableSize = 16 / sizeof(void*) };`

I'm guess MSVC is choosing a signed type for the enum which is causing the problem. Changing it to

`enum : unsigned int { kMinTableSize = 16 / sizeof(void*) };`

makes the warnings go away

title: New Tag: is_sensitive_message
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for feature requests (including cleanup requests) only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->


**What language does this apply to?**
If it's a proto syntax change, is it for proto2 or proto3?
-> proto3

If it's about generated code change, what programming language?
-> I think it's useful for every programming language, but in my case it's Golang.

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
I have a project which has grpc interceptor that log every request and response. Meanwhile in current changes, i added a new sensitive field which i do not want to print that field into the log. I do some research and found that proto3 has a tag called `json_name`. But unfortunately it only generates the proto3 json tag that can only be used by jsonpb / protojson. Also it's still not working as json: `-,omitempty` , it's still printing the field as `"-"`.
Example:
```
proto file:
message Response {
    string phone_number= 1 [json_name="-"];
}

pb.go file:
type Response struct {
     PhoneNumber string `protobuf:"bytes,1,opt,name=phone_number,json=-,proto3" json:"phone_number,omitempty"`
}

json:
{
    "-": "3463625"
}
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I suggest we add new tag, which is `is_sensitive_message`, and by reading that tag in message encoder like protojson we can skip the message to hide sensitive data.
```
proto file:
message Response {
    string phone_number= 1 [is_sensitive_message=true];
}

pb.go file:
type Response struct {
     PhoneNumber string `protobuf:"bytes,1,opt,name=phone_number,json=phone_number,is_sensitive_message=true,proto3" json:"phone_number,omitempty"`
}

json:
{}
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
-

**Additional context**
Currently i'm in progress updating `protocolbuffers/protobuf` to add the tag, as well as the protojson in `golang/protobuf` in my local. If this feature is approved, then i will submit PR ASAP.

	currently from:  "github.com/dk-slack/protos/member_service/golang/admin"
See https://protobuf.dev/reference/go/faq#namespace-conflict
```

nodes.body:
I've successfully updated all package names for both the Golang files and the general package names to ensure uniqueness. Despite these changes, I've noticed that warnings persist, specifically related to the names of the proto files.

I find this situation a bit puzzling. The reason is that, despite the presence of warnings, the files have been successfully compiled, and the resulting code is fully functional. The warnings appear to be more like artifacts—remnants from an earlier stage of development—rather than genuine indications of a current problem or issue.
I believe you're looking for https://github.com/golang/protobuf which is for the protobuf go implementation, but please reopen if I'm mistaken here.

The behavior here is not specific to the Go implementation.

The protobuf descriptors which describe the structure of a set of protobuf declarations (messages, enums, etc.) include the names of the files in which each declaration appears. These filenames are determined by the protobuf compiler (`protoc`) and provided to the language-specific code generator.

The Go protobuf runtime enforces a requirement that there be no namespace conflicts among the descriptors in a program. (See https://protobuf.dev/reference/go/faq/#namespace-conflict for some more details.) This includes conflicts among filenames: There may not be multiple files with the same name.

This requirement is enforced to avoid ambiguity when, for example, attempting to look up the descriptors contained in the file with a given name (using [`protoreflect.Files.FindFileByPath`](https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/protobuf/reflect/protoregistry#Files.FindFileByPath), for example).

Not every protobuf runtime enforces this requirement. Some ignore conflicts, some print a warning at startup. The Go runtime's current behavior was mandated by the protobuf-team and the Go maintainers don't have discretion to change it, so we have historically deferred questions about it to this issue tracker.

In the specific case described here, it is not possible to say with certainty how to resolve the problem since the report doesn't include details on how `protoc` is being invoked, but I can infer a probably cause and solution from the report:

You have, for example, files named:

```
events_service/admin.proto
mailbox_service/admin.proto
```

You are probably invoking `protoc` with a command like:

```
protoc --go_out=... -Ievents_service events_service/admin.proto
protoc --go_out=... -Imailbox_service mailbox_service/admin.proto
```

or

```
(cd events_service && protoc --go_out=... admin.proto)
(cd mailbox_service && protoc --go_out=... admin.proto)
```

In both cases, `protoc` associate the filename `admin.proto` with each of the generated files.

What you want is for the files to have unique names: `events_service/admin.proto` and `mailbox_service/admin.proto`. You can achieve this with something like (note the lack of `-I`):

```
protoc --go_out=... events_service/admin.proto
protoc --go_out=... mailbox_service/admin.proto
```

This may require adjusting the `--go_out` option or other aspects of your configuration.

In each service I have a script to generate the go code for all the files in that service

```sh
├── eventservice
│   ├── generate.sh
│   ├── go.mod
│   ├── go.sum
│   └── protos
│       ├── admin.proto
│       ├── eventtype.proto
│       ├── location.proto
│       ├── locationtype.proto
│       ├── models.proto
│       ├── public.proto
│       └── services.proto
├── mailboxservice
│   ├── generate.sh
│   ├── go.mod
│   ├── go.sum
│   └── protos
│       ├── admin.proto
│       ├── models.proto
│       ├── services.proto
│       └── user.proto
└── memberservice
    ├── generate.sh
    ├── go.mod
    ├── go.sum
    └── protos
        ├── activist.proto
        ├── admin.proto
        ├── models.proto
        ├── public.proto
        ├── registration.proto
        ├── services.proto
        ├── slacktype.proto
        └── statistics.proto
```

My development flow for the services are autonomous and they could as well have been developed by 3rd party developers in each separate codebase.

The service eventservice and mailboxservice each have their own generation script, so I am basically doing what you said and calling protoc on a file ./protos/services,proto in each project. which is then giving me the namespace issue. 

for instance in mailboxservice

```sh 
protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:./mailboxadmin \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:./mailboxadmin \
  protos/admin.proto \

protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:./mailboxuser \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:./mailboxuser \
  protos/user.proto \

protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:./mailboxmodels \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:./mailboxmodels \
  protos/models.proto \

protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:. \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:. \
  protos/services.proto \
```

And then in event service

```sh
protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:./eventadmin \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:./eventadmin \
  protos/admin.proto \

protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:./eventpublic \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:./eventpublic \
  protos/public.proto \

protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:./eventmodels \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:./eventmodels \
  protos/models.proto \

protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:./locationadmin \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:./locationadmin \
  protos/location.proto \

protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:./locationtypeadmin \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:./locationtypeadmin \
  protos/locationtype.proto \

protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:./eventtypeadmin \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:./eventtypeadmin \
  protos/eventtype.proto \

protoc -I./protos \
  --go_out=paths=source_relative:. \
  --go-grpc_out=paths=source_relative:. \
  protos/services.proto \

```

## Conclusion

I guess I was assuming some kind of encapsulation when I was developing the services separately like this, but I see now that grpc is looking at everything like its on the same level, and I can solve it by naming my 'protos' folder in each service project, '{service_name}protos' instead and then I just have to make sure not to give 2 services the same name.

title: Python: Error on packing Any "'Any' object has no attribute 'type_url'"
body:
### Specs
Python protobuf module, version 4.25.1
Python 3.9.10 (tags/v3.9.10:f2f3f53, Jan 17 2022, 15:14:21) [MSC v.1929 64 bit (AMD64)] on win3
Windows 10 Pro


### Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run following code
```python
from google.protobuf.internal.well_known_types import Any
Any().Pack(message)
```
Expected behavior:
`Any` object is created and then, a message is packed into it.

`Any` reference: https://protobuf.dev/reference/python/python-generated/#any

### Actual behavior:

```
lib\site-packages\google\protobuf\internal\well_known_types.py", line 54, in Pack
    self.type_url = '%s%s' % (type_url_prefix, msg.DESCRIPTOR.full_name)
AttributeError: 'Any' object has no attribute 'type_url'
```
----
I tested it with was a simple String message declared as such:
```protobuf
message StringGrpc{
    string string = 1;
}
```
```python
Any().Pack(StringGrpc(string="test"))
```


### The bug
I believe it fails due to error in `well_known_types.py`.
Let me paste the implementation:
```python
class Any(object):
  """Class for Any Message type."""

  __slots__ = ()

  def Pack(self, msg, type_url_prefix='type.googleapis.com/',
           deterministic=None):
    """Packs the specified message into current Any message."""
    if len(type_url_prefix) < 1 or type_url_prefix[-1] != '/':
      self.type_url = '%s/%s' % (type_url_prefix, msg.DESCRIPTOR.full_name)
    else:
      self.type_url = '%s%s' % (type_url_prefix, msg.DESCRIPTOR.full_name)
    self.value = msg.SerializeToString(deterministic=deterministic)
```
The issue is that this class uses slots. It tries to access `type_url` and `value` properties in `Pack()` method but those properties are not added to slots.

Slots reference: https://wiki.python.org/moin/UsingSlots

### Workaround
The simplest workaround you can do is subclassing Any and providing slots yourself.
```
from google.protobuf.internal.well_known_types import Any


class MyOwnAny(Any):

    __slots__ = ("type_url", "value")
```

title: [Ruby] Support for currently ignored Array methods in `RepeatedField`
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
This is about protobuffer's `RepeatedField` compatibility with Ruby 3 `Array` methods.

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
I discovered this when trying to apply [Class: RuboCop::Cop::Style::ArrayIntersect](https://www.rubydoc.info/github/rubocop/rubocop/master/RuboCop/Cop/Style/ArrayIntersect) to the Ruby application I'm working on. In particular, this lints against `(array1 & array2).empty?`, as it can be replaced by the more efficient and idiomatic `!array1.intersect?(array2)`.

However, when `array1` is a `RepeatedField` instead, this doesn't work, as `RepeatedField` does not have that method, even though it *mostly* behaves like an array.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like to see this code also delegate `intersect?`:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/a4576cb8208ea8f1c4b05b9bb35533201e301171/ruby/lib/google/protobuf/repeated_field.rb#L30-L55

It seems like this method is explicitly being ignored in a compatibility test (alongside other interesting ones): https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/a4576cb8208ea8f1c4b05b9bb35533201e301171/ruby/compatibility_tests/v3.0.0/tests/repeated_field_test.rb#L23-L26

I see that the exclusion was added in [[protobuf/pr/9645] Fixed Ruby 3.1 tests by marking intersect? as unimplemented](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/9645) by @haberman, but I couldn't find the reasoning behind excluding them, instead of adding the functionality. I'd be happy to create a PR to get this moving, but didn't know if there's any reason to avoid it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Ignoring the linting suggestion, and adding a comment in the code explaining why it doesn't work

nodes.body:
> It looks like the list of forwarded methods is a fixed list that was written 9 years ago, and hasn't been updated since.
> 
> The gem now requires Ruby 2.7 or above, so it would make sense to update the list of forwarded and wrapped methods to include the ones added to Array as of at least that version

I created [[protobuf/pr/15652] [Ruby] Delegate difference, intersection, union from RepeatedField to Array](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/pull/15652) to start delegating some of the methods, as I found it confusing that some of their versions were delegated, while others weren't (e.g. `|` vs `union`)

> It would also make sense to use feature detection code (`respond_to?` checks, for instance), to delegate more methods if they exist in Array.

I'm hesitant about this because of this comment: https://github.com/marianosimone/protobuf/blob/58b582ba310afda710585211cc75e7b140284593/ruby/lib/google/protobuf/repeated_field.rb#L45-L46

It looks like being explicit was a design decision.

It would be nice, though, to be able to have per-version delegation (e.g., if using Ruby 3, I'd like to be able to use `intersect?`). Is there any prior art on supporting something like this?

> @marianosimone in the short term, you can patch the class to add the missing methods. You'd have to check the source to determine which methods could be delegated and which would need custom wrappers.

Yeah, this is what we are going to do internally for now, but would love to see it fixed upstream :)
Closing as #15652 has merged. Please reopen if there is still more to do.

I don't have permissions to re-open, so I can't :)

Arguably, this is not completely solved, as there's no ongoing solution for *all* methods, and it just works with the ones I added to the allowlist for delegation.

nodes.body:
Unfortunately the listed patch is dangerous: the multiple registrations of potentially different contents implies surprising skew which could cause locally correct code to break.

In theory it could be safe to ignore multiple registrations which were exactly identical but I think such a case is a 'this is suspicious and likely to break if you don't stop doing this' enough situation that its probably better to noisily fail. In the dynamic linking case like the 2016 issue linked it'll end up with multiple registrations where the descriptor may happen to match until you actually get skew, then it could break even though you didn't change anything in your code.

Basically any given file should just only be registered once: if there's PyTorch code that is registering the same file twice then it more likely is something to fix on the caller's side.

Hope that makes sense!

title: Enhancement of Protobuf Reflection Capabilities for Improved Runtime Flexibility
body:
Dear Protobuf Contributors,

I hope this message finds you well. I am reaching out to discuss a potential enhancement to the Protocol Buffers framework that could significantly augment its runtime flexibility, particularly in dynamic environments.

**Context:**
As you are aware, Protocol Buffers offers a robust mechanism for serialising structured data across a variety of languages and platforms. However, one area where I believe it could be further improved is in its reflection capabilities. Currently, the reflection API provides a way to inspect and manipulate protobuf messages at runtime, but it is somewhat limited when it comes to dynamic message construction and schema evolution.

**Proposal:**
I propose the introduction of a more advanced reflection API that would allow for the dynamic creation of message types based on runtime information. This could be particularly beneficial for applications that need to adapt to changing data models without recompilation. For instance, a service that ingests data from multiple sources with varying schemas could leverage this feature to construct messages on-the-fly.

**Potential Benefits:**
- Increased adaptability to schema changes at runtime without the need for recompilation or redeployment.
- Enhanced ability to work with meta-programming techniques, allowing developers to write more generic and flexible code.
- Improved support for scenarios where the full schema is not known at compile time, such as in certain data integration or ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processes.

**Seeking Feedback:**
I am keen to hear your thoughts on this suggestion and whether it aligns with the vision you have for the future of Protocol Buffers. Additionally, I would appreciate any insights into the feasibility of such an enhancement from a technical standpoint.

Thank you for considering this proposal. I look forward to a fruitful discussion and am happy to contribute to the design and implementation should there be interest in moving forward with this idea.

Best regards,
yihong1120

nodes.body:
Hi @yihong1120,

thanks for reaching out. It sounds like the features you're describing are largely covered by the existing dynamic_message.h header in our C++ API. I recommend exploring that first.  While we're always open to improvements, it's unlikely that we'll make major expansions to the dynamic reflective API in the immediate future.

Best,
Jakob

title: csharp: Support for generated types name customization
body:
**What language does this apply to?**
C#

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**

The main problem is naming collision with types generated from proto contracts.
Most of our team's projects use hexagonal architecture with gRPC living in a presentation layer. Because we don't have dedicated domain model, we use anaemic data model with types shared between application, infrastructure and presentation (because models are just records). To avoid code duplication, we don't use separate dto's, meaning that the naming for application models and proto messages is virtually the same.

This leads to naming collision between our own types, and types that are generated from proto contracts. As gRPC projects in our applications are basically glorified mappers, this issue is pretty severe, because the only solution right now is to use using alias directives (prefix proto generated types with `Proto`) or qualifying type names with namespaces. This "hacky" solution results in messy, and sometimes hard to comprehend or even ambiguous code.

Other potential solutions are to prefix messages with `Proto` right in contract names, or postfix them with `Dto`. First is kinda verbose for contracts (if it is in .proto file, it is already clear that it is proto, right?) and it differs from conventions that are used by other teams (using other languages). Second solution is not really applicable to all projects (there are places where dto's exist), so the problem either would persist but in smaller range of services, or contracts for these services would be missing the postfix. Both solutions are not ideal and would lead to contract inconsistency.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

The ability to define patterns to names of types generated from proto messages project wide would solve the problem. It can be implemented via new attribute in .csproj's `Protobuf` tag. Parameterising just the prefix or postfix would do as well.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Alternative solution is to use options in proto contracts themselves (ex: `csharp_type_name_prefix`) similar to `csharp_namespace`. It is better from portability standpoint (you do not have to alter `Protobuf` tag in your csproj). But it is way worse in transferability, as you have to do it right away in contracts, which can be an issue when consuming contracts from services that do not follow this convention (ex: services written in other languages).

**Additional context**

As i do not know much about internals of C# protobuf library, i cannot judge the complexity of changes that this feature requires. But I am up for learning these internals and contributing to implementation.
Additionally, if there is a way to achieve desired result in an existing state of library, i would be glad to know about it.

nodes.body: Sorry but I don't think this is a change we would want to accept. We tend to be extremely reluctant to add new flags if we can avoid it, since they add complexity and become a permanent maintenance cost. It seems to me like if a lot of naming conflicts are happening then some sort of namespacing is the way to go. I'm not sure I fully understand your situation but I would try disambiguating using `csharp_namespace`, or if that doesn't work (i.e. because other teams own some of the proto files) then perhaps use a different namespace for your C# models.

Sad to hear that.

There is not exact (namespace + type name) conflicts, only type name conflicts. Types were in different namespaces from the beginning, but that namespacing is exactly what leads to messy code.

I would like to be able to write generic code that accepts a message type and parses it.

T Deserialize<T>(BinaryData data);

Add an interface that exposes [static virtual members](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/proposals/csharp-11.0/static-abstracts-in-interfaces) and emit it in codegen.

```cs
public interface IParsableMessage<T> where T : IMessage<T>
{

    public abstract static MessageDescriptor Descriptor { get; }
}

Which would allow writing code like this:

```cs
T Deserialize<T>(BinaryData data)  where T : IParsableMessage<T> => T.Parser.ParseFrom(data.ToMemory().Span);
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I could add this interface myself, but then I'd have to manually implement it for every generated contract.

title: C#: Add DateOnly and TimeOnly conversion methods for Timestamp
body:
<!--

NOTE: this form is for feature requests (including cleanup requests) only. For questions or troubleshooting, please see the protobuf mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/protobuf

-->


**What language does this apply to?**
C#

**Describe the problem you are trying to solve.**
.NET has added DateOnly and TimeOnly types. There should be a way to easily convert these to Protobuf's Timestamp

**Describe the solution you'd like**
There are conversion methods for DateTime and DateTimeOffset already:
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/27275da1c0033331e55277613f32457b2500e811/csharp/src/Google.Protobuf/WellKnownTypes/TimeExtensions.cs
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/27275da1c0033331e55277613f32457b2500e811/csharp/src/Google.Protobuf/WellKnownTypes/TimestampPartial.cs

Replicate these methods for the new types.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

nodes.body: TimeOnly doesn't make sense as a Timestamp, but it could be convertible to a Duration.

Personally I don't think either of these types is suitable as a conversion target.

`TimeOnly` is a time of day, not a duration of time. (`DateTime.TimeOfDay` uses a `TimeSpan`, but that's problematic too IMO. That's why `TimeOnly` was created...)

`Timestamp` is an instant in time - it's "machine time" rather than "civil time" whereas `DateOnly` is about civil time, and that usually involves a time zone - any conversion from `Timestamp` to `DateOnly` would have to *assume* UTC, and that feels like it's misleading to me.

The conversion to `DateTimeOffset` (or `DateTime`) allows you to get to a `DateOnly` reasonably easily (and both conversion methods give a value that really does represent the original `Timestamp`, as it includes the UTC offset or UTC kind), so I don't think that providing additional methods that could easily cause confusion would be a benefit.
Ok. I don't feel strongly about either.

Was this closed without adding any support for them? What's the recommended way to use `TimeOnly` with protobuf then if that's the case?

Since `TimeOnly` can be converted to and from `TimeSpan` and `TimeSpan` is convertible to `Duration` why can't `TimeOnly` also be directly convertible to `Duration` for consistency? I understand the argument that `TimeOnly` is a time of day and not a duration of time but can't it also be seen as the time elapsed since midnight like the documentation for `TimeOnly.FromTimeSpan` says?

nodes.body:
This is by design - it's providing the JSON representation, which is a string value, and therefore quoted as such. In general, calling `ToString` on any message provides the JSON representation. > Clearly should not be in the output

This is working as intended, and changing it would be a very breaking change.

(I do understand it's surprising at first sight - but it's still the intended behavior.)

title: Using the suffix "Value" conflicts with generated enum getters/setters

nodes.body: Sorry for the inconvenience, but unfortunately we're not able to prioritize fixing this right now. Probably the best workaround is to tweak the names in the proto file to keep them from conflicting in the generated code.

@acozzette Thanks for the response. I totally understand. For now, we're working around this in two ways: 1) when translating schemas to `proto`, we "sanitize" names of fields that cause this problem by mangling their names -- ugly, but effective. 2) We've added in-house linting validation that prohibits naming fields in a way that conflict with enum fields when such enum fields exist in the schema.

In terms of a fix at the protobuf level, any idea _how_ this would be addressed? For example, would we append the field number to the getter/setter, similar to how other conflicts are handled? If we have some idea of _how_ we could handle this, then it may be possible to have a fix contributed rather than left on your plate.

I think the fix would have to detect when this conflict between `x` and `x_value` happens, and then adjust the generated names to prevent them from conflicting. (If `x_value` appears by itself then we wouldn't want to mess with it because that might break existing code that works.) The question then is just what the adjustment should look like. I wasn't aware that we append the field number to address similar conflicts, but if so then that sounds like a reasonable precedent to follow.
The same kind of conflict can happen for oneof and its "Case" suffixed getters, and all other artificial class properties.

Looking at the [blame](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blame/v25.2/src/google/protobuf/compiler/command_line_interface_unittest.cc) of the respective file (and the logs noting something about the fixture constructor), my first suspicion was that this is related to 

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/a9b006bddd52e289029f16aa77b77e8e0033d9ee/src/google/protobuf/compiler/command_line_interface_unittest.cc#L198-L204

`_putenv` on windows [requires](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/putenv-wputenv#requirements) `<stdlib.h>` (though that's probably satisfied by some transitive include), but more importantly, it's explicitly not threadsafe. The docs note:
> The `_putenv` and `_getenv` families of functions are not thread-safe. `_getenv` could return a string pointer while `_putenv` is modifying the string, causing random failures. Make sure that calls to these functions are synchronized.

However, even with including that header and running the test suite in parallel, the failures persist. They also persist if we build the static variant of protobuf.

Couple of other things I noticed:
* [`_putenv`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/putenv-wputenv) is soft-deprecated in favour of [`_putenv_s`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/putenv-s-wputenv-s), a "more secure" variant
* Both variants have a [table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/putenv-s-wputenv-s#generic-text-routine-mappings) that describe which function flavour to use depending on some global symbols related to Unicode and multibyte strings, reproduced for `_putenv_s` below:

    | `TCHAR.H` routine | `_UNICODE` and `_MBCS` not defined | `_MBCS` defined | `_UNICODE` defined |
    |-|-|-|-|
    | `_tputenv_s` | `_putenv_s` |  `_putenv_s` | `_wputenv_s` | 
  
  This is actually a pretty good candidate for an ABI break IMO.
* Protobuf will set the `_UNICODE` symbol based on `protobuf_UNICODE`
  https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/a9b006bddd52e289029f16aa77b77e8e0033d9ee/cmake/protobuf-configure-target.cmake#L35-L37
* The windows tests in [`appveyor.bat`](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/v25.2/appveyor.bat#L15-L25) only test the `protobuf_UNICODE=ON` [case](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/v25.2/appveyor.yml#L16-L23).
* Another [gem](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/environ-wenviron) in the MSFT docs about `UNICODE` vs. shared builds:
  > Polling `_environ` in a Unicode context is meaningless when [/MD](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/reference/md-mt-ld-use-run-time-library) or `/MDd` linkage is used. For the CRT DLL, the type (wide or multibyte) of the program is unknown. Only the multibyte type is created because that is the most likely scenario.

  "Most likely" indeed... 🤦

There's also a couple of leaks around mocked objects which happen in _other_ tests; not sure if that's an unrelated issue or somehow connected:
```
D:\bld\libprotobuf-split_1705373215324\work\src\google\protobuf\io\coded_stream_unittest.cc(1494): ERROR: this mock object (used in test CodedStreamTest.InputOver2G) should be deleted but never is. Its address is @000000B6EBEFE170.

            _sym_db.pool.Add(file)
        

def string_enum_value(enum_name:str, alias:str):
    enum_descriptor = _sym_db.pool.FindEnumTypeByName(enum_name)
    
    for value in enum_descriptor.values:
        if not  value.has_options:
            continue
        options = value.GetOptions()
        enum_alias =  _sym_db.pool.FindExtensionByName('custom_options.enum_alias')
        if  alias in options.Extensions[enum_alias]  :
            return value.number
    return None





if __name__ == "__main__":
    load_pb('main.pb')
    string_enum_value('main.MultiGameType' , '1PK')

windows

idea
**What did you do?**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. use `JsonFormat.printer().print(data)` convert protobuf to json
2. one field is string type,  when value contains char '=', json is \u003d.
for example:  fied value is "ns=100;s=DEVICE_NAME", but to json is "ns\u003d100;s\u003dDEVICE_NAME"
4. one field is bytestype,  when convert to json, the value is not excepted.
for example:  fied value is "QPJ", but to json is "UVBK"
some code like:
```
message Field {
    string name = 1;
    oneof Value {
        double float_value = 2;
        int64 int_value = 3;
        bool bool_value = 4;
        bytes binary_value = 5;
        Ints int_values = 6;
        Floats float_values = 7;
    }
}
```
```
fieldBuilder.setName("ns=100;s=DEVICE_NAME").setBinaryValue(ByteString.copyFrom("QPJ".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)));
```
json output:
```
"fields":[{"name":"ns\u003d100;s\u003dDEVICE_NAME","binaryValue":"UVBK"}]
```

**What did you expect to see**
two question:
1. why character '=' to json is '\u003d' ?
2. I know binary value may not readable, but json is for read, how to convert binary value to readable string as above "QPJ" set to protobuf and out to json is always "QPJ"?

nodes.body:
> why character '=' to json is '\u003d' ?

I believe this is because all html characters are escaped in the JSON format. You can read more about it here: https://groups.google.com/g/google-gson/c/JDHUo9DWyyM

> I know binary value may not readable, but json is for read, how to convert binary value to readable string as above "QPJ" set to protobuf and out to json is always "QPJ"?

In JSON format binary values are encoded with base64. You'll either need to use a string type instead of bytes or base64 decode your bytes.
